body.text: Mahāsannipātaratnaketudhāraṇī sūtraṃ
body.translated_text: <s>Mahāsannipātaratnaketudhāraṇī Sūtra</s>

body.text: START Rkp 1
body.translated_text: START <s>Rkp</s> 1

body.text: prathamaḥ parivartaḥ
body.translated_text: First Chapter

body.text:
namastathāgatāya gandhaprabhaśriye / namo mahābrahmaghoṣāya /
eteṣāṃ namaskartāsaṃprāptaḥ māravyūhena /
body.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Gandhaprabhaśrī</s>. Homage to <s>Mahābrahmaghoṣa</s>. The one who pays homage to these has arrived, through <s>Māra</s>'s array.

body.text: eṣā dhāraṇī udgrahaṇīyā / mayā asyāṃ vidyāyāṃ siddhiḥ prāptā / avāme avāme avāme / om vare om vare / parikuñja naṭa naṭa puskara vahaja lukha / khama khama / ili mili / kili mili / kīrtivara / mudre mudre mukhe svāhā / evaṃ mayā śrutam / ekasmin samaye bhagavān rājagṛhe mahānagare viharati vyākalantakanivāpe sārdhaṃ mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhaṃ bhikṣusahasraiḥ sarvairarhadbhiḥ kṣīṇāsravairniṣkleśairvaśībhūtaiḥ suvimuktacittaiḥ suvimuktaprajñairājāneyaiḥ mahānāgaiḥ kṛtakṛtyaiḥ kṛtakaraṇīyaiḥ apahṛtabhāraiḥ anuprāptasvakārthaiḥ parikṣīṇabhavasaṃyojanaiḥ samyagājñāsuvimuktacittaiḥ sarvacetovaśitāparamapāramitāprāptairekānte niṣaṇṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ bodhisattvaniyutaiḥ mahatā bodhisattvasaṃghena tadyathā meruśikharadharakumārabhūtena varūṇamatikumārabhūtena sumatikumārabhūtena jinamatikumārabhūtena raśmimatikumārabhūtena ākāśamatikumārabhūtena vidyunmatikumārabhūtena mañjuśriyā kumārabhūtena śākyakumārabhūtena varūṇakumārabhūtena vimalakumārabhūtena maitreyeṇa bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / te sarve bodhisattvaniyutāḥ kṣāntidhāraṇa-samādhi-pratilabdhāḥ sarvadharmānāvaraṇajñāḥ sarvasattvasamacittāḥ sarvamāraviṣayasamatikrāntāḥ sarvatathāgataviṣayāvatārajñānakuśalā mahāmaitrī mahākaruṇāsamanvāgatā upāyajñānakuśalāḥ /
body.translated_text: This <s>dhāraṇī</s> (protective spell) is to be memorized. I have attained success in this <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge-spell). <s>Avāme avāme avāme / oṃ vare oṃ vare / parikuñja naṭa naṭa puskara vahaja lukha / khama khama / ili mili / kili mili / kīrtivara / mudre mudre mukhe svāhā</s>. Thus have I heard. At one time the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling in the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, at <s>Vyākalantakanivāpa</s>, together with a great assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), together with thousands of <s>bhikṣus</s>, all of whom were <s>arhats</s> (worthy ones) who had destroyed the impurities, were free from afflictions, had gained mastery over themselves, were well-liberated in mind, well-liberated in wisdom, were thoroughbreds, great serpents, who had done what was to be done, accomplished what was to be accomplished, laid down the burden, attained their own goal, completely destroyed the fetters of existence, were well-liberated in mind through perfect knowledge, had attained the supreme perfection of complete mastery over all mental states, and were seated in a secluded place; together with tens of millions of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, a great assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, namely the prince <s>Meruśikharadhara</s>, the prince <s>Varūṇamati</s>, the prince <s>Sumati</s>, the prince <s>Jinamati</s>, the prince <s>Raśmimati</s>, the prince <s>Ākāśamati</s>, the prince <s>Vidyunmati</s>, the prince <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the prince <s>Śākya</s>, the prince <s>Varūṇa</s>, the prince <s>Vimala</s>, and the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> (great being) <s>Maitreya</s>. All those tens of millions of <s>bodhisattvas</s> had attained the <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention), and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration); they knew all <s>dharmas</s> without obstruction, had equal minds toward all beings, had completely transcended the domain of all <s>māras</s>, were skilled in the knowledge of entering the domain of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, were endowed with great loving-kindness and great compassion, and were skilled in the knowledge of skillful means.

body.text: tasmin samaye rājagṛhe mahānagare dvau prājñau parivrājakau prativasataḥ medhāvinau aṣṭādaśavidyāsthānapāraṃgatau pañcaśataparivārau / tatra eka upatiṣya aparaśca kolitaḥ / etau dvau gaṇamukhayau parivrājakau parasparaṃ saṃsthāpanaṃ kṛtavantau / yadāvayoścaikaḥ prathamamamṛtamadhigacchet tadaparasyārocayitavyam /
body.translated_text: At that time, in the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, there dwelt two wise wandering ascetics, intelligent, who had reached the far shore of the eighteen branches of knowledge, each with a retinue of five hundred. One was <s>Upatiṣya</s> and the other was <s>Kolita</s>. These two leaders of their groups, the wandering ascetics, had made an agreement with each other: whichever of the two first discovers the deathless should inform the other.

body.text: atha khalu āyuṣmānaśvajit pūrvāṇhakālasame nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya prāviśat / adrākṣīdupatiṣyaḥ parivrājako gocarāya prasthitamāyuṣmantamaśvajitaṃ rājagṛhe mahānagare piṇḍāya carantaram / dṛṣṭvāsyaitadabhavat / na me kasyacit pūrvaṃ śramaṇasya vā brāhmaṇasya vānyeṣāṃ vā keṣāṃcin manuṣyabhūtānāmayamevaṃrūpaḥ prāsādikaḥ īryāpa[thaḥ]yathāsya bhikṣoryattvahametamupasaṃkramya paripṛccheyam / kaste āyuṣman śāstā kaṃ boddiśya pravrajitaḥ kasya vā dharmo rocate /
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Aśvajit</s>, having dressed in the morning time and taken his bowl and robe, entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms. The wanderer <s>Upatiṣya</s> saw the venerable <s>Aśvajit</s>, who had set out for his alms-round, walking for alms in the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>. Having seen him, this thought occurred to him: Never before have I seen such a serene deportment in any ascetic, <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (priest), or any other human being as in this <s>bhikṣu</s>. Let me approach him and ask. Who is your teacher, venerable one? Under whom have you gone forth? Whose teaching pleases you?

body.text: athopatiṣyaḥ yenāyuṣmānaśvajit tenopasaṃkrāmadupasaṃkramyābhyupetyāyuṣmatāśvajitā sārdhaṃ saṃmukhaṃ saṃmodanīṃ saṃrañjanīṃ vividhāṃ kathāmupasaṃsṛtya [kānte nyaṣīdat / ekānte niṣaṇṇa upatiṣyaḥ] parivrājaka āyuṣmantaśvajitametadavocat / kaste āyuṣman śāstā kaṃ boddiśya pravrajitaḥ kasya vā dharmo rocate / athāyuṣmānaśvaji[dupatiṣyaṃ parivrāja]kametadavocat /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Upatiṣya</s> approached the venerable <s>Aśvajit</s>, and having approached, exchanged various pleasant and delightful words of greeting face to face with the venerable <s>Aśvajit</s>, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, <s>Upatiṣya</s> the wanderer said this to the venerable <s>Aśvajit</s>: Who is your teacher, venerable one? Under whom have you gone forth? Whose teaching pleases you? Then the venerable <s>Aśvajit</s> said this to <s>Upatiṣya</s> the wanderer:

children.translated_text: There is a son of the <s>Śākyas</s>, of great vows and austerities, supreme among all, self-mastered—
He who has crossed the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) and, though liberated himself, is also a liberator of the world,
Called <s>Buddha</s> (the Awakened One), the unsurpassedly awakened one, the dryer of the ocean of suffering here—

children.text: taṃ yātaḥ śaraṇaṃ sadāhamamalo dharmastato rocate // Rkp_1.1 //
children.translated_text: To him I have gone for refuge, ever pure; his <s>Dharma</s> (teaching) pleases me. //<s>Rkp</s> 1.1//

body.text: upatiṣya āha / kiṃvādī tava śāstā kimākhyāyī /
body.translated_text: <s>Upatiṣya</s> said: What does your teacher proclaim? What does he teach?

body.text: āyuṣmānaśva[jidāha / tasmāt āyuṣman śṛṇu sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru bhāṣiṣye /
body.translated_text: The venerable <s>Aśvajit</s> said: Therefore, venerable one, listen well and pay careful attention; I shall speak.

children.translated_text: Just as the course of the world proceeds with <s>karma</s> (action) and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) together with their causes and conditions,
The <s>Nāyaka</s> (Leader) also proclaimed the cause for the cessation of <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s>.
Where suffering, bound by birth, old age, and calamity, does not persist—

children.text: taṃ mokṣapravaraṃ sa vādivṛṣabho jñātvā svayaṃ bhāṣate // Rkp_1.2 //
children.translated_text: That supreme liberation, the bull among debaters, having known it himself, proclaims. //<s>Rkp</s> 1.2//

body.text: athopatiṣyasya parivrājakasyemaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā virajovigatamalaṃ vigatopakleśaṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣurviśuddham / sa srotaāpattiphalaṃ prāptastasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata /
body.translated_text: Then, upon hearing this exposition of the <s>Dharma</s>, the wanderer <s>Upatiṣya</s>'s <s>Dharma</s>-eye became purified—stainless, free from impurity, free from defilements—regarding all phenomena. Having attained the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>), at that moment he uttered these verses:

children.translated_text: ...... ...... ...... the one that always dries up the rivers of birth,

children.text: yad buddhen sudurlabhaṃ śruta mayā dharmāmṛtaṃ deśitam /
children.translated_text: That <s>Dharma</s>-nectar, so hard to obtain, taught by the <s>Buddha</s>, has been heard by me.
For the pacification of the world's suffering, incomparable in the splendor of wisdom—
...... ...... ...... this path is indeed accomplished. //<s>Rkp</s> 1.3//

body.text: athopatiṣyaḥ parivrājakaḥ āyuṣmantamaśvajitametadavocat / kutrāyuṣmā[na viha]ratyarhan samyak saṃbuddhaḥ / āyuṣmānaśvajidāha /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Upatiṣya</s> the wanderer said this to the venerable <s>Aśvajit</s>: Where, venerable one, does the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, dwell? The venerable <s>Aśvajit</s> said:

body.text: ihaivāyuṣman bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati sma veṇuvane kalandakani [vāpe mahābhikṣusaṃghe]na sārdhaṃ yaduta jaṭilasahasreṇa pravrajitena / upatiṣya āha / eṣo 'haṃ sakhāyaṃ saśiṣyavargamavalokya pravrajiṣyāmi /
body.translated_text: Right here, venerable one, the <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, at the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove), at the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s> (Squirrel Feeding Ground), together with a great assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s>, namely with a thousand matted-hair ascetics who had gone forth. <s>Upatiṣya</s> said: I shall go and, having seen my friend together with his group of disciples, will go forth.

body.text: athopatiṣyaḥ parivrājakaḥ āyuṣmato 'śvajitaḥ pādau śirasābhivandya triḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā prākrāmat / ya[tra kolitaḥ] tenopajagāma / adrākṣīt kolitaḥ parivrājakaḥ upatiṣyaṃ parivrājakaṃ dūrata evāgacchantam / dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ upatiṣyaṃ pari[vrājakamāha] / viprasannāni te āyuṣmannindriyāṇi pariśuddho mukhavarṇaḥ paryavadātaśchavivarṇaḥ / āha / amṛtaṃ te āyuṣmannadhigatam / upatiṣya [āha / āyuṣma]nnadhigatamamṛtamiti / āyuṣman śṛṇu sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te yanmayādhigatam /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Upatiṣya</s> the wanderer, having bowed his head at the feet of the venerable <s>Aśvajit</s> and circumambulated him three times, departed. He went to where <s>Kolita</s> was. The wanderer <s>Kolita</s> saw the wanderer <s>Upatiṣya</s> coming from afar. Having seen him, he said to <s>Upatiṣya</s> the wanderer: Your faculties are serene, venerable one; your complexion is pure; your skin color is radiant. He said: You have attained the deathless, venerable one! <s>Upatiṣya</s> said: Venerable one, the deathless has been attained. Venerable one, listen well and pay careful attention; I shall tell you what I have attained.

body.text: atha kolitaḥ pari[vrājaka e]kāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yenopatiṣyaḥ parivrājakastenāñjaliṃ praṇamyai[tadavocat] /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Kolita</s> the wanderer, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder and placed his right knee on the ground, extended his joined palms toward <s>Upatiṣya</s> the wanderer and said this:

children.translated_text: By which I might cross over this flood of the three realms of existence and destroy the great <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates)—

children.text: vada mārgamekaṃ śiva śokahīnaṃ yamatra jāneyaṃ hyapunarbhavāya] // Rkp_1.4 //
children.translated_text: Tell me that one path, auspicious and free from grief, by which I may know the way to non-return. //<s>Rkp</s> 1.4//

body.text: athopati[ṣyaḥ ā]ha /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Upatiṣya</s> said:

children.translated_text: Just as the course of the world proceeds with <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> together with their causes and conditions,
The <s>Nāyaka</s> (Leader) also proclaimed the cause for the cessation of <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s>.
Where suffering, bound by birth, old age, and calamity, does not persist—

children.text: taṃ mokṣapravaraṃ sa vādivṛṣabho jñātvā svayaṃ bhāṣate // Rkp_1.5 //
children.translated_text: That supreme liberation, the bull among debaters, having known it himself, proclaims. //<s>Rkp</s> 1.5//

body.text: kolito 'pyāha /
body.translated_text: <s>Kolita</s> also said:

children.translated_text: For the pacification of suffering, O peaceful one ...... ......
That which pacifies all afflictions, impurities, wrong views, and faults, and which cuts off ignorance,
The conditioned is merely empty, hollow, void, and deceptive—

children.text: bhūyo brūhi padaṃ hi yena vimalaṃ śrutvā [śamaṃ lapsyate] // Rkp_1.6 //
children.translated_text: Speak again that word by which, having heard it, one will attain the stainless peace. //<s>Rkp</s> 1.6//

body.text: upatiṣya āha /
body.translated_text: <s>Upatiṣya</s> said:

children.translated_text: Just as the course of the world proceeds with <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> together with their causes and conditions,
The <s>Nāyaka</s> (Leader) also proclaimed the cause for the cessation of <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s>.
Where suffering, bound by birth, old age, and calamity, does not persist,

children.text: taṃ mokṣapravaraṃ sa vādivṛṣabho jñātvā svayaṃ bhāṣate // Rkp_1.7 //
children.translated_text: That supreme liberation, the bull among debaters, having known it himself, proclaims. //<s>Rkp</s> 1.7//

body.text: atha tatraiva kolitena parivrājakena virajovigatamalaṃ vigatopakleśaṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣurviśuddhaṃ sa śrotaāpattiphalaṃ saṃprāptaḥ / evamāha /
body.translated_text: Then right there, the wanderer <s>Kolita</s>'s <s>Dharma</s>-eye became purified—stainless, free from impurity, free from defilements—regarding all phenomena. He attained the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>). He spoke thus:

children.text: oghottāraṇa eṣa bhūtacaraṇaḥ śāntaḥ plavo vegavān
children.translated_text: This is the crossing over the flood, the true practice, peaceful, a swift raft—
This supreme knowledge, the pacifier of the three sufferings, leading to the far shore of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
This is indeed the full understanding that destroys the <s>skandhas</s> and <s>kleśas</s> and subdues <s>Māra</s>—
This is liberation, cleansed of enmity and conflict, the dryer of the ocean of suffering. //<s>Rkp</s> 1.8//

body.text: kolita āha / kutra sa bhagavānetarhi buddho viharati / upatiṣya āha / śrutaṃ me āyuṣmannihaiva ca sa bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati veṇuvane kalandakani[vāpe] bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhaṃ bodhisattvasaṃghena sārdham / evaṃ śrutvā upasaṃkramya ekānte nyaṣīdat / āvāṃ bhagavato 'ntike pravrajyāṃ grahīṣyāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Kolita</s> said: Where does the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Buddha</s>, now dwell? <s>Upatiṣya</s> said: I have heard, venerable one, that right here the <s>Bhagavān</s> is dwelling in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, at the <s>Veṇuvana</s>, at the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>, together with an assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> and an assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Having heard this, let us approach and sit to one side. We two shall receive ordination in the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: kolita āha / evam āyuṣman pravrajyaivāstu sahāvayoḥ parivāreṇa / upatiṣya-kolitau parivrājakau parivārasaṃghena sārdhaṃ yena bhagavān tenopajagmatuḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Kolita</s> said: So be it, venerable one; let the going forth be for both of us together with our retinue. The wanderers <s>Upatiṣya</s> and <s>Kolita</s>, together with their retinue, went to where the <s>Bhagavān</s> was.

body.text: atha tena kṣaṇalavamuhūrtena māraḥ pāpīyānaśrauṣit / yāvaṅgamagadheṣu janapadeṣu vikhyātayaśaskīrttisamanvāgatau satpuruṣā vupatiṣyakolitau saparivārāvicchataḥ śramaṇasya gautamasya śāsane pravrajyāṃ [grahītum] / evaṃ śrutvā so 'cintayat /
body.translated_text: Then, in that very instant, moment, and second, <s>Māra</s> the Evil One heard: The two renowned and illustrious good men, <s>Upatiṣya</s> and <s>Kolita</s>, together with their retinues, in the provinces of <s>Aṅga</s> and <s>Magadha</s>, wish to receive ordination in the teaching of the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>. Having heard this, he thought:

body.text: sa cettau śramaṇasya gautamasya śiṣyau bhaviṣyataḥ śūnyaṃ me māraviṣayaṃ kariṣyataḥ / sāṅkathyataḥ satpuruṣau pravrajyāyā vicchedayeyam / atha pāpī[yān acintayat / veṣāntaraṃ parigṛhya upasaṃkrameyam] /
body.translated_text: If those two become disciples of the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>, they will make my domain of <s>Māra</s> empty. Through conversation, I shall turn those good men away from going forth. Then the Evil One thought: I shall approach them in a different guise.

body.text: atha tena kṣaṇena māraḥ pāpīyān śīghrameva svabhavanādantardhāyāyuṣmato 'śvajito veṣaliṅgena ca pathena tayoḥ satpuruṣayoḥ [purataḥ upasaṃkrāntaḥ / upasaṃkramya etadavocat /
body.translated_text: Then, in that instant, <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, swiftly disappearing from his own abode, assumed the appearance and marks of the venerable <s>Aśvajit</s> and approached along the path in front of those two good men. Having approached, he said this:

children.text: uktaṃ] sarvamidaṃ mayā hi vitathaṃ hetūpamaṃ kāraṇaṃ
children.translated_text: All that was said by me was indeed false—the reasoning about causes and conditions—
It was only to test the inclinations of your minds that I spoke thus.

children.text: sarvaṃ caitadapārthakaṃ hi kathitaṃ nāstyatra hetuḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: All that was spoken is indeed meaningless; there is no cause here,

children.text: kṛṣṇasyāsya śubhasya [karmaṇa iha prā]ptiḥ phalaṃ vā kutaḥ // Rkp_1.9 //
children.translated_text: And from this dark or bright <s>karma</s> (action), where is the attainment of fruit? //<s>Rkp</s> 1.9//

children.text: kṣipraṃ kāmaguṇeṣvatīva carataṃ kriḍāṃ yuvāṃ vindataṃ
children.translated_text: Quickly, indulge excessively in sensual pleasures! You two, find delight!

children.text: mṛtyurnāsti na janma nārtijarase lokaḥ paro nāsti vaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no death, no birth, no suffering, no old age; there is no other world for you.

children.text: puṇyāpuṇyaphalaṃ ca karmajanitaṃ nāstyatra hetuḥ kriyā
children.translated_text: There is no fruit of merit or demerit born from <s>karma</s>; there is no cause here—religious practice

children.text: lābhāya vadatīha śākyatanayo mā śraddhayā gacchatam // Rkp_1.10 //
children.translated_text: Is spoken for profit by this son of the <s>Śākyas</s>. Do not go with faith! //<s>Rkp</s> 1.10//

body.text: athopatiṣya-kolitayoretadabhūt / māro vatāyaṃ pāpīyānupa[saṃkrānta āvayoḥ pravrajyābhicchedanārtham / athopatiṣyaḥ parāṅmukhaḥ [svapa]riṣadamāhūyaivamāha / śṛṇuta yūyaṃ māṇavakāḥ / smarata saṃsāradoṣān /
body.translated_text: Then this thought occurred to <s>Upatiṣya</s> and <s>Kolita</s>: This is indeed <s>Māra</s> the Evil One who has approached to obstruct our going forth. Then <s>Upatiṣya</s>, turning away, summoned his assembly and spoke thus: Listen, young men! Remember the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s>!

children.translated_text: The world is afflicted by old age and surrounded by death.
For the abandonment of both, take up the going forth well! //<s>Rkp</s> 1.11//

body.text: atha
body.translated_text: Then <s>Kolita</s> said to <s>Māra</s>:

body.text: kolito māraṃ provāca /

children.text: te jñātaḥ pravaraḥ satāṃ matidharo dharmastriduḥkhāntakṛt
children.translated_text: He is known as the foremost of the virtuous, the bearer of wisdom, whose <s>Dharma</s> puts an end to the three sufferings—
There is no one who could shake this resolve of ours in any way.
With steadfast minds, ever risen for the pacification of craving through speech—
Do not confuse us with the words of a jackal wearing the appearance of a lion! //<s>Rkp</s> 1.12//

body.text: yāśca devatā dṛṣṭasatyāstā gaganasthitāstābhyāṃ satpuruṣābhyaṃ sādhukāraṃ pradaduḥ / sādhu sādhu satpuruṣāḥ sarvalokaviśru[ta] eṣa mārgo yaduta pravrajyāniṣkramaḥ / sarvaduḥkhopaśānta eṣa mārgaḥ / sarvatathāgatagocarāvatāra eṣa mārgaḥ sarvabuddhairbhagavadbhirvarṇitaḥ / praśasta eṣa mārgaḥ /
body.translated_text: And those deities who had seen the truth, standing in the sky, gave their applause to those two good men: Well done! Well done, good men! This path is renowned throughout the world, namely the departure into going forth. This is the path that pacifies all suffering. This is the path that enters the domain of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, praised by all the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones. This path is commended.

body.text: atha khalu māraḥ pāpīyān duḥkhito durmanā vipratisārī tatraivāntarjagāma / atha khalu upatiṣyakolitau parivrājakau svapariṣadamavalokyaitad vacanam ūcatuḥ / yat khalu māṇavakā yūyaṃ jānīdhvamāvāṃ jarāmaraṇasāgarapāraṃgamāya tathāgatamuddiśya
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, pained, dejected, and remorseful, vanished right there. Then the wanderers <s>Upatiṣya</s> and <s>Kolita</s>, looking at their own assembly, spoke these words: Know this, young men: we two have set out for the going forth, aiming to cross beyond the ocean of old age and death, directed toward the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: pravrajyāṃ saṃprasthitau / yaḥ punaryuṣmākaṃ necchati bhagavataḥ śāsane pravrajitum ihaiva nivartatām / sarvāṇi ca tāni pañca māṇavakaśatānyevamāhuḥ / yat kiñcid vayaṃ jānīmastat sarva yuvayoranubhāvena / nūnaṃ yuvāmudāre sthāne pra[vrajitau / yam uddiśya pravrajitau yuvāṃ tamuddiśya] vayamapi pravrajiṣyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: Whoever among you does not wish to go forth in the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, let him turn back right here. And all those five hundred young men spoke thus: Whatever we know, all of that is through the power of you two. Surely you two have gone forth to a noble station. He toward whom you two have gone forth—toward him we too shall go forth.

body.text: athopatiṣyakolitau parivrājakau pañcaśataparivārau bhagavantamuddiśya pravrajyāyāṃ saṃprasthitau viditvā māraḥ pāpīyān bahirdeśe rājagṛhasya mahānagarasya mahāprapātamabhinirmitavān yojanaśatānāmadhastāt yathā tau na śakṣyataḥ śramaṇasya gautamasyāntikamupasaṃkramitumiti / bhagavāṃśca punastādṛśī[mṛddhimabhinirmimīte yena]tāvupatiṣyakolitau parivrājakau taṃ mahāprapātaṃ na dadarśatuḥ ṛjunā mārgeṇa gacchantau / punarapi māraḥ pāpīyāṃstayoḥ purataḥ parvatamabhinirmimīte [kaṭhinamekaghanamabhedyaṃ] suṣiraṃ yojanasahasramuccaistvena sahasraṃ ca siṃhānāmabhinirmimīte caṇḍānāṃ duṣṭānāṃ ghorāṇām / tau ca satpuruṣau bhagavatastejasāpyanubhāvena na ca dadarśatuḥ siṃham / na ca siṃhanādaṃ śuśruvatuḥ / ṛjunā ca mārgeṇa yena bhagavāṃstenopacakramatuḥ / bhagavāṃścānekaśatasahasrayā pariṣadā parivṛtaḥ [puraskṛto dharmaṃ] deśayati sma /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Upatiṣya</s> and <s>Kolita</s>, the two wandering ascetics with a retinue of five hundred, having set out for ordination directed toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>—<s>Māra</s> the Evil One, knowing this, created a great abyss outside the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, a hundred <s>yojanas</s> deep, so that those two would not be able to approach the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>. But the <s>Bhagavān</s> in turn manifested such supernatural power that those two wandering ascetics <s>Upatiṣya</s> and <s>Kolita</s> did not see that great abyss and went by the straight path. Again <s>Māra</s> the Evil One created before them a mountain—hard, solid, impenetrable, hollow, a thousand <s>yojanas</s> in height—and created a thousand lions, fierce, vicious, and terrifying. But those two good men, by the power and majesty of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, neither saw a lion nor heard a lion's roar, and they proceeded by the straight path toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>. And the <s>Bhagavān</s>, surrounded and attended by an assembly of many hundreds of thousands, was teaching the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma / paśyata yūyaṃ bhikṣavaḥ etau dvau satpuruṣau gaṇapramukhau gaṇaparivārau / anupaśyāmo
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: 'Look, monks, at these two good men, leaders of their group, attended by their group.' 'We see them

body.text: vayaṃ bhagavan / bhagavānāha / abhyanujñātau etau dvau satpuruṣau saparivārau mamāntike [pravrajiṣyataḥ /] pravrajitvā eko mama sarvaśrāvakāṇāṃ prajñāvatāmagre bhaviṣyati dvitīya ṛddhimatām / athānyataro bhikṣustasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata /
body.translated_text: , <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'These two good men with their retinue are permitted to go forth in my presence. Having gone forth, one will become foremost among all my disciples in wisdom, the second foremost in supernatural powers.' Then another monk at that moment spoke these verses:

children.text: etau ca vijñapuruṣau paricāra[ya]ntau yau vyākṛto hitakareṇa narottamena /
children.translated_text: These two wise men who attend [the Teacher], who were prophesied by the beneficent, best of men—

children.text: samanvitaṛddhiyau dhī-viśāradau upentīha gauravādatra etau // Rkp_1.13 //
children.translated_text: endowed with supernatural powers and wisdom, bold—they come here out of reverence, these two. // Rkp_1.13 //

body.text: atha khalu sa bhikṣurutthāyāsanād bahubhirbhikṣubhiḥ sādhaṃ bahubhiśca gṛhasthapravrajitairabhyudgamya tau satpuruṣau paryupāste sma / atha [tau satpuruṣau] yena bhagavāṃstenopajagmatuḥ / upetya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavataḥ purataḥ sthitvā bhagavantametadūcatuḥ / labhevahi āvāṃ vo bhagavato 'ntike pravrajyāmupasampadāṃ bhikṣubhāvena / careva āvāṃ bhagavato 'ntike brahmacaryam / bhagavānāha / kiṃnāmā[nau] yuvāṃ kulaputrau / upatiṣya
body.translated_text: Then that monk, rising from his seat, together with many monks and many householders-gone-forth, went out to meet those two good men and attended upon them. Then those two good men approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, circumambulated him three times, stood before the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and said to him: 'May we obtain, <s>Bhagavān</s>, the going forth and full ordination as monks in your presence. May we practice the holy life in your presence.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What are your names, sons of good family?' <s>Upatiṣya</s>

body.text: āha / tiṣyasya brāhmaṇasyāhaṃ putraḥ / [mā]tā me śārikā nāma / tato me janma / tena me śāriputra iti nāmadheyaṃ kṛtam / abhyanujñāto 'haṃ pūrvaṃ mātāpitṛbhyāṃ pravrajyāyai / kolita āha / pitā me kolito nāma / mātā me mudgalā nāma / tena me maudgalyāyana iti sāmānyaṃ nāmadheyaṃ kṛtam / kaści[t]me janaḥ kolita iti saṃjānāti / kaścinmaudgalyāyana iti / [abhyanujñāto ']haṃ pūrvaṃ mātāpitṛbhyāṃ pravrajyāyai / bhagavānāha / carataṃ śāriputra-maudgalyāyanau saparivārau mamāntike brahmacaryamiti / saivānayoḥ pravrajyopasampadā ca / acirapravrajitau ca śāriputra-maudgalyāyanau saparivārau /
body.translated_text: said: 'I am the son of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Tiṣya</s>. My mother is named <s>Śārikā</s>. From her is my birth. Therefore the name <s>Śāriputra</s> was given to me. I was previously permitted by my parents for the going forth.' <s>Kolita</s> said: 'My father is named <s>Kolita</s>. My mother is named <s>Mudgalā</s>. Therefore the common name <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> was given to me. Some people know me as <s>Kolita</s>, some as <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>. I was previously permitted by my parents for the going forth.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Practice the holy life in my presence, <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, with your retinue.' That itself was their going forth and full ordination. And <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, recently ordained, with their retinue—

body.text: atha māraḥ pāpīyān maheśvararūpeṇa bhagavataḥ purataḥ sthitvaivamāha /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, standing before the <s>Bhagavān</s> in the form of <s>Maheśvara</s>, spoke thus:

children.translated_text: Those who are skilled in attending to the meaning of the scriptures, who have reached the far shore of the sciences—

children.text: te sarve praṇamanti matsucaraṇau teṣāmahaṃ nāyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: they all bow to my feet; I am their leader.

children.text: kṣipraṃ maccharaṇaṃ saśiṣyapariṣaṃ gacchāhi bho gautama
children.translated_text: Quickly go to my refuge with your disciples and assembly, O <s>Gautama</s>!

children.text: īpsitanirvṛti[prāpaṇāya] viśadaṃ vakṣyāmi mārgaṃ tava // Rkp_1.14 //
children.translated_text: I shall clearly teach you the path for attaining the desired liberation. // Rkp_1.14 //

body.text: bhagavānāha /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

children.translated_text: Your path leads this world to evil destinies, bringing it to the ocean of suffering;

children.text: mārgo me sa carācarasya jagato duḥkhārṇavocchoṣakaḥ /
children.translated_text: my path dries up the ocean of suffering for this world of moving and unmoving beings.
Why do you prattle on, bold and garrulous, with the voice of a wicked jackal?

children.text: vyābhagno 'si na mārakarma iha me śakto 'si kartuṃ punaḥ // Rkp_1.15 //
children.translated_text: You are defeated! You are not able to perform <s>Māra</s>'s work here against me again. // Rkp_1.15 //

body.text: atha māraḥ pāpīyān maheśvararūpamantardhāya brahmaveṣena punarbhagavantaṃ purataḥ sthitvaivamāha /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, making the form of <s>Maheśvara</s> disappear, again stood before the <s>Bhagavān</s> in the guise of <s>Brahmā</s> and spoke thus:

children.translated_text: You who have quelled the sprouts of <s>karma</s>, <s>kleśa</s> (afflictions), and existence through wisdom—
why do you endure sufferings here again for the sake of beings, O sage?

children.text: nāstyasmin jagati prabho kvacidapi tvatpātrabhūto janaḥ
children.translated_text: There is no person anywhere in this world, O Lord, who is a worthy vessel for you.

children.text: kasmāttvaṃ vigatāmayo na tvaritaṃ nirvāsya kālo hi saḥ // Rkp_1.16 //
children.translated_text: Why do you not swiftly pass into <s>nirvāṇa</s>, free from affliction? For the time has come. // Rkp_1.16 //

body.text: bhagavānāha /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

children.translated_text: I see beings equal in number to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>—

children.text: ye vainayikāḥ sthitāḥ karuṇayā te saṃpramocyā mayā /
children.translated_text: those who are to be trained and who stand ready—they are to be liberated by me through compassion.
The world, having reached the states of middling, superior, and inferior, is destined for liberation;

children.text: nirvāsyāmi tato nimantrayasi māṃ śāṭhyena kiṃ durmate // Rkp_1.17 //
children.translated_text: I shall lead them to <s>nirvāṇa</s>—why do you invite me with deceit, O evil-minded one? // Rkp_1.17 //

body.text: atha punarapi māraḥ pāpīyān duḥkhito durmanā vipratisārī tataścāntardhāya svabhuvanaṃ gatvā śokāgāraṃ praviśya niṣaṇṇaḥ / tatkṣaṇameva ca sarvamārabhuvananivāsinaśca sattvāḥ parasparaṃ pṛcchanti sma / ko heturyadasmākaṃ ma[hārājaḥ śokā]gāraṃ praviśya niṣaṇṇo na ca kaścijjānīte /
body.translated_text: Then again <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, pained, dejected, and remorseful, disappeared from there, went to his own realm, and entered the house of grief and sat down. At that very moment, all the beings dwelling in all the realms of <s>Māra</s> asked one another: 'What is the reason that our great king has entered the house of grief and sat down, and no one knows [why]?'

body.text: atha pañca mārakanyāśatāni paramaprītikarāṇi puṣpamālyavilepanāni gṛhītvā paramamanojñairvastrābharaṇai[ra]laṃkṛtya paramamanojñaharṣakarāṇi divyāni tūryāṇi pravādayantyaḥ paramamanojñasvareṇa
body.translated_text: Then five hundred <s>Māra</s> maidens, most delightful, took flowers, garlands, and unguents, adorned themselves with most lovely garments and ornaments, playing most lovely and joy-producing divine instruments, singing and dancing with most lovely voices

body.text: nṛtyantyo gāyantyo vādayantyo mahatā divyena pañcāṅgikena tūryeṇa [ratikriḍāyu]ktena mārasya pāpīmataḥ purataḥ sthitāḥ / sa ca māraḥ pāpīyān bāhūn pragṛhya prakośitumārabdhaḥ / mā śabdaṃ kuruta mā śabdaṃ kuruteti / evamuktāstāḥ punarapi pragāyantyastūryāṇi parājaghnuḥ / māraśca pāpīyān punarapi bāhudvayamutkṣipya prakrośitumārabdho yāvat saptakṛtvaḥ / apsarasastā rati[krīḍāyuktena mārasya pāpīmataḥ purataḥ sthitāsta]thaiva bahudvayam unnāmyotkrośaṃ [ca]kāra / mā śabdaṃ kurudhvaṃ mā śabdaṃ kurudhvamiti / evamuktāśca tāḥ apsarasastūṣṇīṃ tasthuḥ /
body.translated_text: , playing and performing with the great divine five-part music suited for amorous sport, stood before <s>Māra</s> the Evil One. But <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, extending his arms, began to cry out: 'Make no sound! Make no sound!' Thus addressed, they again began singing and striking the instruments. And <s>Māra</s> the Evil One again raised both arms and began to cry out, up to seven times. The <s>apsarases</s>, standing before <s>Māra</s> the Evil One with music suited for amorous sport, likewise raised both arms and he cried out: 'Make no sound! Make no sound!' Thus addressed, those <s>apsarases</s> stood silent.

body.text: atha khalu vidyudvalgusvarā nāmāpsarā yena [māraḥ pāpīyāṃ]stenāñjaliṃ praṇamyaivamāha /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>apsaras</s> named <s>Vidyudvalgusvara</s>, joining her palms toward <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, spoke thus:

children.text: kiṃ te vibho cyutinimittamihādya dṛṣṭaṃ kiṃ vā jagaddhutavahākulamadya jātam /
children.translated_text: What sign of downfall have you seen today, O Lord? Or has the world today become engulfed in fire?

children.text: śatrustavādhikabalaḥ kimihāsti kaścit [kiṃ vā na nandasi sa]māśrayase ca śokam // Rkp_1.18 //
children.translated_text: Is there some enemy here with greater power than yours? Or why do you not rejoice but take refuge in grief? // Rkp_1.18 //

body.text: māraḥ prāha /
body.translated_text: <s>Māra</s> said:

children.text: śatrurmamāsti balavān nigṛhītacetā māyāsuśikṣita bhuvi nara śākyaputraḥ /
children.translated_text: My enemy is powerful, of restrained mind, well-trained in the arts of illusion on earth—the man, the son of the <s>Śākyas</s>.

children.text: tallakṣaṇaṃ yadi na hasti ca kaścidevaṃ śūnyaṃ kariṣya [ti] mamaiṣa sa kāmadhātum // Rkp_1.19 //
children.translated_text: If there is no one of such marks [to oppose him], he will empty my <s>Kāmadhātu</s> (realm of desire). // Rkp_1.19 //

body.text: sā apsarāḥ provāca /
body.translated_text: The <s>apsaras</s> said:

children.text: svāminnupāyabalavīryaparākramaiḥ kaḥ kartuṃ kṣayaṃ para[ma]mīśa ihādya tasya /
children.translated_text: O Master, who by means of skill, strength, valor, and prowess could today bring about the destruction of that supreme lord?

children.text: kaḥ śaknuyāt tribhava[bandha]na-dīrghatīraṃ tṛṣṇārṇavaṃ kṣapayituṃ balaśaktiyuktaḥ // Rkp_1.20 //
children.translated_text: Who, endowed with power and might, could dry up the ocean of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), whose shore is the long bondage of the three realms of existence? // Rkp_1.20 //

body.text: māraḥ prāha /
body.translated_text: <s>Māra</s> said:

children.translated_text: He has nooses of generosity, vows, intention, compassion, and aspiration; he holds the bow grasped with the supreme weapon of emptiness and signlessness;
he teaches the complete cessation of becoming; he is favorable to the path of peace leading out of <s>saṃsāra</s>. // Rkp_1.21 //

children.text: śūnyeṣu grāmanagareṣu vanāntareṣu girikandareṣvapi ca santi tasya śiṣyāḥ /
children.translated_text: In empty villages and cities, in forest interiors, and in mountain caves are his disciples—

children.text: dhyānābhiyuktamanasaḥ praviviktacārāḥ doṣakṣayāya satataṃ vidhivat prayuktāḥ // Rkp_1.22 //
children.translated_text: their minds devoted to <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), wandering in solitude, constantly and properly engaged in the destruction of faults. // Rkp_1.22 //

children.text: ṛddhyāḥ balaiḥ karuṇayā ca sahāyavantau upatiṣya-kaulita ubhau muninā vinītau /
children.translated_text: <s>Upatiṣya</s> and <s>Kaulita</s>, both endowed with powers of <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural ability) and compassion, trained by the Sage—

children.text: trailokyasarvavidhinā suvinītadharmā śūnyaṃ kariṣyati ca me kila kāmadhātum // Rkp_1.23 //
children.translated_text: well-trained in the <s>Dharma</s> by all the methods of the three worlds—will indeed empty my <s>Kāmadhātu</s>. // Rkp_1.23 //

body.text: atha taiḥ pañcabhirmārakanyāśatairmārasya pāpīmato 'ntikād bhagavato guṇavarṇaṃ śrutvā sarvairākāravigatavidyunnāma bodhisattvasamādhiḥ pratilabdhā /
body.translated_text: Then those five hundred <s>Māra</s> maidens, having heard the praise of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s virtues in the presence of <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, all attained the <s>samādhi</s> called '<s>Ākāravigatavidyut</s>' (Lightning Free from Marks), the <s>bodhisattva</s> concentration.

body.text: atha tāni pañca mārakanyāśatāni divyāni tūryāṇi tāni ca divyāpuṣpagandhamālyavilepanābharaṇavibhūṣaṇīkarāṇi yena bhagavāṃstenākṣi[pan] bhagavataḥ [samīpe] / tāni ca divyāni
body.translated_text: Then those five hundred <s>Māra</s> maidens cast the divine instruments and the divine flowers, incense, garlands, unguents, ornaments, and adornments toward the <s>Bhagavān</s> in his presence. And those divine

body.text: [puṣpāṇi tāni ca divyāni] tūryāṇi te ca yāvadalaṃkārā bhagavato 'nubhāvena veṇuvane vavarṣuḥ / tāśca mārakanyāḥ svayamadrākṣuḥ saparivāram / dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ svayameva prasādajātā babhūvuḥ / yena veṇuvane evaṃrūpaṃ puṣpavarṣaṃ pravṛṣṭamiti te ca bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātā bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ / yadbhagavannūnaṃ [śāriputramaudga]lyāyanayoḥ saparivārayoridam evaṃrūpaṃ mahāścaryādbhutādṛṣṭāśrutapūrvaṃ varṣaṃ pravṛṣṭām / ko nvatra bhagavan hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ / bhagavānāha / nāyaṃ [kulaputrayoranubhāvaḥ] hanta pāpīmataḥ pañcamātraiḥ paricārikāśataistato mārabhavanādidamevaṃrūpaṃ mahāpuṣpavarṣaṃ yāvadalaṅkāravarṣamutsṛṣṭaṃ mama pūjākarmaṇe / cira [metā me anukūlāḥ / tā ma]māntikād vyākaraṇaṃ pratilapsyante 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau /
body.translated_text: flowers and divine instruments and all the ornaments, by the power of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, rained down upon the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove). And those <s>Māra</s> maidens saw themselves with their retinue. Having seen, they were again filled with faith on their own. 'What kind of flower rain has fallen in the <s>Veṇuvana</s>!'—and those monks, filled with wonder, asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Surely, <s>Bhagavān</s>, this great, wondrous, marvelous, never-before-seen-or-heard rain has fallen for the sake of <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> with their retinue. What is the cause here, <s>Bhagavān</s>? What is the condition?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'This is not the power of those sons of good family. Rather, five hundred attendant maidens of the Evil One sent from <s>Māra</s>'s realm this great flower rain and ornament rain as an offering to me. They have long been favorable to me. They will receive from me a prophecy of supreme perfect awakening.'

body.text: atha tāni pañcamātrāṇi mārakanyāśatāni svayameva bhagavataḥ śrutaghoṣavyāhāramabhi[śṛṇvanti] / etāśca bhagavanto 'ntike prasādajātāstena prasādaprāmodyena bodhicittam asaṃpramoṣaṃ nāma samādhiṃ pratilebhire /
body.translated_text: Then those five hundred <s>Māra</s> maidens themselves heard the utterance of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s spoken word. And having generated faith in the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, through that faith and joy they attained the <s>samādhi</s> called '<s>Bodhicitta-asaṃpramoṣa</s>' (Non-loss of the Mind of Awakening).

body.text: atha khalu tā mārakanyāḥ [tatraiva veṇu]vane ekāṃsaṃ cīvaraṃ prāvṛtya dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpyāñjaliṃ kṛtvā yasyāṃ diśi bhagavān viharati tāṃ diśaṃ nirīkṣamāṇā evamūcuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then those <s>Māra</s> maidens, right there in the <s>Veṇuvana</s>, having arranged their robes over one shoulder, placed their right knee on the ground, joined their palms, and gazing toward the direction where the <s>Bhagavān</s> dwelt, spoke thus:

body.text: tṛṣṇā nadī nikhilaśoṣakasarvalokam ālokya netravikalaṃ jagadekacakṣuḥ /
body.translated_text: Having seen this entire world parched by the river of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), O single eye of the world for the sight-impaired—

body.text: tvaṃ tārako 'sya jagataḥ sanarāmarasya buddhā vayaṃ kathamihāśu mune bhavema // Rkp_1.24 //
body.translated_text: you are the savior of this world with its humans and gods; how may we, O Sage, quickly become <s>Buddhas</s>? // Rkp_1.24 //

children.text: naradevapūjya bhagavan paramārthavādin strītvaṃ jugupsitamapāsya vayaṃ samagram /
children.translated_text: O <s>Bhagavān</s> honored by humans and gods, speaker of the supreme truth—having cast off entirely the despised state of womanhood,

children.text: ṛddhyā tavottamagatiṃ [tvaritaṃ labhema] gatvā munīndravacanaṃ śṛṇuyāma evam // Rkp_1.25 //
children.translated_text: may we by your supernatural power swiftly attain the supreme destination, and having gone, may we thus hear the word of the Lord of Sages. // Rkp_1.25 //
O <s>Bhagavān</s>, teacher of non-self, seer of the supreme truth, jewel of the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), lamp of pure speech—

children.text: ākṛṣya mārabalamapratima tvamasyodbodhāya śīghramadhunā mama vyākuruṣva // Rkp_1.26 //
children.translated_text: having drawn away the incomparable force of <s>Māra</s>, swiftly grant me now a prophecy of awakening. // Rkp_1.26 //

body.text: atha khalu mārakanyā utthāyāsanādekakaṇṭhena māraṃ pāpī mantametadūcuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Māra</s> maidens, rising from their seats, said in unison to <s>Māra</s> the Evil One:

children.text: tvaṃ nāma duṣkṛtamatibhagavatsakāśe duṣṭaḥ kathaṃ śriyamavāpya calāmasārām /
children.translated_text: You of wicked mind, evil one—how, having obtained fleeting and worthless glory in the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>,
afflicted in your entire being by the sufferings of birth and the rest, have you reached this terrible state, intoxicated with pride? // Rkp_1.27 //

children.text: śraddhāṃ jine kuru tathā vyapanīya roṣaṃ saṃsāra-doṣa-madapaṅka-samuddhṛtātmā /
children.translated_text: Place faith in the Conqueror (<s>Jina</s>), and likewise remove your anger; lift yourself out of the mire of the faults, intoxication, and defilement of <s>saṃsāra</s>;

children.text: eṣo ['stu te vidita] sarvajagasvabhāvaḥ āgaccha kāruṇikamāśugatiṃ prayāmaḥ // Rkp_1.28 //
children.translated_text: may this be known to you—the nature of all worlds. Come, let us with compassion swiftly proceed to the [supreme] destination. // Rkp_1.28 //

body.text: atha khalu mārasya pāpīmataḥ paramaduṣṭamanasaḥ etadabhūt / yattvahaṃ tādṛśaṃ mārabalaviṣayavegaṃ samanusmareyaṃ yadetāni pañca paricārikāśatāni pañcapāśabandhanavaddhamātmānaṃ saṃpaśyeyuryathehaiva nivṛtya vane na punargantuṃ śaknuyuḥ / [mārastāśca bandhuṃ na śaktaḥ /] tat kutaḥ / tathāhi tāni pañca paricārikāśatāni tathāgatādhiṣṭhānāni /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, of supremely wicked mind, thought: 'Let me summon such force of <s>Māra</s>'s power and domain that these five hundred attendant maidens would see themselves as if bound by the five bonds and, turning back right here, would not be able to go again to the forest.' But <s>Māra</s> was unable to bind them. Why? Because those five hundred attendant maidens were under the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s protection.

body.text: atha khalu tāni pañca paricārikā [śatāni] mārasya pāpīmato 'ntikāt pracakramuḥ / [atha mārasya pāpīmataḥ] duṣṭasyaitadabhavat / yattvahaṃ punarapi tādṛśaṃ mārabalaviṣayavegaṃ samanusmareyaṃ yat sarvamidam ākaśavairambhyasaṃghātairmahākālameghairmahākālavāyu [bhiḥ āvṛtaṃ] yathā tā eva paricārikāḥ sarvā digvidikṣu saṃbhrāntāḥ śramaṇagautamaṃ na paśyeyuḥ / punareva me bhavanamāgaccheyuḥ / tathāpi buddhādhiṣṭhānabalena kiya[ntamapi vāyuṃ] na śaknotyutpādayituṃ yo 'ntato bālāgramapi kampayet prāgeva bahutaram /
body.translated_text: Then those five hundred attendant maidens departed from the presence of <s>Māra</s> the Evil One. Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, wicked, thought: 'Let me again summon such force of <s>Māra</s>'s power and domain that all this [space] would be covered with whirlwind storms in the sky, great black clouds, and great black winds, so that those very attendant maidens, confused in all directions, would not see the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> and would return again to my realm.' But even so, by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>'s protection, he was unable to produce even so much wind as would stir a single hair-tip, let alone anything more.

body.text: atha māraḥ pāpīmān bhūyasyā mātrayā duṣṭo duḥkhito durmanā vipratisārī [uccaiḥ]svareṇa svaputragaṇapāriṣadyān vyākrośat / sarvaṃ mārabhavanaṃ śabdena pūrayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s> <s>Pāpīmān</s>, exceedingly corrupted, pained, dejected, and remorseful, shouted in a loud voice at his sons, retinue, and assembly, filling the entire abode of <s>Māra</s> with his cries.

body.text: āgacchata priyasutā gaṇapāriṣadyā bhraṣṭā vayaṃ svaviṣayāt svabālācca ṛddheḥ /
body.translated_text: "Come, dear sons, retinue and assembly! We have fallen from our own domain and from our own power and prosperity.

body.text: jāto 'tra
body.translated_text: There has arisen here, like a poison tree from within, that deceitful conjurer, that sweet-talker, that son of the <s>Śākyas</s>." //1.29//

body.text: eṣa viṣavṛkṣa ivāntarāt sa māyāśaṭho madhuravādī sa śākyaputraḥ // Rkp_1.29 //

atha tena śabdena sarvāstā mārakanyā māraduhitaraśca sarve ca māraputrā gaṇapārṣadyā [dūrataḥ] ṛtamānarūpāḥ śīghramupagamya pāpīmataḥ puratastasthuḥ / tasyāṃ ca pariṣadi jayamatirnāma māra putraḥ sa prāñjalirbhūtvaivamāha /
body.translated_text: Then, upon hearing that cry, all those <s>Māra</s>-maidens, <s>Māra</s>-daughters, all <s>Māra</s>-sons, and retinue members came swiftly from afar in their natural forms and stood before <s>Pāpīmān</s>. In that assembly, a <s>Māra</s>-son named <s>Jayamati</s>, joining his palms, spoke thus:

children.text: kiṃ durmanāḥ paramakopaviduṣṭacetā no kalpadāha iha na cyutirasti te 'smāt /
children.translated_text: "Why are you dejected, with a mind corrupted by extreme anger? This is not a cosmic conflagration, nor is there any fall from this [realm] for you.

children.text: śatrurna cāsti tava kaścidiha pravṛddho mohaṃ gato 'si kimutānyamati[ra]kasmāt // Rkp_1.30 //
children.translated_text: No enemy of yours has grown powerful here. Have you gone mad? What is this sudden delusion?" //1.30//

body.text: māraḥ prāha /
body.translated_text: <s>Māra</s> replied:

children.text: na tvaṃ paśyasi śākyaputra vṛṣalaṃ yat sanniṣaṇṇaṃ
children.translated_text: "Do you not see that low-born son of the <s>Śākyas</s>, seated

children.text: drume yadvākyaṃ vadasīha nāsti balavān śatrustavetyagrataḥ /
children.translated_text: at the tree? The words you speak—'there is no powerful enemy of yours'—right before [us]!

children.text: sarve tena śaṭhena caikabalinā saṃbhrāmitā naikaśo
children.translated_text: By that one deceiver, single-handed, all have been thrown into confusion, each and every one—
...we together with sons and retinue [...] //1.31//

body.text:
ye 'pyasmin jagati pradhānapuruṣā vikhyātakīrtiśriyo
vidvāṃso bahuśāsrakāvyaracanāvyagrāḥ samagrā drutam /
ye taṃ śākyasutaṃ gatādhi[śa]raṇaṃ dha[rmāṅkuśaistāḍitāḥ]
body.translated_text: Even those who are the foremost persons in this world, of celebrated fame and glory, scholars engrossed in composing many treatises and poems—all of them swiftly having taken refuge in that son of the <s>Śākyas</s>, struck by the goads of <s>Dharma</s>,

body.text: sa tveṣa priyavigrahaḥ śaṭhamatiḥ śatrurmayā yudyate // Rkp_1.32 //
body.translated_text: and he, of lovely form but deceitful mind—it is this enemy with whom I must fight." //1.32//

children.text: etā vai paricārikāḥ priyatamāḥ protsṛjya māṃ niṣkṛpāḥ
children.translated_text: "These beloved attendants, most dear, having mercilessly abandoned me,
have swiftly gone to that ascetic for refuge today, forsaking my kingdom.

children.text: taṃ śramaṇaṃ gatādya śaraṇaṃ hitvā [hi me rājyakam] /

children.translated_text: That deceiver will make this entire triple existence empty through his illusions.
Let us burn him to ashes today with all our power and effort!" //1.33//

body.text: atha te sarve māraputrāḥ sapārṣadyāḥ [prāñjalayaḥ etadūcuḥ] / evamastu yadasmākam ṛddhibalaviṣānubhāvavikurvitaṃ sarvaṃ darśayisyāmaḥ / yadi śaknumaḥ etaṃ śākyaputraṃ bhasmīkartumityevaṃ ku[śalam / yadi na śaknumaḥ tasya śaraṇaṃ gamiṣyāmaḥ /] svayameva pitastvaṃ pratyakṣo 'si / yad vayaṃ mahāsainyaparivṛtāḥ prāgeva ekākinā advitīyena anena śākyaputreṇādhikabalena parājitāḥ kiṃ punaretarhyanekaparicārikā dṛṣṭivivhalāḥ / māraḥ pāpīyānevamāha / gacchata tāvad bhadramukhāḥ / yadi śaknuta evanaṃ śramaṇagautamaṃ ghātayituṃ punarāgacchata / atha na śaktāstathāpyāgacchata / sva[bhavanaṃ vayaṃ pālayiṣyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then all those <s>Māra</s>-sons together with their retinue, joining their palms, said: "So be it! We shall display all our power, strength, might, splendor, and supernatural transformations. If we are able to burn that son of the <s>Śākyas</s> to ashes, then good. If we cannot, we shall go to him for refuge. You yourself, father, are a witness to this. That we, with our great army—"

body.text: atha māraparṣaddvādaśabimbarāṇi tato 'tikramya ita ūrdhvaṃyāvaccaturaśītiṃ yojanasahasrāṇi sphuritvā tādṛśaṃ mārabalaṛddhivegaṃ
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s>'s retinue, traversing beyond twelve <s>bimba</s>-lengths and spreading upward for eighty-four thousand <s>yojanas</s>, displayed such a furious onset of <s>Māra</s>'s army-power and supernatural force.

body.text: darśayāmāsuḥ / [sa]rvaṃ caturdvīpikāyāmākāśaṃ mahākālameghairāpūrayāmāsuḥ / mahākālavāyubhiśca ulkāpātaiśca sumeruṃ parvatarājānaṃ pāṇibhiḥ parājaghnuḥ / sarvaṃ cāturdvīpaṃ prakampayāmāsuḥ / paramabhairavāṃśca śabdān samutsasarjuḥ / yato nāgā mahānāgā yato yakṣā mahāyakṣāḥ sarvāvantyā mahāpṛthivyā sagiriśailaparvatāyāḥ sumeruśca parvatarājaḥ kampaṃ viditvā sarasāṃ mahāsarasāṃ nadīkunadīmahānadīnāṃ mahāsamudrāṇāñca saṃkṣobhaṃ jñātvā gaganatale tasthuḥ / sā ca māraparṣat sumerumavanīṃ sthitvā yojanapramāṇāṃ vṛṣṭim abhinirmīya aṅgamagadheṣu samutsasarjuḥ / mahāntaṃ cāsya musala-pāśa-tomara-bhiṇḍipāla-nārāca-kṣurapra-kṣuramukha-kṣura-nārāca-kṣuraprakṣuramukha-kṣuravāsi-kṣuradantamukha-kṣuradanta-karālavajravāsikṣuradanta-mukha-kṣuradanta-karālavaktra-vikarālavaktra-dṛḍha-kharaparuṣarūkṣavarṣaṃ nirmāya utsasarjuḥ /
body.translated_text: They filled the entire sky over the four continents with great black storm clouds, and with great dark winds, meteor showers, and their fists they struck <s>Sumeru</s>, the king of mountains. They caused the entire four continents to tremble, and they let forth supremely terrifying sounds. All the <s>Nāgas</s>, great <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, great <s>Yakṣas</s>, throughout the great earth—

body.text: atha bhagavān tasmin samaye māramaṇḍalavidhvaṃsanaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpede / [yena sarvāṃ] śilāpraharaṇavṛṣṭiṃ divyotpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīka-māndāravamahāmāndārava-puṣpavṛṣṭimadhitiṣṭhat /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, entered the <s>samādhi</s> called "Destruction of <s>Māra</s>'s Maṇḍala." Through it, he transformed the entire rain of stones and weapons into a divine rain of <s>utpala</s>, <s>padma</s>, <s>kumuda</s>, <s>puṇḍarīka</s>, <s>māndārava</s>, and great <s>māndārava</s> flowers.

body.text: tāṃśca śabdān nānāvādyānadhyatiṣṭhat / yaduta [dharmaśabdaṃ buddhaśa]bdaṃ saṃghaśabdaṃ pāramitāśabdam abhijñāśabdaṃ bodhimaṇḍopasaṃkramaṇaśabdaṃ yāvatsopā[dānanirupādānaśabdā] nadhyatiṣṭhat / sarvā rajo 'ndhakāravāyavaḥ praśemuḥ / ye kecidiha cāturdīpike tṛṇagulmauṣadhivanaspatikṣitiśailaparvatāstān sarvān sapta mahāratnānadhyatiṣṭhat / anava loka]nataḥ mūrdhnā bhagavān yāvad brahmalokaṃ kāyena vaśaṃ vartayāmāsa / ekaikasmācca lakṣaṇādbhagavatastādṛśī prabhā niścacāra yayā prabhayā tri[sāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātū]dāreṇābhāsena sphuṭo 'bhūt / ye cāsyāṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasrayāṃ lokadhātau devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnara-mahoragapretapiśāca-kumābhāṇḍa [manuṣyāmanuṣyā] nairayikā vā tairyagyonikā vā yāmalaukikā vā te sarve bhagavantamadrākṣuḥ bahūni ca devanāgayakṣamanuṣyāmanuṣyaśatasahasrāṇi gaganasthāḥ puṣpairavākiran [pra]dakṣiṇaṃ cakruḥ stuvanto namaścakruḥ / bahūni nairayikā tairyagyonikā yāmalaukikākṣobhyakoṭīśatasahasrāṇi smṛtiṃ pratilebhire / pūrvāvaropitakuśalamūlamanusmṛtya namo buddhāya iti kṛtvā tebhyo 'pāyebhyaścyavitvā deveṣūpapannaḥ / tataśca mārasainyā dvāviṃśatimāraputraśatasahasrāṇi sapārṣadyāni bhagavata evaṃrūpaṃ prātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhagavato 'ntike atīva prasādaṃ pratilabdhvā yena bhagavāṃstenopajagmatuḥ / upetya taiḥ sārdhaṃ pañcabhirmārakanyāśatairbhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya añjalīn pragṛhya ābhirgāthabhiradhibhāṣante sma /
body.translated_text: And those [terrifying] sounds he transformed into various kinds of music—namely, the sound of <s>Dharma</s>, the sound of <s>Buddha</s>, the sound of <s>Saṃgha</s>, the sound of the <s>Pāramitās</s>, the sound of the <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), the sound of approaching the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, and even the sounds of "with remainder" and "without remainder." All the dust, darkness, and winds subsided. Whatever grasses, shrubs, herbs, trees, earth, rocks, and mountains existed in the four continents—

children.translated_text: "O one of pure form, supremely beautiful, ocean of wisdom, equal to a golden <s>Meru</s>,

children.text: vitatya lokaṃ yaśasā vibhāsi tvāmeva nāthaṃ śaraṇaṃ brajāmaḥ // Rkp_1.34 //
children.translated_text: pervading the world with your glory, you shine forth—to you alone, our protector, we go for refuge!" //1.34//
"When the path is lost and eyes are closed, you blaze forth like the sun over the world.

children.text: aparājita prāṇinastvekabandhuṃ tvāṃ sārthavāhaṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajāmaḥ // Rkp_1.35 //
children.translated_text: O Unconquered One, you who are the sole kinsman of beings—to you, our caravan leader, we go for refuge!" //1.35//
"O you whose treasury is enriched with spontaneously arisen wisdom, whose mind is liberated from the very beginning, having the nature of space,
whose words are pleasant and delightful with a compassionate disposition—to the one who has accomplished all aims, we go for refuge!" //1.36//
"You are the liberator from the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s>, the complete demonstrator of cause and effect.

children.text: maitravihārī paramavidhijñaḥ karuṇāvihārī śaraṇaṃ vrajāmaḥ // Rkp_1.37 //
children.translated_text: Abiding in <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), supreme knower of the method, abiding in <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion)—we go to you for refuge!" //1.37//

body.text: māyāmarīcidakacandrasnnibhe bhave prasakto viṣayāśrayeṇa /
body.translated_text: "In this existence, which resembles illusion, a mirage, a reflection, and a moon in water, [beings are] attached through dependence on sense objects.

body.text: ajñānarugnāśaka [lokanātha] taṃ baidyarājaṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajāmaḥ // Rkp_1.38 //
body.translated_text: O Destroyer of the disease of ignorance, O Lord of the World—to that King of Physicians we go for refuge!" //1.38//

children.translated_text: "You are the bridge in the midst of the four floods, the deliverer through the sevenfold noble wealth.

children.text: sanmārgasandarśaka lokabandhuḥ kṛpānvitaṃ tvāmiha pūjayāmaḥ // Rkp_1.39 //
children.translated_text: Shower of the true path, kinsman of the world—compassionate one, we honor you here!" //1.39//
"Forgive us, O one of perfect wisdom—we who were corrupted toward you.

children.text: tamatyayaṃ vīra gṛhāṇa nātha tvamekabandhurjagati pradhānaḥ // Rkp_1.40 //
children.translated_text: Accept that transgression, O Hero, O Protector! You alone are the foremost kinsman in the world." //1.40//

children.text: vayaṃ samutsṛjya hi mārapakṣaṃ [janayāma śreṣṭhamiha bodhicittam] /
children.translated_text: "We, having abandoned <s>Māra</s>'s faction, shall generate the supreme <s>bodhicitta</s> (awakening mind) here.

children.text: nimantrayāmaḥ kila sarvasattvān bodhiṃ labhemo vayamuttamāttu // Rkp_1.41 //
children.translated_text: We invite all beings—may we attain the supreme <s>bodhi</s> (awakening)!" //1.41//
"Show us the noble conduct, so that we may practice the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections).

children.text: ananyavādaiḥ katibhistu [dharmaiḥ sattvā yutā bodhimavāpnuvanti] // Rkp_1.42 //
children.translated_text: By how many teachings, without other doctrines, do beings endowed [with them] attain <s>bodhi</s>?" //1.42//

body.text: puṣpāṇi yatte 'bhimukhaṃ kṣipāmaḥ chatrāṇi tāni bhavantu sarvadikṣu /
body.translated_text: "The flowers that we cast toward you—may they become canopies in all directions,

body.text: tiṣṭhantu murdhni dvipadottāmānāṃ kṣetreṣu sarvartusukhākareṣu // Rkp_1.43 //
body.translated_text: may they rest upon the heads of the best among bipeds, in realms that bring the comfort of all seasons!" //1.43//

body.text: atha khalu māra[putra māra]kanyāśca sagaṇapārṣadyā bhagavantaṃ muktakusumairabhyavākiran / tāni ca bhuktakusumāni bhagavataḥ ṛddhyanubhāvenānekāni koṭīniyutasahasrāṇi gaṅgānadīvālukā[samāni] puṣpacchatrāṇi santiṣṭhante sma / tāni nānāpuṣpacchatrāṇi daśasu dikṣu sarvabuddhānāṃ tiṣṭhatāṃ yāpayatāṃ mūrdhasandhīnāmuparyantarikṣe tasthuḥ svayaṃ ca tā mārakanyāḥ sagaṇapārṣadyā adrākṣuḥ / daśasu dikṣu sarvabuddhakṣetreṣvasaṃkhyeyeṣvaprameyeṣu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ tiṣṭhatāṃ yāpayatāṃ dharmaṃ deśayatāṃ pariṣadā parivṛtānāṃ bhāṣatāṃ tapatāṃ virocatāṃ sanniṣaṇṇānāṃ tāni puṣpacchatrāṇi uparyantarikṣe mūrdhasandhau saṃsthitāni / te ca buddhā bhagavantaḥ samavarṇāḥ samaliṅgāḥ samarūpāḥ samadarśanāḥ / kevalaṃ teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ siṃhāsana-nānātvaṃ pariṣado-[nānātvaṃ] buddhakṣetraguṇavyūha-nānātvaṃ dadṛśuḥ / na ca teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ svaramaṇḍalaṃ [śuśruvuḥ / sā] ca māraparṣat bhagavato 'nubhāvenaivaṃrūpaṃ prātihārya dṛṣṭvā paramaprītiprasādajātā bhagavataḥ pādau śirobhirvanditvā purato niṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Māra</s>-sons, <s>Māra</s>-maidens, and their retinue scattered loose flowers over the Blessed One. Through the supernatural power of the Blessed One, those offered flowers became many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s>, as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and remained as flower canopies. Those various flower canopies [settled] upon the heads of all the <s>Buddhas</s> dwelling and teaching in the ten directions.

body.text: atha khalu tāni māraputrāṇāṃ sagaṇapārṣadyānāṃ daśabimbarāṇāṃ pratinivartya mārabhavane evaṃ vṛttāntaṃ mārāya pāpīmate
body.translated_text: Then those ten <s>bimba</s>-groups of <s>Māra</s>-sons together with their retinue, having turned back, returned to <s>Māra</s>'s abode and reported the entire matter in detail to <s>Māra</s> <s>Pāpīmān</s>.

body.text: vistareṇārocayanti / ekaromakūpamapi cāyaṃ tasya śramaṇasya gautamasya na śakto vidhvaṃsayitumiti / bhūyaśca viṃśatisahasrāṇi tameva śaraṇaṃ jagmuḥ tasyaiva cāgrato niṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya /
body.translated_text: "We were not able to disturb even a single hair-pore of that ascetic <s>Gautama</s>." Furthermore, twenty thousand [more beings] went to him for refuge and sat before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: atha khalu māraḥ pāpīmān bhūyasyā mātrayā caṇḍībhūto duḥkhito durmanāḥ vipratisārya evamāha /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s> <s>Pāpīmān</s>, becoming even more furious, pained, dejected, and remorseful, spoke thus:

children.text: lakṣmīrgatā mama punarna paraiti tāvad yāva[nna mama rājya śākyasuta]sya nāśaḥ /
children.translated_text: "My glory is gone and will not return as long as the son of the <s>Śākyas</s> and [his threat to] my kingdom are not destroyed.

children.text: tūṣṇīṃ sthitā vayamananyamanaḥpratarkāḥ śākyātmajaṃ kathamimamadya tu ghātayema // Rkp_1.44 //
children.translated_text: Let us remain silent, our minds fixed on this single thought—how shall we kill this son of the <s>Śākyas</s> today?" //1.44//

body.text: atha māraḥ pāpīmān durmanaskaḥ eva śokā[gāraṃ prāviśat /]
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s> <s>Pāpīmān</s>, dejected, entered his chamber of grief.

body.text: mahāyānasūtrādratnaketu-mārajihmīkaraṇaḥ parivarto nāma prathamaḥ // 1 //
body.translated_text: End of the first chapter, called "The Humiliation of <s>Māra</s>," from the <s>Mahāyāna</s> sūtra <s>Ratnaketu</s>. //1//

body.text: START Rkp 2
body.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Ratnaketudhāraṇī</s> Chapter 2

body.text: dvitīyaḥ parivartaḥ
body.translated_text: Second Chapter

body.text: atha tā mārakanyā māraputrāśca saganapāriṣadyā bhagavantaṃ [tatkṣaṇaṃ prārthayāmāsuḥ / a]rthikā vayaṃ bhagavannanenaivaṃrūpeṇa yānena ca jñānena ca ṛddhayā kṛpayopāyena pratibhānena ca / āścaryaṃ bhagavan yāvadupāya[jñāna]samanvāgatastathāgataḥ / [katamairbha]gavan dharmaiḥ samanvāgataḥ puruṣapudgalo na ca pāpamitrahastaṃ gacchati kṣipraṃ cānuttarāṃ samyak saṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate / bhagavānāha / caturbhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgataḥ [kulaputra]ihaikatyapuruṣapudgalo na pāpamitrahastaṃ gacchati kṣipraṃ cānuttarāṃ samyak saṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate / katamaiścaturbhiḥ / iha bhadramukhāḥ kulaputraḥ sarvadharmānna parāmārṣṭi na ca kvacid dharmamudgṛṇhāti nopaiti nopādatte nādhitiṣṭhati na kalpayati na vikalpayati yaduta dānapāramitāyāṃ caran na dānaphalaṃ paricarati nodgṛṇhāti nopādatte nādhitiṣṭhati na kalpayati na vikalpayati yāvat prajñāpāramitāyāmapi caran yāvanna kalpayati na vikalpayati /
body.translated_text: Then those <s>Māra</s>-maidens and <s>Māra</s>-sons with their retinue immediately entreated the Blessed One: "We are desirous, O Blessed One, of just such a vehicle, such wisdom, such supernatural power, such compassion, such skillful means, and such eloquence. It is wonderful, O Blessed One, how the <s>Tathāgata</s> is endowed with [such] knowledge of skillful means! With what qualities, O Blessed One, is a person endowed—"

body.text: punaraparaṃ bhadramukhāḥ sa kulaputro na sattvavādī bhavati na jīvavādī na poṣavādī na puruṣavādī na pudgalavādī na sattvadhātuṃ manasā parāmārṣṭi yāvanna kalpayati na vikalpayati /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O fair-faced ones, that son of good family does not hold the view of a being, nor of a life-force, nor of a nourisher, nor of a person, nor of an individual. He does not mentally grasp at the realm of beings, and he neither conceptually constructs nor discriminates.

body.text: punaraparaṃ bhadramukhāḥ sa kulaputro na rūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyāni parāmārṣṭi yāvanna kalpayati na vikalpayati /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O fair-faced ones, that son of good family does not grasp at form, sound, smell, taste, or tangible objects, and he neither conceptually constructs nor discriminates.

body.text: punaraparaṃ bhadramukhāḥ sa kulaputraḥ sarvatryadhvatraidhātukaskandhadhātvāyatanānāṃ hetupratyayālambanaphalavipākasamutthānāśrayotpādānna parāmārṣṭi yāvanna kalpayati na vikalpayati /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O fair-faced ones, that son of good family does not grasp at, nor even conceptualize or discriminate regarding the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) of all three times and the three realms, their causes, conditions, objects, results, fruitions, origins, and supports.

body.text: tat kutaḥ / sarva[jñatājñāna]caryādhiṣṭhānaṃ [sarvaviṣayakalpanāvikalpanāviraheṇa anālambanayogacaryayā] ca kartavyam / abhāvā bhadramukhāḥ sarvadharmāḥ sarvajñatā ca yāvadaghoṣānimittānakṣarāpraṇihitānutpādānirodhālakṣaṇāsaṃgā anālambanādarśanā viviktā nirātmā alakṣaṇīyā kṣaṇavyūpaśāntā atamānālokāsthānāviṣayā[vaśā]pakṣyāpratipakṣyā acintyāheyāmatsarāprapañcā[rajovirajo]niravayavā akiṃcanākārakāvedakānāśrayāgrāhyāvijñaptikāpratibhāsākṣaṇikā bhadramukhāḥ [sa]rvajñatā gaganasamā śūnyānupalambhayogenānadhiṣṭhānayogenāparāmarśayogena
body.translated_text: Why is that? The basis of the practice of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) must be accomplished through freedom from conceptualization and discrimination of all objects, and through the practice of yoga without an object. O fair-faced ones, all <s>dharmas</s> are non-existent, and <s>sarvajñatā</s> likewise—they are without sound, without marks, without syllables, without aspiration, without arising, without cessation, without characteristics, without attachment, without object, without seeing, secluded, without self, undefinable, momentarily quiescent, without darkness or light, without abode, without domain, without sides or counter-sides, inconceivable, without anything to be abandoned, without envy, without proliferation, without dust or freedom from dust, without parts, without possessions, without form, without feeling, without support, ungraspable, without cognizable manifestation, without appearance, momentary. O fair-faced ones, <s>sarvajñatā</s> is like space—it must be accomplished through the yoga of emptiness and non-apprehension, through the yoga of non-establishment, through the yoga of non-grasping,

body.text: akalpavikalpayogena kartavyam /
body.translated_text: through the yoga of non-conceptualization and non-discrimination.

body.text: ebhirbhadramukhāścaturbhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgataḥ [puruṣapu]gdalo na pāpamitrahastaṃ gacchati kṣipraṃ cānuttarāṃ samyak saṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate / yaḥ kaścid bhadramukhāḥ sarvaviṣayasaṃgasamucchraya[la]kṣaṇādhiṣṭhāna[paricaryayā sarvajñatāṃ prārthayate] sa dvayasakto bhavati / dvaya [sakta]manaḥsaṃkalpo visaṃvādayati sarvajñatām / tatra katamad dvayam / yat skandhadhātvāyatanāni lakṣaṇavyavacāreṇādhitiṣṭhati [udgṛṇhāti / dvaya]metad visaṃvādayati sarvajñatām / caryādhiṣṭhānaphalakalpanā dvayametat / jāṭibhavopādānasattvādhiṣṭhānakalpanā dvayametat / deśanāprakāśanaprajñāpana-vākpatharutavyā[hārā]dhiṣṭhānakalpanā dvayametat / uccheda-śāśvatavyavalokana-jñāna-jñeyādhiṣṭhānakalpanā dvayametat / sattvajīvapoṣapuruṣapudgala-kārakakārāpakasaṃjñādhiṣṭhānakalpanā dvayametat / yaḥ pārāpārohāpohānadhitiṣṭhati kalpayati dvayametat / yaḥ kaścid bhadramukhāḥ sarvajñajñānaṃ paryeṣate puruṣapudgalaḥ sa tryadhvāhaṃkāramamakārasamudayanirodhavyavacārānadhitiṣṭhati saṃkalpayati [udgṛṇhāti] tasya dvayametat sarvajñajñāne / tad yathā kaścit puruṣaḥ agnayarthiko bhūtalaṃ parāmṛśet pānārthiko 'gniṃ bhojanārthikaḥ [pāṣāṇaṃ]
body.translated_text: O fair-faced ones, a person endowed with these four <s>dharmas</s> does not fall into the hands of evil friends and quickly fully awakens to unsurpassed perfect <s>sambodhi</s> (complete awakening). O fair-faced ones, whoever seeks <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) through the practice of establishing attachment to all objects and characteristics of arising, that one is attached to duality. One whose mind is intent on duality contradicts <s>sarvajñatā</s>. What is that duality? When one establishes the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, and <s>āyatanas</s> through the determination of characteristics and grasps them—this is the duality that contradicts <s>sarvajñatā</s>. Conceptualization of the results of establishing practices—this is duality. Conceptualization of establishing birth, existence, attachment, and beings—this is duality. Conceptualization of establishing teaching, illumination, instruction, speech-paths, sounds, and expressions—this is duality. Conceptualization of establishing annihilation and eternalism, examination, knowledge, and the knowable—this is duality. Conceptualization of establishing the notions of being, life-force, person, individual, doer, and agent—this is duality. Whoever establishes and conceptualizes the removal and non-removal of the far and near shore—this is duality. O fair-faced ones, whoever, being a person, seeks <s>sarvajña-jñāna</s> (omniscient knowledge) and establishes and conceptualizes the arising and cessation of ego-making and mine-making across the three times and their determination—for that person this is duality regarding <s>sarvajña-jñāna</s>. It is as if a person desiring fire were to grasp at the ground, one desiring drink were to grasp at fire, one desiring food at a stone,

body.text: puṣpārthikaḥ cīvaraṃ gandhārthiko manuṣyakuṇapaṃ cīvarārthikaḥ śmaśānaṃ vastrārthiko 'śmānaṃ vilepanārthikaḥ ākāśaṃ parāmṛśet evameva bhadramukhāḥ yaścaryādhiṣṭhānasaṃgavyavacārasamucchraya-dvayādhiṣṭhānena sarvajñajñānaṃ paryeṣate niṣphalastasya vyāyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: one desiring flowers at a robe, one desiring fragrance at a human corpse, one desiring a robe at a cremation ground, one desiring cloth at a stone, one desiring ointment were to grasp at space—just so, O fair-faced ones, whoever seeks <s>sarvajña-jñāna</s> through the establishment of duality characterized by the determination of attachment to all objects and the arising [of grasping], that person's effort is fruitless.

body.text: atha khalu tasyāmeva pariṣadi dhāraṇamatirnāma bodhisattvaḥ sannipatito 'bhūt sanniṣaṇṇaḥ / sa yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamaiyavamāha / yad bhagavan anabhilāpyadharmaḥ śakyamabhisamboddhum / bhagavānāha / eṣa evābhisaṃbodho yadanabhilāpyaṃ jānīte / tena hi kulaputra tvāmeva pravakṣyāmi / yadi te kṣamaṃ tathā vyākuru /
body.translated_text: Now in that very assembly there was a <s>bodhisattva</s> named <s>Dhāraṇamati</s>, who had arrived and was seated. He approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>, joined his palms in salutation, and spoke thus: 'O <s>Bhagavān</s>, can the inexpressible <s>dharma</s> be fully awakened to?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'This itself is the full awakening—that one knows the inexpressible. Therefore, O son of good family, I shall explain to you. If it is acceptable to you, declare it thus.'

body.text: asti dvayalakṣaṇabhāvo yaḥ sarvajñatā nāma labhate / āha / yadyastīti vakṣyāmi śāśvato bhaviṣyati / atha nāsti ceda vakṣyāmyucchedo bhaviṣyati / madhyamā ca pratipannopalabhyate / nāsāvasti nāpi nāstīti / yadeṣvasaṃgānutpādāvyayāpramāṇāsaṃkhyo 'tamānālokeṣu jñānam eṣa evābhisaṃbodhaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Is there an entity with the characteristic of duality that obtains what is called <s>sarvajñatā</s>?' He said: 'If I were to say "it exists," it would be eternal. If I were to say "it does not exist," it would be annihilation. The middle path is apprehended: it neither exists nor does it not exist. Knowledge regarding these—which are without attachment, without arising, without decay, immeasurable, innumerable, without darkness or light—this itself is the full awakening.'

body.text: vidyunmatirbodhisattva āha / yatra bhagavan nāgatirna gatirityeva jñānāvatārakauśalam eṣa evābhisaṃbodhaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Vidyunmati Bodhisattva</s> said: 'O <s>Bhagavān</s>, where there is neither coming nor going—skill in the descent of knowledge in just this way—this itself is the full awakening.'

body.text: vairocano bodhisattva āha / yatra bhagavan na prāptilakṣaṇaṃ nābhisamayo na sākṣātkriyā na śamo na praśamo na trayadhvaṃ na triyānaṃ na praṇidhisāmīcīmanyanā eṣa evābhisaṃbodhaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Vairocana Bodhisattva</s> said: 'O <s>Bhagavān</s>, where there is no characteristic of attainment, no comprehension, no direct realization, no calm, no tranquility, no three times, no three vehicles, no aspiration or approval—this itself is the full awakening.'

body.text: dhāraṇamatirbodhisattva āha / yo bhagavan na tradhātukaṃ na trīṇī saṃyojanāni na traividyatāṃ na triyānatāṃ na skandhadhātvāyatanāni na kalpayati na vikalpayati na hāniṃ na vṛddhiṃ na sāmīcīṃ karoti eṣa evābhisaṃbodhaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Dhāraṇamati Bodhisattva</s> said: 'O <s>Bhagavān</s>, whoever does not conceptualize or discriminate regarding the three realms, the three fetters, the threefold knowledge, the three vehicles, the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, and <s>āyatanas</s>, and does not make decrease or increase or propriety—this itself is the full awakening.'

body.text: vajramatirbodhisattva āha / yaḥ pṛthagjanadharmaḥ vāryadharmo vā śaikṣadharmaḥ vāśaikṣadharmaḥ vā śrāvakadharmaḥ vā pratyekabuddhadharmaḥ na kalpayati na vikalpayati na sāmīcīṃ karoti eṣa evābhisaṃbodhaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Vajramati Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Whoever does not conceptualize or discriminate regarding the <s>dharma</s> of ordinary beings, the <s>dharma</s> to be abandoned, the <s>dharma</s> of the trainee, the <s>dharma</s> of the non-trainee, the <s>dharma</s> of the <s>śrāvaka</s>, or the <s>dharma</s> of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, and does not make propriety—this itself is the full awakening.'

body.text: dṛḍhamatirbodhisattva āha / [yo vivekanayena] tathatāṃ vyavacārayati eṣa evābhisaṃbodhaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Dṛḍhamati Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Whoever determines <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) through the method of seclusion—this itself is the full awakening.'

body.text: ratnapāṇirbodhisattva āha / yo 'nutpādalakṣaṇaṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ na prāptaye nābhisamayāya na [kalpayati eṣa evābhisaṃbodhaḥ] /
body.translated_text: <s>Ratnapāṇi Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Whoever does not conceptualize the characteristic of non-arising of all <s>dharmas</s> for the sake of attainment or comprehension—this itself is the full awakening.'

body.text: acintyamatirbodhisattva āha / yastraidhātukavyavacāracittameva citte praveśayati ubhe citte na vyavacāryeṇopalabhate eṣa evābhisaṃbodhaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Acintyamati Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Whoever causes the mind that discriminates the three realms to enter into mind itself, and does not apprehend both minds as subject to discrimination—this itself is the full awakening.'

body.text: arivijayo bodhisattva āha / [yaḥ] sarvadharmeṣu na sajyate nānunīyate nopekṣate na pratimanyate na spṛhayate na muhyate na gṛṇhāti na mucyate eṣa evābhisaṃbodhaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Arivijaya Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Whoever, with regard to all <s>dharmas</s>, is not attached, not attracted, not indifferent, not resentful, not desirous, not confused, does not grasp, and is not released—this itself is the full awakening.'

body.text: padmagarbho bodhisattva āha / yaḥ puṇyapāpayoḥ na sajjate gambhīrakṣāntinayāvatārāhaṅkāramamakārānna kalpayati eṣa evābhisaṃbodhaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Padmagarbha Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Whoever is not attached to merit and sin, and through entry into the method of profound patience does not conceptualize ego-making and mine-making—this itself is the full awakening.'

body.text: candraprabhaḥ kumārabhūta āha / yo bhagavān praśamāt sarvadharmānna prajānīte na ca dharmāṇāṃ svabhāvamācayaṃ vopacayaṃ vā paśyati eṣa evābhisaṃbodhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Prince <s>Candraprabha</s> said: 'O <s>Bhagavān</s>, whoever, due to quiescence, does not cognize all <s>dharmas</s>, and does not see either the accumulation or the increase of the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s>—this itself is the full awakening.'

body.text: khagamatiḥ kumārabhūta āha / yasya sarva tama-ālokotpādavyayaḥ [vṛddhihāniḥ] cittacaitasikeṣu na pravartante eṣa evābhisaṃbodhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Prince <s>Khagamati</s> said: 'For whom the arising and decay of all darkness and light, increase and decrease, do not operate in the mind and mental factors—this itself is the full awakening.'

body.text: akṣayamatirbodhisattva āha / yastripariśuddhaḥ pāramitāsu abhyāsaṃ karoti anupalambhayogena na rajyate na virajyate eṣa evābhisaṃbodhaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Akṣayamati Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Whoever, being triply pure, cultivates the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) and, through the yoga of non-apprehension, is neither attached nor detached—this itself is the full awakening.'

body.text: mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūta āha / yo bhagavan [sarva]dharmeṣu na rajyate na virajyate gambhiradharmanayaṃ ca prajānāti / yaśca prajānāti tannāyūhati[na]niryūhati nākarṣati na vyākarṣati na ca kasyaciddharmasyāpacayaṃ vāvidyāṃ [vā]vimuktiṃ cotpādayati vyayaṃ vā hānīṃ vā vṛddhiṃ vā vastuṣu na saṃkalpanato [na] vikalpanataḥ eṣa evābhisaṃbodhaḥ / anenaiva nayena sarvābhisaṃbodhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Prince <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'O <s>Bhagavān</s>, whoever is neither attached nor detached regarding all <s>dharmas</s> and understands the method of the profound <s>dharma</s>; and whoever understands that does not construct it or deconstruct it, does not draw it in or push it away, and does not produce the decay, ignorance, liberation, destruction, decrease, or increase of any <s>dharma</s> in things, neither through conceptualization nor through discrimination—this itself is the full awakening. By this very method is all full awakening.'

body.text:
atha kautūhaliko bodhisattva āha / kiṃ mañjuśrīrāyogaprayogena prayojanam / yadanenaikanayatathatāpraveśenaiva gambhīrabhāvanānayena sarvajñajñānaparijñānam /
mañjuśrīrāha / viṣamadṛṣṭirahitaḥ samyagdṛṣṭi[ra]samāropaḥ / aśāṭhya-ṛjukatāsamāropaḥ / pāparahito gurugauravāsamāropaḥ / suvacanāsa 0 samyagājīvāsa 0 sarvasaṃyojanarahitāsa 0 samākrośa-sarvasattvakṛpāsa 0
body.translated_text:
Then <s>Kautūhalika Bodhisattva</s> said: 'What purpose does application of effort serve, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, if by this single method of entry into <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) alone, through the method of profound cultivation, there is complete knowledge of <s>sarvajña-jñāna</s> (omniscient knowledge)?'
<s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'Free from wrong views, right view without superimposition. Without deceit, uprightness without superimposition. Free from sin, reverence for the teacher without superimposition. Obedient, right livelihood without superimposition. Free from all fetters, without superimposition. Compassion for all beings amidst all blame, without superimposition.

body.text: trisaṃvarāsa 0 avisaṃvādanakuśaladharmāsa 0 avyupaśāntāsa 0 saddharmārakṣāsa 0 sarvasattvāparityāgāsa 0 sarvavastuparityāgāsa 0 durbalasattva-balapratiṣṭhāpanāsa 0 bhītaśaraṇābhayāsa 0 / kumārgasaṃprasthitānāṃ pratipattiniyojanāsa 0 kṣāntisauratyāsa 0 sarvagrāhasaṃ[ga]lakṣaṇāsa 0 sarvarajastamaskandhavarjanāsa 0 sarvapariṇāmanā-phalavipākavarjanāsamāropaḥ 0 / ime kulaputra viṃśatiḥ prayogāḥ sarvajñajñānasya / sarvākṣararutagho[ṣavacanavyāhāravākya-] prabheda tathatājñānapraveśena sarvajñajñānasya prayogaḥ / sarvatathāgatavacanāni anyatīrthikavacanatathatāpraveśena sarvacaryātathatāpraveśena sarvapuṇyo[peta]prajñāpāramitāprayogatathatāpraveśena sarvopādānotpādavyayatathatāpraveśena sarvatrivimokṣāśrayahetukarmadharma[tathatā]praveśena va jñātvā sarvajñajñānasya prayogāvabodho bhavati /
body.translated_text: The three restraints, without superimposition. Non-deception, wholesome <s>dharmas</s> without superimposition. Without complete quiescence, without superimposition. Protection of the true <s>dharma</s>, without superimposition. Non-abandonment of all beings, without superimposition. Relinquishment of all possessions, without superimposition. Establishing strength for weak beings, without superimposition. Refuge and fearlessness for the frightened, without superimposition. Guiding the practice of those who have set out on the wrong path, without superimposition. Patience and gentleness, without superimposition. Without the characteristics of attachment to all grasping, without superimposition. Avoidance of all aggregates of dust and darkness, without superimposition. Avoidance of the fruition and ripening of all dedications of merit, without superimposition. O son of good family, these are the twenty applications of <s>sarvajña-jñāna</s>.
