Through entry into <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) via the knowledge of all syllables, sounds, words, utterances, expressions, and speech-distinctions is the application of <s>sarvajña-jñāna</s>. Having known through entry into the <s>tathatā</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s> utterances, entry into the <s>tathatā</s> of the utterances of other <s>tīrthikas</s>, entry into the <s>tathatā</s> of all practices, entry into the <s>tathatā</s> of the application of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> endowed with all merit, entry into the <s>tathatā</s> of the arising and decay of all attachment, and entry into the <s>tathatā</s> of the causes and <s>dharmas</s> of action depending on the three liberations—there comes the understanding of the application of <s>sarvajña-jñāna</s>.'

body.text: kautūhaliko bodhisattva āha / yāvadetat mañjuśrīryadā imaṃ gambhīraṃ dharmanayamavabudhyate tadā na kaściddharma samanupaśyati yo dharmo deśyeta yasmai deśyeta yairvārthapadavyañjanairdeśyeta prakāśyeta / yaṃ vā punaḥ prajahyād yaṃ vā bhāvayed yaṃ vā parijānīyāt sarvadharmānabhilāpyayogena tathatāṃ praviśati saḥ sarvajñajñānamavabudhyate /
body.translated_text: <s>Kautūhalika Bodhisattva</s> said: 'To the extent that, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, when one understands this profound <s>dharma</s>-method, one does not perceive any <s>dharma</s> that could be taught, to whom it could be taught, or by what meanings, words, and syllables it could be taught or illuminated. Whatever one might abandon, whatever one might cultivate, whatever one might fully know—through the yoga of the inexpressibility of all <s>dharmas</s>, one enters <s>tathatā</s>; that one understands <s>sarvajña-jñāna</s>.'

body.text: bhagavānāha / sādhu sādhu kulaputra subhāṣitaste 'yamekanayena
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Well said, well said, O son of good family! Well spoken is this attainment of <s>sarvajña-jñāna</s> by a single method.

body.text: sarvajñajñānapratilābhaḥ / tat kutaḥ sarvadharmā hyasamāropaḥ / anutpādāvināśakoṭīkaḥ avidyānirvāṇānutpādabhūtakoṭīkaḥ ākāśanirvāṇā[nutpādabhūta] koṭīkaḥ anabhilāpyakoṭīkaḥ sarvadharmāḥ / evaṃ sarvasattvāḥ / sarvadharmā na dravyakoṭīkaḥ sarvāsaṃgavastutaḥ parikīrtitaḥ / sarvatryadhvatraidhātukaskandhaniṣkiñcanakoṭīkaḥ trisaṃskāraśūnyatākoṭīkaḥ dharmaskandhavipākaskandhādayaḥ apacayaskandhā na dravyakoṭīkaḥ [parikīrtitaḥ] / śūnyatābhūtakoṭyanabhilāpyārthasarvadharmasamanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvajñajñānamavatarati /
body.translated_text: Why is that? Because all <s>dharmas</s> are without superimposition, having the limit of non-arising and non-destruction, having the limit of the true nature of non-arising of ignorance and <s>nirvāṇa</s>, having the limit of the true nature of non-arising of space and <s>nirvāṇa</s>, having the limit of inexpressibility—all <s>dharmas</s> are thus. So too are all beings. All <s>dharmas</s> do not have the limit of substance; they are proclaimed as being of the nature of complete non-attachment to all things. Having the limit of nothingness regarding the <s>skandhas</s> of the three realms across all three times, having the limit of the emptiness of the three <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned formations)—the <s>dharma</s>-aggregate, the fruition-aggregate, and the rest are aggregates of decay, not having the limit of substance, so it is proclaimed. A <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> endowed with all <s>dharmas</s> whose meaning is inexpressible, having the limit of emptiness and true nature, descends into <s>sarvajña-jñāna</s>.'

body.text: tasmin khalu punaḥ sarvajñajñānapratilābhavyākaraṇe bhāṣyamāṇe viṃśatibhirmārakanyāmāraputragaṇapārṣadyasahasrairanutpattikeṣu dharmeṣu kṣāntiḥ pratilabdhā / audārikaṃ ca kāyaṃ vijahya manomayaṃ kāyaṃ pratilebhire / apareṣāmapyeṣāṃ viṃśatīnāmanutpattikadharmakṣāntipratilābho
body.translated_text: When this explanation of the attainment of <s>sarvajña-jñāna</s> was being spoken, twenty thousand daughters of <s>Māra</s>, sons of <s>Māra</s>, and members of his retinue attained patience regarding the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti</s>). They abandoned their gross bodies and obtained mind-made bodies. And for these other twenty [thousand] as well, there was attainment of <s>anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti</s>

body.text: 'bhūt / dvinavatīnāṃ ca devamanuṣyabimbarāṇāṃ vicitravicitrāṇāṃ ca bodhisattvakṣāntidhyānadhāraṇīnāṃ pratilābho 'bhūt /
body.translated_text: and ninety-two kings of gods and humans attained various and diverse <s>bodhisattva</s> patiences, <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), and <s>dhāraṇīs</s> (mystic formulas).

body.text: atha tāni viṃśatisahasrāṇi anutpattikadharmakṣāntipratilabdhānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ bhagavantaṃ divyaiḥ puṣpairabhikiranti abhiprakiranti sma / bhagavataśca pādau śirobhirabhivandyaivamāhuḥ / paśya bhagavan kalyāṇamitrasaṃsargavaśena sattvānāṃ sarvapuṇyopāyakuśalamūlāni manasikārāṇi bhavanti / bhagavānāha / karmapratyaya eṣa draṣṭavyaḥ kautūhalaprāptānāṃ ca sattvānāṃ bhagavān saṃśayachittyarthamimaṃ pūrvayogamudājahāra /
body.translated_text: Then those twenty thousand <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> who had attained <s>anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti</s> showered and scattered divine flowers upon the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having bowed their heads at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, they spoke thus: 'Behold, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, through the power of association with a spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), beings develop mental formations of all meritorious skillful means and roots of virtue.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'This should be seen as the condition of <s>karma</s>.' And for those beings who had arrived at curiosity, the <s>Bhagavān</s> narrated this account of a former connection (<s>pūrvayoga</s>) in order to cut through their doubt.

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ kulaputrā atīte 'dhvani aparimāṇeṣu mahākalpeṣu atikrāntesu asyāmeva cāturdvīpikāyāṃ yadāsīt tena kālena tena samayena dyutindhare mahākalpe vartamāne aṣṭaṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāyuṣkāyāṃ prajāyāṃ tena ca kālena tena samayena jyotisomyagandhāvabhāsaśrīrnāma tathāgato 'bhūt vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān / kliṣṭe pañcakaṣāye loke vartamāne ca caturṇāṃ parṣadāṃ triyānapratisaṃyuktāṃ sandeśayati sma / tena khalu punaḥ samayena rājābhūt utpalavaktro nāma caturdvīpeśvaraścakravartī / atha rājā utpalavaktro 'pareṇa kālasamayena sāntaḥpuraparivāraḥ sabalakāyo yena
body.translated_text: 'O sons of good family, in the past, in immeasurable great <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) that have elapsed, in this very four-continent world, at a time when the great <s>kalpa</s> called <s>Dyutindhara</s> was current, when the lifespan of people was sixty-eight thousand years, at that time there was a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Jyotisomyagandhāvabhāsaśrī</s>, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, trainer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>. When the world was in a defiled state of the five corruptions, he taught the <s>dharma</s> connected with the three vehicles to the four assemblies. At that time there was a king named <s>Utpalavaktra</s>, a universal monarch ruling over the four continents. Then King <s>Utpalavaktra</s>, after some time, together with his inner palace retinue and his entire army, approached

body.text: jyotisomyagandhāvabhāsaśrīstathāgatastenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya tasya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya bhagavantaṃ nānapuṣpairabhyavākirat nānāgandhairnānādhūpaiśca pūjāṃ kṛtvā bhagavato bhikṣusaṃghasya pādau śirasābhivandyābhyāṃ gāthābhyām abhyaṣṭāvīt /
body.translated_text: the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Jyotisomyagandhāvabhāsaśrī</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, scattered various flowers upon the <s>Bhagavān</s>, made offerings of various fragrances and various incenses, bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s community of monks, and praised [him] with two verses:

children.translated_text: Praised exceedingly by <s>nāgas</s>, <s>amaras</s>, and others with [his] qualities, remover of abundant faults,

children.text: dhanasaptakena ca hito jagato vada kena sūkṣmamatimān bhavati // Rkp_2.1 //
children.translated_text: benefactor of the world with the seven treasures—tell me, how does one become possessed of subtle wisdom? //Rkp 2.1//
Destroyer of the darkness of the world, lamp-maker of peace, tamer of the falling away of birth, aging, arising, forest, and grief,

children.text: jagatastvapāyapathavārayatā vada kena mucyati ha mārapathā // Rkp_2.2 //
children.translated_text: For one who blocks the paths to the lower realms for the world—tell, by what means is one freed from <s>Māra</s>'s path? //<s>Rkp</s> 2.2//

body.text: atha khalu māraputrāḥ sa jyotisomyagandhavabhāsaśrīstathāgato rājānamutpalavaktrametadavocat / tribhiḥ satpuruṣadharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvaḥ sūkṣmamatirbhavati / katamaistribhiḥ / adhyāśayena sarvasattveṣu karuṇāyate / sarvasattvānāṃ duḥkhapraśamāya udyato bhavati
body.translated_text: Then, O sons of <s>Māra</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Jyotisomyagandhāvabhāsaśrī</s> said this to King <s>Utpalavaktra</s>: A <s>bodhisattva</s> endowed with three qualities of a good person becomes one of subtle wisdom. Which three? With deep aspiration, he has compassion for all beings. He exerts himself for the pacification of all beings' suffering,

body.text: mātṛvat / sarvadharmādīn nirjīvaniṣpoṣaniṣpudgalānānākaraṇa-samān vyupaparīkṣate / ebhistribhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgataḥ satpuruṣo bodhisattvaḥ sūkṣmamatirbhavati / aparaistribhiḥ mahārāja dharmaiḥ samanvāgataḥ satpuruṣo mārapāśeṣu na sajjate / katamaistribhiḥ / yaduta sarvasattveṣvakrodhano bhavati anavatāraprekṣī sarvasattvasamadakṣiṇīyaḥ samasaṃjñāmayo bhavati / sarvadharmānekanayena vyupaparīkṣate yaduta ākāśasamān niḥsaṃskārānanānātvānajātānanutpannānaniruddhān / sarvānākāśavad dravyalakṣaṇavigatānanupalambhayogena pratyavekṣate / ebhirmahārāja tribhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgataḥ puruṣo mārapāśeṣu na sajjate mārapathācca nirmucyate /
body.translated_text: like a mother. He examines all <s>dharmas</s> as beginningless, lifeless, without substance, without a person, and without differentiation—all equal. A good person, a <s>bodhisattva</s> endowed with these three qualities, becomes one of subtle wisdom. Furthermore, O great king, a good person endowed with three [other] qualities does not become ensnared in <s>Māra</s>'s bonds. Which three? Namely, he is free from anger toward all beings, does not look for faults, regards all beings equally as worthy of offerings, and has an equal perception of all. He examines all <s>dharmas</s> in a single way—namely, as equal to space, without conditioned formations, without differentiation, unborn, unarisen, and unceased. He contemplates all as devoid of material characteristics like space, through the method of non-apprehension. O great king, a person endowed with these three qualities does not become ensnared in <s>Māra</s>'s bonds and is freed from <s>Māra</s>'s path.

body.text: atha rājñaḥ utpalavaktrasyāgramahiṣī surasundarī nāma sā caturaśītibhiḥ strīsahasraiḥ parivṛtā puraskṛtā yena jyotisomyagandhāvabhāsaśrīstathāgatastenopajagāma / upetya taṃ bhagavantaṃ jyotisomyagandhāvabhāsaśriyaṃ tathāgataṃ nānāpuṣpairabhyavakīrya ābhirgāthābhiradhyabhāṣata /
body.translated_text: Then the chief queen of King <s>Utpalavaktra</s>, named <s>Surasundarī</s>, surrounded and attended by eighty-four thousand women, went to where the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Jyotisomyagandhāvabhāsaśrī</s> was. Having approached, she scattered various flowers upon the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Jyotisomyagandhāvabhāsaśrī</s>, and addressed him with these verses:

body.text:
asadṛguṇadhara vitimirakaraṇa cyutihara vada kathamihā yuvati /
bhavatiha puruṣo vyapagatakugati
body.translated_text: O bearer of incomparable virtues, remover of darkness, averter of falling—tell, how does a woman here

body.text: śriyu vinayamana drutahitakara // Rkp_2.3 //
body.translated_text: become a man free from bad destinies, endowed with glory, of disciplined mind, and a swift benefactor? //<s>Rkp</s> 2.3//

children.text: paramagatigata sugata praśamaratikara bhagavan tyajati yuvati tāṃ kathamiha puruṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: O <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), who has attained the supreme state, creator of the delight of peace, O <s>Bhagavān</s>—how does a man here abandon womanhood?

children.text: vada mama laghu suvinaya parahitakara śamayātitimirā mama nayagaganāt // Rkp_2.4 //
children.translated_text: Tell me quickly, O well-disciplined one, benefactor of others—dispel the great darkness from the sky of my understanding! //<s>Rkp</s> 2.4//

children.text: asamasama jagati śramaṇa parama prathita guṇagaṇa smṛtivinayadhara /
children.translated_text: O peerless equal in the world, supreme among ascetics, renowned, bearer of hosts of virtues, holder of mindfulness and discipline—

children.text: mama yadi puriṣeha bhavati hi dharatā laghu vada vitimira sugatapathāmṛtam // Rkp_2.5 //
children.translated_text: If here a woman can bear this, tell me quickly the stainless nectar of the <s>Sugata</s>'s path, O remover of darkness! //<s>Rkp</s> 2.5//

body.text: evamukte kulaputra sa jyotisomyagandhāvabhāsaśrīstathāgatastāṃ surasundarīmagramahiṣīmetadavocat / asti bhagini paryāyo yena mātṛgrāmo mātṛgrāmabhāvaṃ laghveva parivartayati pūrvākṣiptamātṛgrāmabhāvo laghvaśeṣaṃ kṣīyate na ca bhūyo mātṛgrāmeṣu upapattiṃ pratigṛṇhāti yāvadanuttaraparinirvāṇe hānyā [hyanatra sva]praṇidhānāt / tatra bhagini kataraḥ paryāyo yena paryāyeṇa mātṛgrāmo laghu puruṣo bhavati pūrvākṣiptaṃ ca mātṛgrāmabhāvaṃ laghvaśeṣaṃ kṣepayati / iha bhagini iyaṃ ratnaketurnāma dhāraṇī mahārthikī mahānuśaṃsā mahāprabhāvā sarvamātṛgrāmabhāvakṣayakarī kāyavāṅmanoduḥkhavipākadauṣṭhulyaṃ
body.translated_text: When this was said, O son of good family, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Jyotisomyagandhāvabhāsaśrī</s> said this to the chief queen <s>Surasundarī</s>: There is, O sister, a method by which a woman quickly transforms her female nature; the previously acquired female nature is quickly and completely exhausted, and she does not again accept rebirth among women, until unsurpassed <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation)—except by her own aspiration. What then, O sister, is that method by which a woman quickly becomes a man, and quickly and completely removes the previously acquired female nature? Here, O sister, this <s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Ratnaketu</s> (Jewel Banner) is of great meaning, of great benefit, of great power, and it eliminates all female nature. It completely removes the afflictive results of suffering of body, speech, and mind,

body.text: niravaśeṣaṃ kṣepayati / asyāśca ratnaketudhāraṇyāḥ samāśrayaṇena mātṛgrāmasya mātṛgrāmabhāvo niravaśeṣo gacchati / strīndriyamantardhāya puruṣendriyaṃ prādurbhavati / puruṣaścāpi rūpa[vān sarvāṅga]paripūrṇo bhavati ṛjuḥ sūkṣmajñānakuśalo bhavati kāyavāṅmanaḥsukṛtakarmāntaḥ sucaritacārī sarvaśaturnirjetā bhavati / yaścāsya dṛṣṭadharmasāṃparāyikaḥ kāya[vāṅma]noduḥkhapratisaṃvedanīyo duṣkṛtānāṃ vāṅmanaḥkarmaṇāṃ phalavipākaḥ sa parikṣayaṃ gacchati / sthāpyānantaryakāriṇaṃ saddharmapratikṣepakamāryāpavādakaṃ ca teṣāṃ punastenaiva bhāvena parikṣayaṃ gacchati [a]pariśeṣaḥ strībhāvaḥ / kāyavāṅmanodauṣṭhulyavaipākikaḥ sumerumātraḥ pārajanmikaḥ strībhāvenāpi nivartako duḥkhavipākapratisaṃvedanīyaḥ karmāvaraṇa-pāpaniṣyandaniravaśeṣaḥ parikṣayaṃ gacchati / tat kutaḥ / [tad] yathā nāma iyaṃ ratnaketudhāraṇī sarvairatītaistathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksambuddhairbhāṣitāścādhiṣṭhitā anyonyamanumoditāḥ stutā abhiṣṭutā varṇitāḥ sattvānāṃ duḥkhavipākakarmaparikṣayāya kuśalamūlabivṛddhitāyai / ebhiḥ kecidetarhi daśasu dikṣu pratyutpannāstathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāstiṣṭhanti yāpayanti svakasvakeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu / sarve te buddha bhagavanta imāṃ ratnaketudhāraṇīṃ bhāṣante yāvat praśaṃsanti sattvānāṃ karmaparikṣayāya kuśalamūlavivṛddhaye / ye 'pi te bhaviṣyanti anāgate 'dhvani daśasu dikṣu anyonyeṣu tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāste 'pīmāṃ ratnaketuṃ dhāraṇīṃ bhāṣiṣyanti
body.translated_text: without remainder. And by relying upon this <s>Ratnaketudhāraṇī</s>, the female nature of a woman disappears completely. The female faculties vanish and male faculties appear. And the man becomes handsome, complete in all limbs, upright, skilled in subtle knowledge, performing good deeds of body, speech, and mind, walking in good conduct, and overcoming all enemies. And whatever ripened fruit of evil deeds of body, speech, and mind that is to be experienced in this life and the next—that goes to complete exhaustion. Excepting those who have committed the five acts of immediate retribution, those who have rejected the true <s>Dharma</s>, and those who have slandered the noble ones—for those too, by this very means, the female nature goes to complete exhaustion without remainder. The karmic obstruction productive of suffering, vast as Mount <s>Sumeru</s>, pertaining to future lives, and even causing the reversion to female birth—the evil outflow of karmic obstruction goes to complete exhaustion without remainder. Why? Because this <s>Ratnaketudhāraṇī</s> has been spoken, empowered, mutually approved, praised, extolled, and commended by all past <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, for the exhaustion of beings' karmically produced suffering and for the increase of their roots of merit. And those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones who now exist in the ten directions and abide in their respective <s>Buddha</s>-fields—all those <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavāns</s> speak this <s>Ratnaketudhāraṇī</s>, and praise it for the exhaustion of beings' karma producing suffering and for the increase of their roots of merit. And those who in the future will be <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones in various [fields in] the ten directions—they too will speak this <s>Ratnaketu</s> <s>dhāraṇī</s>,

body.text: yāvat praśaṃsiṣyanti sattvānāṃ duḥkhavipākakarmaparikṣayāya kuśalamūlavivṛddhaye / te 'hamapyetarhi ratnaketuṃ dhāraṇīṃ bhāṣiṣyāmi / anumodiṣyanti ca daśasu dikṣu pratyutpannānaṃ tathāgatānāṃ bhāṣamāṇānāmahamimāṃ ratnaketudhāraṇīṃ varṇayiṣyāmi praśaṃsiṣyāmi / yaḥ kaścid bhagini rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣikto janapadasthāmaprāptaḥ imāṃ ratnaketuṃ dhāraṇīṃ pustake likhitvā dhārayiṣyanti tasya rājñaḥ kṣatriyasya daśasu dikṣū udāraḥ kīrtiśabdaśloko 'bhyudgamiṣyati / yāvat paraṃ rūpadhātumudāraiḥ kirtiśabdairāpūrayiṣyati / anekāni ca devanāgayakṣagandharvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi tasya kṣatriyasya pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddhā rakṣānuguptaye sthāsyanti / sarve ca tasya viṣaye kalikalahadurbhikṣarogaparacakravātavṛṣṭiśītoṣṇadoṣāḥ praśamaṃ yāsyanti / sarve ca duṣṭayakṣarākṣasasiṃhamahiṣagajavṛkā anapabādhino bhaviṣyanti / sarve viṣatiktakaṭukarūkṣavirasaparuṣa duḥkhasaṃsparśavedanīyā doṣāḥ praśamaṃ yāsyanti / sarvāṇi cāsya dhanadhānyauṣadhivanaspatayaḥ phalapuṣpāṇi prarohiṣyanti vivardhiṣyanti strigdhāni surasāni ca bhaviṣyanti / sa ced rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktaḥ saṃgrāme pratyupasthite imaṃ ratnaketuṃ dhāraṇīpustakaṃ dhvajāgrāvaropitaṃ kuryāt sa rājā kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktaḥ paracakraṃ parājeṣyati / sa cedubhayo rājñoḥ kṣatriyayormūrdhābhiṣiktayoḥ saṃgrāmābhirūḍhayoryayo ratnaketudhāraṇīpustakaṃ dhvajāgrāvaropitaṃ bhaviṣyati tau parasparaṃ prītisāmagrīṃ kariṣya[taḥ] /
body.translated_text: and will praise it for the exhaustion of beings' karmically produced suffering and for the increase of their roots of merit. I too shall now speak the <s>Ratnaketu</s> <s>dhāraṇī</s>. And I shall praise and commend this <s>Ratnaketudhāraṇī</s> while the <s>Tathāgatas</s> presently existing in the ten directions are speaking it. Whoever, O sister—whether a king, a <s>kṣatriya</s> (warrior), a consecrated sovereign, one who has attained the power of a province—shall write this <s>Ratnaketu</s> <s>dhāraṇī</s> in a book and preserve it, for that king, that <s>kṣatriya</s>, an exalted fame and renown shall arise in the ten directions, and it shall fill even the <s>rūpadhātu</s> (form realm) above with exalted fame and renown. And many billions and ten billions and hundreds of thousands of <s>devas</s> (gods), <s>nāgas</s> (serpents), <s>yakṣas</s> (nature spirits), and <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians) will follow behind that <s>kṣatriya</s> and stand guard for protection. And all strife, conflict, famine, disease, foreign invasion, storms, and faults of cold and heat in his domain shall be pacified. And all hostile <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons), lions, buffalo, elephants, and wolves shall become non-harmful. All faults of poisonous, bitter, pungent, harsh, tasteless, rough, and painfully felt contact shall be pacified. And all his wealth, grain, herbs, trees, fruits, and flowers shall sprout and flourish and shall become rich and flavorful. And if that king, that consecrated <s>kṣatriya</s>, when a battle has arisen, should place this <s>Ratnaketu</s> <s>dhāraṇī</s> book atop his banner, that king, that consecrated <s>kṣatriya</s>, shall defeat the enemy force. And if two kings, two consecrated <s>kṣatriyas</s>, having both entered battle, both have the <s>Ratnaketudhāraṇī</s> book placed atop their banners, those two shall make peace and harmony with each other.

body.text: ityevaṃ bahuguṇānvayā ratnaketudhāraṇī yatra kvacid grāme vā nagare vā nigame vā manuṣyāṇāṃ vāmanuṣyāṇāṃ vā catuṣpadānāṃ vyādhitānāmakālamaraṇaṃ viheṭhaṃ vā syāt tatrāyaṃ ratnaketudhāraṇīpustako mahāpūjopakaraṇaiḥ praveśayitavyaḥ / praveśya susnātena suviliptagātreṇa navacīvaraprāvṛtena brahmacāriṇā nānāpuṣpasamīrite nānāgandhapradhūpite nānārasaparivṛte siṃhāsane 'bhiruhya tatrāyaṃ ratnaketudhāraṇīpustako vācayitavyaḥ / sarve tatra vyādhayo 'kālamaraṇāni ca praśamaṃ yāsyati / sarvāṇi ca tatra bhayaromaharṣadurnimittāni antardhāsyanti / yaḥ kaścinmātṛgrāmaḥ putrārthī bhavet tena snātvā navacīvaraṃ prāvṛtya brahmacāriṇā puṣpagandhamālyavilepanairimaṃ pustakamarcayitvā svayaṃ nānāpuṣpasamīrite nānāgandhapradhūpite nānārasaparivṛte āsane 'bhiruhyeyaṃ ratnaketudhāraṇī vācayitavyā / putrapratilābhī bhaviṣyati / eṣaḥ [asya bhavati antimo] mātṛgrāmabhāvo yāvadanuttaraparinirvāṇādanyatra svapraṇidhānāt sattvaparipācanaheto /
body.translated_text: Thus, this <s>Ratnaketudhāraṇī</s>, which brings many benefits—wherever, in any village, city, or market town, there is untimely death or affliction of humans, non-humans, or quadrupeds who are ill, there this <s>Ratnaketudhāraṇī</s> book should be brought in with great worship and offerings. Having brought it in, one who has bathed well, anointed the body, put on fresh robes, is celibate, should ascend a lion-throne that is perfumed with various flowers, incensed with various fragrances, and surrounded by various essences, and there this <s>Ratnaketudhāraṇī</s> book should be recited. All diseases and untimely deaths there shall be pacified. And all fearful, hair-raising, and evil omens there shall vanish. Whatever woman desires a son, she should bathe, put on fresh robes, be celibate, worship this book with flowers, fragrances, garlands, and ointments, and then herself, ascending a seat perfumed with various flowers, incensed with various fragrances, and surrounded by various essences, should recite this <s>Ratnaketudhāraṇī</s>. She shall obtain a son. This will be her final female birth, until unsurpassed <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, except by her own aspiration for the purpose of ripening beings.

body.text: [tasmin kāle tathāgato jyotiprabhaśrīrimāṃ ratnaketudhāraṇīm udāharat / jaloke jaloke / moke jali / jala
body.translated_text: At that time the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Jyotiprabhaśrī</s> proclaimed this <s>Ratnaketudhāraṇī</s>: <s>jaloke jaloke / moke jali / jala</s>

body.text: jalimi / jalavrate jahile / vara-puruṣa-lakṣaṇasamāruhya / amame vamame vamame / navame mahāse / jahame jahame jahame jahame / varame varame / vavave / vavave / vahave / vaṃgave / vajave / vāra vāraśe / jamalekha / parakha / ala jahili / jana tule / jana tubhukhe / vahara vahara / siṃha vrate / nana tilā / nana tina dālā / sūryavihaga / candravihaga / cakṣu rajyati śavihaga / sarvakṣayastritvasuravihaga / jakhaga jakhaga / surakhagha vahama / amrikha / amrikha / amrikha / amrikha / amrikha / amrikha / amrikha amrikha / mrikha mrikha mrikha / vyavadeta karma / dune dune / upata vyavacched jñānakṛta / anuda padākhaga / neruka / aṅgule bhaṅgule vibhaṅgule / kulaha / indraparivibhaha / vyavaccheda karabha / vavrati / vavrati / ca prati / ca prati / amoha daraśane / parivarta bhaṣyu / khasama / krimajyotikhaga / jahi jahi jyoti / niṣka bhirasa / bhirasa / bhirasa / bhiraja / matikrama / bhivakriva / mahākriva / hile hihile / aruṇavate / samaniṣke / damadānadhyāna aparāmṛśe / phalakuṇḍalalekha / nivarta istribhāva / karmakṣaya [prādurbhava puruṣatvam / asamasama / samayavibhidadhi]jña tathāgata svāhā /
body.translated_text: <s>jalimi / jalavrate jahile / vara-puruṣa-lakṣaṇasamāruhya / amame vamame vamame / navame mahāse / jahame jahame jahame jahame / varame varame / vavave / vavave / vahave / vaṃgave / vajave / vāra vāraśe / jamalekha / parakha / ala jahili / jana tule / jana tubhukhe / vahara vahara / siṃha vrate / nana tilā / nana tina dālā / sūryavihaga / candravihaga / cakṣu rajyati śavihaga / sarvakṣayastritvasuravihaga / jakhaga jakhaga / surakhagha vahama / amṛkha / amṛkha / amṛkha / amṛkha / amṛkha / amṛkha / amṛkha amṛkha / mṛkha mṛkha mṛkha / vyavadeta karma / dune dune / upata vyavacched jñānakṛta / anuda padākhaga / neruka / aṅgule bhaṅgule vibhaṅgule / kulaha / indraparivibhaha / vyavaccheda karabha / vavrati / vavrati / ca prati / ca prati / amoha daraśane / parivarta bhaṣyu / khasama / kṛmajyotikhaga / jahi jahi jyoti / niṣka bhirasa / bhirasa / bhirasa / bhiraja / matikrama / bhivakriva / mahākriva / hile hihile / aruṇavate / samaniṣke / damadānadhyāna aparāmṛśe / phalakuṇḍalalekha / nivarta istrībhāva / karmakṣaya prādurbhava puruṣatvam / asamasama / samayavibhidadhijña tathāgata svāhā</s>

body.text: samanantarabhāṣitāyāṃ śākyamuninā tathāgatenāsyāṃ ratnaketudhāraṇyāṃ punarapi mahāpṛthivī kampi[tā / pañcaśatamārakanyānāṃ
body.translated_text: Immediately upon this <s>Ratnaketudhāraṇī</s> being spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the great earth trembled again. For five hundred daughters of <s>Māra</s>,

body.text: sahaśravane]na asyā ratnaketudharaṇyāḥ strīvyañjanamantardhāya puruṣavyañjanaṃ prādurabhavat / aprameyāsaṃkhyeyānāṃ devanāgayakṣaga[ndharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragarākṣasa]kumbhāṇḍa-kanyānāṃ sahasravaṇenāsyā ratnaketudhāraṇyāḥ strīvyañjanānyantardhāya puruṣavyañjanāni prādurbhūtāni / [tāsāṃ sarvāsāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau anivartanacittamabhūt] / sarvāsāṃ cānāgata-strībhāva-pratilābhasaṃvartanīyaṃ karmāvaramaśesamanirudvaṃ ca / tāḥ striyaḥ prāñjalaya[stathāgataṃ śākyamuniṃ mahāsvareṇa prārthayantya] āhuḥ / namo nama āścaryakārakāya śākyamunaye tathāgatāyārhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya / brūhi mahākṛpayā [vistareṇa kathamasmākaṃ] strībhāvamantarhitaṃ sarvākāraparipūrṇaṃ puruṣabhāvaṃ sambhūtam / tenāścaryaprātihāryasaṃvegena [vayamanuttarāyaṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittaṃ janayema / bhagavan brūhi] imaṃ pūrvayogaprameyāsaṃkhyeyadevamanuṣyāṇāmabhibhavāya /
body.translated_text: upon hearing this <s>Ratnaketudhāraṇī</s>, the female marks vanished and male marks appeared. For immeasurable and innumerable thousands of daughters of <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s> (titans), <s>garuḍas</s> (divine birds), <s>kinnaras</s> (celestial beings), <s>mahoragas</s> (great serpents), <s>rākṣasas</s>, and <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s> (gourd-demons), upon hearing this <s>Ratnaketudhāraṇī</s>, the female marks vanished and male marks appeared. In all of them arose the irreversible mind directed toward unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). And all their karmic obstruction leading to the future attainment of female birth was exhausted without remainder. Those women, with palms joined, in a great voice supplicated the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> and said: Homage, homage to <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, the worker of marvels! Speak with great compassion in detail: how has our female nature disappeared and the complete male nature arisen? By the wonder and astonishment of this miraculous display, may we generate the mind directed toward unsurpassed perfect awakening. O <s>Bhagavān</s>, speak of this former connection, for the overwhelming of immeasurable and innumerable <s>devas</s> and humans.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān śākyamunistathāgataḥ [pūrvayogamavocat / bhadramukhāmuṣmin kāle yasmin samaye] jyotisaumyagandhāvabhāsaśriyastathagatasyāntikād rājña utpalavaktrasyāgramahiṣyā
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, spoke of the former connection: O fair-faced ones, at that time, in the era when, in the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Jyotisomyagandhāvabhāsaśrī</s>, the chief queen of King <s>Utpalavaktra</s>—

body.text: surasundaryā devyā sārdhaṃ ca[turaśītistrīsāhasreṇa sā ratnaketudhāraṇī śrutā śravaṇamātreṇaiva] tasyāḥ surasundaryāḥ agramahiṣyāsteṣāṃ caturaśītināṃ strīsahasrāṇāṃ strīvyañjanānyantardhāya puruṣavyañjanāni [prādurbhūtāni / tathaivāsaṃkhyeyāprameyāṇāṃ] devakanyānāṃ yāvanmanuṣyāmanuṣyakanyānāṃ[śravaṇamātreṇaiva] asyā ratnaketudhāraṇyāḥ strīndriyamantarhitaṃ pu[ruṣendriyaṃ prādurbhūtam / sarvāsāṃ tāsāṃ strī] sahasrāṇāmanāgata-strībhāva-pratilābha-saṃvartanīyaṃ karmāvaraṇamaśeṣaṃ saṃniruddham / yadā ca rājñaḥ utpalavaktrasyāgramahiṣyāḥ [surasundaryāḥ sapāriṣadyāyaḥ puruṣatvaṃ saṃjātaṃ] tadā sa rājā utpalavaktraścāturdvīpeśvaraścakravartī jyeṣṭhakumāraṃ rājyābhiṣekeṇābhiṣicya sārdhamekonena putrasahasreṇa [sārdhaṃ surasundareṇa] sārdhaṃ caturaśītibhiḥ surasundaramahāpuruṣasahasraiḥ sārdhamaparirdvinavatibhiḥ prāṇasahasrairabhiniṣkramya tasya jyotisomyagandhāvabhāsaśriyastathāgatasyāntike keśaśmaśrūṇyavatārya kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇi paridhāya samyagevāgārādanāgārikāṃ pravrajitaḥ / pravrajitvā svādhyāyabhirato yoniśaṃ manasikārābhiyukto 'bhūt /
body.translated_text: Together with Queen <s>Surasundarī</s> and eighty-four thousand women, that <s>Ratnaketudhāraṇī</s> was heard. Merely by hearing it, the female characteristics of <s>Surasundarī</s> the chief queen and those eighty-four thousand women disappeared and male characteristics appeared. Likewise, for innumerable and immeasurable divine maidens, and even for human and non-human maidens, merely by hearing this <s>Ratnaketudhāraṇī</s>, their female faculties disappeared and male faculties appeared. For all those thousands of women, the karmic obstruction (<s>karmāvaraṇa</s>) that would have resulted in future attainment of female birth was entirely extinguished. When the chief queen <s>Surasundarī</s> together with her attendants attained manhood, King <s>Utpalavaktra</s>, the <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) ruling over the four continents, consecrated his eldest prince with the royal consecration, and together with ninety-nine thousand sons, together with <s>Surasundara</s>, together with eighty-four thousand great men [formerly women] of <s>Surasundara</s>, and together with ninety-two thousand other beings, went forth. Having cut off his hair and beard in the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Jyotisomyagandhāvabhāsaśrī</s>, donning the saffron robes, he went forth from the household life to homelessness in the proper way. Having gone forth, he became devoted to study and was diligently engaged in proper mental attention (<s>yoniśo manasikāra</s>).

body.text: atha tatra bahūnāṃ prāṇakoṭīnāmetadabhavat / kasmād rājā cakravartī pravrajitaḥ / te parasparamevamāhuḥ / mārakarmābhiyukta eṣa tathāgataḥ śaṭho māyāvī mārakarmasamāyuktama imaṃ
body.translated_text: Then it occurred to many <s>koṭis</s> of beings there: 'Why has the <s>cakravartin</s> king gone forth?' They said to one another: 'This <s>Tathāgata</s> is engaged in <s>Māra</s>'s work! He is a cheat, a deceiver, endowed with <s>Māra</s>'s work! He teaches this

body.text: dharmaṃ deśayati / keṣāṃcit strīvyañjanamupanāmayati / keṣāṃcit puruṣavyañjanam / keṣāñcit keśaśmaśrūṇyavatārayati / keṣāñcid raktāni vāsāṃsi prayacchati keṣāñcit pāṇḍurāṇi / keṣāṃcid devopapattaye dharmaṃ deśayati / keṣāñcinmanuṣyopapattaye keṣāñcittiryagyonyupapattaye keṣāñcid cyutyupapattaye dharmaṃ deśayati / mārakarmapathābhiyuktaḥ strīkaraṇamāyayā samanvāgataḥ sa śramaṇo jyotisomyagandhāvabhāsaśrīḥ śramaṇarūpeṇa visaṃvādakaḥ yannūnaṃ vayamitaḥ prakramena na cāsya rūpaliṅgagrahaṇaṃ paśyema na cāsya kiñcid vacanaṃ śṛṇuyāma /
body.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s>. To some he gives female characteristics, to some male characteristics. He shaves the heads of some. To some he gives red garments, to some white ones. To some he teaches <s>Dharma</s> for rebirth among gods, to some for rebirth among humans, to some for rebirth in animal wombs, to some he teaches <s>Dharma</s> for death and rebirth. He is devoted to the path of <s>Māra</s>'s work, endowed with the sorcery of making women—that ascetic <s>Jyotisomyagandhāvabhāsaśrī</s> is a deceiver in the guise of an ascetic! Let us depart from here and neither see the appearance and marks of this one nor hear any word of his!'

body.text: atha tatraiva kumārabhṛto nāma bhaṭaḥ / sa evamāha / yā mama bhāryā antaḥpurikā duhitaraścābhūvan sarvāsāmanena śramaṇakoraṇḍakena strīvyañjanānyapanīya puruṣendriyāṇyabhinirmitāni / sarvāsāṃ śirāṃsi nirmuṇḍāni kṛtvā raktāni vāsāṃsi anupradattāni / ahaṃ caikākī śokārto bhūtaḥ / ete sarve vayaṃ samagrā bhūtvā viṣamaṃ mahāgahanaparvataṃ praviśāmaḥ / yatra vayamasya mārapāśābhiyuktasya śramaṇakoraṇḍakasya śramaṇamāyāvinaḥ svaraghoṣamapi
body.translated_text: Now there was a soldier named <s>Kumārabhṛta</s>. He spoke thus: 'My wife, my harem women, and my daughters—all of them have had their female characteristics removed and male organs created by this false ascetic (<s>śramaṇakoraṇḍaka</s>). All their heads have been shaved and red garments given to them. And I alone am left, stricken with grief. Let us all gather together and enter the rough, great wilderness mountain, where we shall not even hear the voice of this ascetic (<s>śramaṇakoraṇḍaka</s>) who is caught in <s>Māra</s>'s snare, this sorcerer-ascetic,

body.text: na śṛṇuyāma prāgeva paśyāma iti / te sarve tuṣṭā evamāhuḥ / evamastviti /
body.translated_text: much less see him!' They were all pleased and said: 'So be it!'

body.text: atha kumārabhṛto bhaṭastairvicikitsāprāptairbahubhiḥ prāṇakoṭībhiḥ sārdhaṃ prākrāmat pratyantime janapade viṣamaparvatagahane sva-ṛṣiveṣeṇa caryāṃ cacāra / tebhyaśca sattvebhyaḥ evaṃ dharmaṃ deśayāmāsa / nāsti saṃsārānmīkṣo nāsti sukṛtaduṣkṛtānāṃ karmaṇāṃ phalavipākaḥ / ucchedavādī [ayaṃ] śramaṇaḥ utpanno mārakarmābhiyukto visaṃvādakaḥ / ye ca taṃ darśanāyopasaṃkramanti ye ca tamabhivādayanti ye cāsya dharmaṃ śṛṇvanti te vikṣiptacittā bhavanti / śirāṃsi caiṣāṃ muṇḍayati / gṛhānnirvāsayati / raktāni vāsāṃsi prayacchati / śmaśānacaryāṃ cārayati / bhaikṣyacaryāsu niveśayati / ekāhāriṇaḥ karoti / viṣamadṛṣṭimanaso 'nityodvignān vivekavāsābhiratānlayanaprakṣiptān kāmaratinṛtyagītagandhamālyavilepanābharaṇavibhūṣaṇa-maithunadharma-surāmadyapāna-rahitānalpa-bhāṣiṇaḥ karoti / evaṃrūpaḥ sa śramaṇaveṣeṇocchedavādī mārapathābhiyuktaḥ sattvānāṃ śatrubhūta utpannaḥ adṛṣṭaśrutapūrvametasya śramaṇagautamasya kriyopalakṣita iti / tena bahūni prāṇakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇyevaṃrūpāmimāṃ pāpikāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ grāhitānyabhūvan /
body.translated_text: Then the soldier <s>Kumārabhṛta</s>, together with those many <s>koṭis</s> of beings who had fallen into doubt, departed to a frontier region, to a rough mountain wilderness, and conducted himself in the manner of a self-proclaimed sage. And to those beings he taught <s>Dharma</s> thus: 'There is no liberation from <s>saṃsāra</s>. There is no ripening of the fruits of good and bad <s>karmas</s>.' This nihilist (<s>ucchedavādī</s>) ascetic has arisen, devoted to <s>Māra</s>'s work, a deceiver. Those who approach him for audience, those who salute him, and those who listen to his <s>Dharma</s>—they become distracted in mind. He shaves their heads, drives them from their homes, gives them red garments, makes them wander in charnel grounds, establishes them in begging rounds, makes them eat once a day, makes them of wrong views, agitated by impermanence, delighting in solitude, given to torpor, bereft of desire for pleasures, dancing, singing, garlands, perfumes, ornaments, adornments, sexual enjoyment, and liquor and intoxicating drink—makes them of few words. Such is this nihilist in ascetic's guise, devoted to <s>Māra</s>'s path, arisen as an enemy of beings—unprecedented and unheard of is this practice attributed to the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>!' By him, many <s>koṭis</s>, <s>nayutas</s>, hundreds of thousands of beings were made to adopt this evil wrong view.

body.text: yo vāpareṇa samayena utpalavaktro mahāśramaṇo 'śrauṣīt kasmiṃścit parvatagahane kecit svayaṃ kumārgasaṃprasthitāḥ parānapyetāṃ viṣamāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ grāhayantaḥ trayāṇāṃ ratnānāmavarṇaṃ cārayantīti śrutvā cāsyaitadabhavat / yāvadahaṃ tāvat sattvāṃstataḥ pāpakāt dṛṣṭigatānna parimokṣayeyaṃ na ca samyagdṛṣṭau pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ nirarthakaṃ me śrāmaṇyaṃ bhavet / kathaṃ cāham anāgatādhvani andhabhūte loke anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam / kathaṃ ca vyasanagatāṃścaturmārapāśabandhanabaddhān sattvān śakṣyāmi parimocayitumiti /
body.translated_text: At another time, the great ascetic <s>Utpalavaktra</s> heard that in a certain mountain wilderness, some had set out on wrong paths of their own accord and were causing others also to adopt this wrong view, speaking ill of the Three Jewels. Having heard this, it occurred to him: 'So long as I do not liberate those beings from that evil wrong view and establish them in right view, my asceticism (<s>śrāmaṇya</s>) would be fruitless. And how would I, in the future, when the world has become blind, attain supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>)? And how would I be able to liberate beings who have fallen into calamity, bound by the bonds of the four <s>Māras</s>?'

body.text: athotpalavaktro mahāśramaṇo mahādṛḍhaparākramaḥ kāruṇikastaṃ jyotisomyagandhavabhāsaśriyaṃ tathāgatamavalokyānekaprāṇi-śata-sahasraparivṛtaḥ puraskṛtasteṣu teṣu pratyantimeṣu grāmanagaranigamaparvataviṣamakarvaṭasthāneṣu caryāṃ caran tatra vā atra tebhyaḥ sattvebhyo dharmaṃ deśayāmāsa / tān sattvān pāpakān dṛṣṭigatān nivārayitvā samyagdṛṣṭau niyojyānuttarāyaṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pratiṣṭhāpayāmāsa / kāṃścidaparān pratyekabuddhayānapraṇidhāne kāṃścit śrāvakayāne kāṃścit phale pratiṣṭhāpayāmāsa / kāṃścit pravrajayāmāsa / kāṃścidupāsakasaṃvare kāṃścidupavāse kāṃścit triśaraṇagamane pratiṣṭhāpayāmāsa / strībhyaśca imāṃ ratnaketudhāraṇīṃ deśayāmāsa / strībhāvānnivartayitvā pratiṣṭhāpayāmāsa puruṣatve / yāśca tāvat hyaśrāmaṇyastathāgatasyāntike vicikitsāprāptā abhūvaṃstāḥ sarvastataḥ pāpakadṛṣṭigatāt nivāryātyayaṃ pratideśāpayitvānuttarāyāṃ
body.translated_text: Then the great ascetic <s>Utpalavaktra</s>, of great firmness and valor, compassionate, looking to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Jyotisomyagandhāvabhāsaśrī</s>, surrounded and attended by many hundreds of thousands of beings, wandered in those various frontier villages, towns, market-towns, mountain wildernesses, and hamlets, teaching <s>Dharma</s> to those beings here and there. Having turned those beings away from their evil wrong views, having engaged them in right view, he established them in supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). Some others he established in the aspiration for the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle, some in the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle, and some in the [respective] fruits. Some he ordained as renunciants. Some he established in the lay precepts (<s>upāsakasaṃvara</s>), some in the observance of fast days (<s>upavāsa</s>), and some in taking the Three Refuges. To the women he taught this <s>Ratnaketudhāraṇī</s>, turning them away from womanhood and establishing them in manhood. And all those women who had fallen into doubt regarding the <s>Tathāgata</s> due to lack of faith in the monastic life—all of them he turned away from that evil wrong view, made them confess their transgressions, and established them in supreme perfect

body.text: samyaksaṃbodhau pratiṣṭhāpayāmāsa / tasyaiva ca jyotisomyagandhāvabhāsaśriyastathāgatasyāntikamupanīya pravrajayāmāsa sthāpya kumārabhṛtaṃ bhaṭam / tena caivaṃ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtamabhūt / yathā mamānenotpalavaktreṇa śramaṇena parṣadaṃ vilopya nītā tathā 'hamapyasyānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhiprasthitasya tatra buddhakṣetre māratvaṃ kārayeya yaduta garbhasthānāt prabhṛti enaṃ viheṭhayeyam / tataḥ paścājjātamātraṃ kumārakrīḍāparaṃ śilpakarmapaṭhanasthaṃ ratikrīḍāntaḥpuragataṃ yāvad bodhimaṇḍasaṃniṣaṇṇaṃ saṃtrāsayeyam / vighnāni ca kuryām / bodhiprāptasya ca śāsanavipralopaṃ kuryām /
body.translated_text: awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). He brought them into the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Jyotisomyagandhāvabhāsaśrī</s> himself and ordained them—except for the soldier <s>Kumārabhṛta</s>. And that one [<s>Kumārabhṛta</s>] had made this aspiration: 'Just as this ascetic <s>Utpalavaktra</s> has stolen away my assembly and led them off, so too may I create obstruction as <s>Māra</s> in the <s>Buddha</s>-field of this one who has set out for supreme perfect awakening—namely, I would torment him from the time he is in the womb. Then, after his birth, during his childhood play, his study of arts and crafts, his enjoyment in the inner chambers, and up until he is seated at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, I would terrify him and create obstacles. And after he attains awakening, I would corrupt his teaching.'

body.text: atha sa utpalavaktro mahāśramaṇastaṃ kumārabhṛtaṃ bhaṭamevaṃ praṇidhikṛtāvasāyaṃ mahatā kṛcchodyogaparākramaiḥ prasādayitvā tataḥ pāpakadṛṣṭigatāt pratinivartyātyayaṃ pratideśāpayitvānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayati sma /
body.translated_text: Then the great ascetic <s>Utpalavaktra</s>, with great difficulty, effort, and valor, persuaded that soldier <s>Kumārabhṛta</s>, who had made such a determined aspiration, turned him away from that evil wrong view, made him confess his transgression, and caused him to generate the mind of supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhicitta</s>).

body.text: atha kumārabhṛtabhaṭo vinītaprasādaḥ idaṃ praṇidhānaṃ cakāra / yadā tvaṃ mahākāruṇika anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddho bhavestadā bodhiprāpto māṃ vyākuryā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau /
body.translated_text: Then the soldier <s>Kumārabhṛta</s>, having been tamed and gladdened, made this aspiration: 'When you, O Greatly Compassionate One, have attained supreme perfect awakening, then, having attained awakening, please give me a prediction (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>) for supreme perfect awakening.'

body.text: syāt khalu punarbhadramukhā yuṣmākaṃ kāṃkṣā vā vimatirvānyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayenāsīdutpalavaktro nāma yena tasya jyotisomyagandhāvabhāsaśriyastathāgatasya saparivārasyānekavidhaṃ pūjopasthānaṃ kṛtamanekaiśca prāṇakoṭīnayutaśatasahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ niṣkramya pravrajitaḥ apramāṇāni ca prāṇakoṭīnayutaśasahasrāṇi
body.translated_text: Now then, O fair-faced ones, you may have doubt or uncertainty about this. He who at that time, at that occasion, was the one named King <s>Utpalavaktra</s>, who performed manifold worship and service to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Jyotisomyagandhāvabhāsaśrī</s> and his retinue, and who went forth together with many <s>koṭis</s>, <s>nayutas</s>, hundreds of thousands of beings, and immeasurable <s>koṭis</s>, <s>nayutas</s>, hundreds of thousands of beings

body.text: tataḥ [pāpakadṛṣṭi]gatānnivārayitvā triṣu yāneṣu niveśitāni / aprameyaḥ sattvaḥ phalaṣu pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ / apramāṇaśca strīkoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ puruṣapratilābhaḥ kṛta iti / na khalu yuṣmābhirevaṃ draṣṭavyam / ahaṃ sa tena kālena tena samayena rājābhūt cāturdvīpeśvaraścakravartī utpalavaktro nāma / mayā sa evaṃrūpaḥ manasikāraḥ kṛtaḥ / yat khalu punaryuṣmākaṃ bhadramukhāḥ kāṅkṣā [vā] vimatirvā anyā sā tena kālena tena samayenābhūt surasundarī nāmāgramahiṣī yayā śrāmaṇyamavāptam / maitreyaḥ sa bodhisattvo mahāsattvastena kālena tena samayenābhūt / syāt khalu bhadramukhāḥ yuṣmākaṃ kāṅkṣā vā vimatirvānyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena kumārabhṛto nāma bhaṭo 'bhūt sārdhaṃ prāṇakoṭībhiḥ / na khalu punaryuṣmābhirevaṃ draṣṭavyam / ayaṃ sa māraḥ pāpīmāṃstena kālena tena samayena kumārabhṛto nāma bhaṭo 'bhūt / yanmayā tatkālaṃ [tasya pārṣadaḥ] pravrājitaḥ tena mayi pradoṣamutpādyaivaṃ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam / yadā tvamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ syāstadā tvaṃ māṃ vyākuryā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / tasyaiva yū[yaṃ kula]putrā jyotisomyagandhāvabhāsaśriyastathāgatasyāntike[']prasādaṃ kṛtvāsaṃvṛtavāgbhāṣitaṃ pāpakaṃ dṛṣṭigataṃ parigṛhya mayaiva yūyaṃ tataḥ pāpadṛṣṭigatāt parimocya pravrājitāḥ / tataḥ anu[pū]rveṇa
body.translated_text: were turned away from that evil wrong view and established in the three vehicles. Immeasurable beings were established in the [respective] fruits. And for immeasurable <s>koṭis</s>, <s>nayutas</s>, hundreds of thousands of women, the attainment of manhood was accomplished—you should not view this otherwise. I myself was at that time, at that occasion, the king, the <s>cakravartin</s> ruling over four continents, named <s>Utpalavaktra</s>. I myself performed that mental attention. Now then, O fair-faced ones, whatever doubt or uncertainty you may have—she who at that time was the chief queen named <s>Surasundarī</s>, who attained the monastic life—that was the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> at that time. And, O fair-faced ones, whatever doubt or uncertainty you may have—he who at that time was the soldier named <s>Kumārabhṛta</s> together with <s>koṭis</s> of beings—you should not view it thus [as someone else]. This <s>Māra</s> <s>Pāpīmān</s> was at that time the soldier named <s>Kumārabhṛta</s>. Because I at that time ordained his assembly, he generated malice toward me and made this aspiration: 'When you attain supreme perfect awakening, then grant me a prediction for supreme perfect awakening.' It was you, O sons of good family, who at that time, before that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Jyotisomyagandhāvabhāsaśrī</s>, generated faithlessness, uttered unrestrained speech, and adopted that evil wrong view. And it was I who liberated you from that evil wrong view and ordained you. Then, in due course,

body.text: yuṣmābhirbahūni buddhasahasrāṇi paryupāsitāni / teṣāṃ ca pūjopasthānaṃ kṛtam / tebhyaśca dharmaṃ śrutvā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam / ṣaṭsu pāramitāsu [caryā kṛtā] iti / tena yūyaṃ kāyavāṅmanoduścarikarmaṇā pūrvaṃ triṣvapāyeṣu anekakalpaduḥkhānyanubhūtavantaḥ / tenaiva karmāvaraṇena etarhi mārasya pāpīmato bhavane upapanna iti / asmin khalu punā ratnaketudhāraṇī-pūrvayoge bhāṣyamāṇe bhagavatā śākyamuninā tathāgatena teṣāṃ pañcānāṃ mārakanyāśatānāṃ strībhāvamantardhāya puruṣabhāvaḥ saṃvṛtto 'nupattikadharmakṣāntipratilambhaścābhūt / apramāṇānām asaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ sadevamānuṣāyāḥ prajāyāśca anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpannāni / [te] avaivartyāścābhūvan anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / evamaprameyāsaṃkhyeyāni sattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi śrāvakapratyekabuddhayāne [']vaivartyāni abhūvan / aprameyāsaṃkhyeyānāṃ devamānuṣakanyānāṃ mātṛgrāmabhāvo 'bhinivṛttaḥ puruṣabhāvāśrayapratilabhaścābhūt /
body.translated_text: you attended many thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>, performed worship and service to them, heard <s>Dharma</s> from them, made aspirations, and practiced the six <s>Pāramitās</s> (perfections). Yet due to your previous misconduct of body, speech, and mind, you experienced suffering for many <s>kalpas</s> in the three lower realms. And it is due to that very karmic obstruction (<s>karmāvaraṇa</s>) that you have now been reborn in the abode of <s>Māra</s> <s>Pāpīmān</s>. Now, when this <s>Ratnaketudhāraṇī</s>-<s>pūrvayoga</s> (previous connection) was being spoken by the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, the female nature of those five hundred <s>Māra</s>-maidens disappeared and male nature arose, and they attained the acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas (<s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>). For immeasurable, incalculable <s>koṭis</s>, <s>nayutas</s>, hundreds of thousands of beings, including the assembly of gods and humans, minds were generated toward supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). They became irreversible (<s>avaivartya</s>) in supreme perfect awakening. Likewise, immeasurable, incalculable <s>koṭis</s>, <s>nayutas</s>, hundreds of thousands of beings became irreversible in the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicles. For immeasurable, incalculable divine and human maidens, the state of womanhood was reversed and the support of manhood was attained.

body.text: mahāyānasūtrādratnaketu-pūrvayogaparivarto nāma dvitīyaḥ // 2 //
body.translated_text: End of the second chapter, called "The Previous Connection of <s>Ratnaketu</s>," from the <s>Mahāyāna</s> sūtra. //2//

body.text: START Rkp 3
body.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Ratnaketudhāraṇī</s> Chapter 3

body.text: tṛtīyaḥ parivartaḥ
body.translated_text: Third Chapter

body.text: atha khalu asyāṃ ratnaketudhāraṇyāṃ bhāṣyamāṇāyāṃ śākyamuninā tathāgatenārhatā sarvāvatīyaṃ sahālokadhāturudāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭābhūt / ye ceha buddhakṣetre koṭīśataṃ cāturdvīpikānāṃ teṣu koṭīśataṃ kāmeśvarāṇāṃ māratvaṃ kārayanti te buddhānubhāvena saṃvignā imāṃ cāturdvīpikāṃ vyavalokayanti sma / kuto 'yamavabhāsaḥ utpannaḥ / nūnaṃ pāpīmān nāma māro yastatra cāturdvīpikāyāṃ prativasati tasyaiṣa prabhāvaḥ yo 'smatto balavantaḥ īśvarataro mahaujaskaśca / atha khalu te mārā vyavalokayanto 'drākṣuḥ taṃ māraṃ pāpīmantaṃ koṣāgāre niṣaṇṇaṃ paramadurmanastham / atha tat koṭīśataṃ mārāṇāṃ yeneyaṃ cāturdvīpikā yena mārasya pāpīmato bhavanaṃ tenopajagāma / upetya māraṃ pāpīmantamevamāha / kiṃ bhoḥ kāmeśvara ! sarvāvatīyaṃ lokadhāturavabhāsitā tvaṃ ca śokāgāraṃ praviśya niṣaṇṇaḥ / atha kāmeśvaro māraḥ teṣāṃ mārakoṭīśatānāṃ vistareṇārocayati sma / yat khalu mārṣāḥ jānīyu[ri]haikaḥ śramaṇa utpannaḥ śākyavaṃśāt paramaśaṭho māyāvī / tenotpannamātreṇa sarvāvatīyamiha lokadhāturavabhāsitā prakampitā kṣobhitā / ye kecidiha kṛtsnalokadhātau vidvāṃso mahendrā vā nāgendrā vā yakṣendrā vā surendrā vā mahoragendrā vā garuḍendrā vā
body.translated_text: Now, while this <s>Ratnaketudhāraṇī</s> was being spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the entire <s>Sahā</s> world-system was illuminated with a magnificent radiance. And in this buddha-field, in a hundred <s>koṭis</s> of four-continent world-systems, those hundred <s>koṭis</s> of lords of desire who hold the office of <s>Māra</s>, stirred by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, gazed upon this four-continent [world].

body.text: kinnarendrā vā yāvadanye 'pi kecinma[nu]ṣyā vidvāṃsaste sarve tamupāgatāḥ pūjākarmaṇe yāvat ṣaḍvarṣāṇi ekākyadvitīyaṃ niṣadyā lakṣaṇāṃ māyāṃ sādhitavān / ahamapi svabaladarśanaṃ cikīrṣuḥ evaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśatkoṭīsainyaparivāraḥ upasaṃkramya samantato 'nuparivārya sarvamārabalavikurvaṇa-ṛddhibalaparākramaṃ saṃdarśita[vān / paśyaikaṃ romakū]pamapyaham aśakto 'smi saṃtrāsayituṃ vā bhīṣayituṃ vā kimaṅga punastasmādāsanāt kampayituṃ kiṃvā punaranyaṃ vighātaṃ kartumiti / atha caitena vṛṣalena tādṛśī māyā pradarśitā [prakaṃ]paśca kṛtaḥ yat sasainyo 'haṃ parājitaśchinnavṛkṣa iva dharaṇītale nipatitaḥ / tena ca tatraiva niṣaṇṇena tādṛśī alakṣaṇā māyā sā[dhitā yayāsau sarvamāraviṣaya]mevā[bhi]bhūtaṃ sādhitavidyāṃ tasmādutthāya sattvebhyaḥ saṃprakāśayāmāsa / ye ca kecidiha cāturdvīpikāyāṃ lokadhātau paṇḍitā vijñāstathā mā[yāyāṃ chandakṛtasteṣāṃ cittaṃ] prajānāmi gatyupapattiṃ vā ṣaṭsu gatiṣu / ye ca taccharaṇagatāsteṣām ekaromakūpamapi na śaknomi saṃtrāsayituṃ vā saṃkṣobhayituṃ
body.translated_text: ...or <s>Kinnara</s> lords, or whatever other learned humans—they all had come for the purpose of worship. For six years, sitting alone, in solitude, he had accomplished the practice of the illusory signs. I too, wishing to display my own power, approached with an army retinue of thirty-six <s>koṭis</s>, surrounded him on all sides, and [deployed] all the supernatural power, might, and prowess of <s>Māra</s>'s forces—

body.text: vā [kampayituṃ vā] loke punastasmād visaṃvādayituṃ vā kampayituṃ vā śaknuyām / adyaiva ca me pañca paricārikāśatāni viṃśatiśca putrasahasrāṇi sagaṇaparṣadyāni vṛṣalaṃ gautamaṃ [śra]maṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāstasya purato niṣaṇṇāḥ / na cāhaṃ bhūyastāni śaktastasmād vivecayitum / tena hi yūyaṃ balavantaḥ puṇyavanto jñānavantaḥ aiśvaryavantaḥ [suhṛdo bha]vata / taṃ śākyaputraṃ vṛṣalaṃ jīvitād vyaparopayiṣyāmaḥ / ye ca sattvāstaccharaṇagatāstān sarvān vidhvaṃsayiṣyāmaḥ / kṛṣṇaṃ māyāśāṭhyaṃ śramaṇapakṣaṃ parājeṣyāmaḥ / [śuklaṃ mārapa]kṣam uddyotayiṣyāmaḥ / tataḥ paścāt sukhasparśaṃ vihariṣyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: —or to shake [him], or to deceive him again, or to cause him to waver—I was unable. And today, five hundred of my attendant-maidens and twenty thousand of my sons with their retinue have gone for refuge to that low-born ascetic <s>Gautama</s> and sit before him. I am no longer able to separate them from him. Therefore you, who are powerful—

body.text: atha jyotiṣprabho māraḥ imaṃ jambudvīpaṃ vyavalokayāmāsa yatra tathāgataḥ [saṃniṣaṇṇo] dharmaṃ deśayati / atha jyotiṣprabho māro bhagavataḥ kāyamadrākṣīt svaraghoṣayukta[stasya dharmade]śanāmaśrauṣīt / atha tāvadeva tasya roma[harṣaṇaḥ] saṃtrā[saḥ] utpannaḥ / atha sa māraṃ pāpīmantamevamāha /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Māra</s> named <s>Jyotiṣprabha</s> surveyed this <s>Jambudvīpa</s> where the <s>Tathāgata</s> sat teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. Then <s>Māra</s> <s>Jyotiṣprabha</s> beheld the body of the Blessed One and, with its melodious voice, heard his teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>. Immediately, a hair-raising terror arose in him. Then he said to <s>Māra</s> <s>Pāpīmān</s>:

children.translated_text: "In this entire field, he is the most distinguished, of supreme form,
endowed with merit and wisdom, of long-enduring [presence], and pure.
Long freed from the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), well-established on the path—
all who are his [followers] are freed from the destruction of existence and from grief." //3.1//
"Do not again fall under the sway of anger, which is connected with wrongdoing.
For he is the foremost, the best, the refuge in this triple existence.
Whoever does not perceive even a trace of hatred toward him—
that [person], deluded, comes to the destruction of happiness here." //3.2//

body.text: athāparo māraḥ sannimiko nāma taṃ māraṃ pāpīmantamevamāha /
body.translated_text: Then another <s>Māra</s> named <s>Sannimi</s> spoke thus to <s>Māra</s> <s>Pāpīmān</s>:

children.translated_text: "He is of great supernatural power, marked by supreme merit, unattached, freed from all destinies.
The teacher of the path to the complete cessation of suffering—he cannot be harmed by hundreds of <s>Māras</s>." //3.3//

body.text: pāpīmānāha /
body.translated_text: <s>Pāpīmān</s> replied:

children.text: vaśaṃ madīyāṃ janatāṃ kṛtāhi yuṣmajjanastasya vaśānugo 'yam /
children.translated_text: "He has brought my people under his control; your people too follow his command.

children.text: na cirāt sa śūnyaṃ viṣayaṃ kariṣyati asmadgatiḥ kutra punarbhaviṣyati // Rkp_3.4 //
children.translated_text: Before long he will make [my] domain empty—where then will our destiny be?" //3.4//

body.text: atha vanarājo nāma māraḥ sa māraṃ pāpīmantamevamāha /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Māra</s> named <s>Vanarāja</s> spoke thus to <s>Māra</s> <s>Pāpīmān</s>:

children.text: yadā tavāsīt parama samṛddhistadā tvayā darśitamātmasauryam /
children.translated_text: "When you possessed supreme prosperity, then you displayed your own heroism.

children.text: balapranaṣṭo 'syadhunā nirāśaḥ kiṃ spardhase sarvavidā sahādya // Rkp_3.5 //
children.translated_text: Now, with your power destroyed, hopeless—why do you contend today with the Omniscient One?" //3.5//

body.text: khaḍgasomo māraḥ prāha /
body.translated_text: <s>Māra</s> <s>Khaḍgasoma</s> said:

children.text: kvacinna tasyāsti manaḥpradoṣa vā na viśuddha [tiṣṭhati cittā]śayena /
children.translated_text: "Nowhere is there any corruption of his mind, nor does he abide with an impure intention.
His movement is freed from the three realms—he cannot be destroyed by others." //3.6//

body.text: pāpīmānāha /
body.translated_text: <s>Pāpīmān</s> replied:

children.text: ye sanniṣaṇṇā iha lokadhātau kāmaprasaktā madamānamūrcchitāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Those who are seated in this world-realm, attached to pleasures, intoxicated by pride and conceit—
they are always obedient servants of mine. How can they not destroy him when united?" //3.7//

children.text: nuvṛttā mama kiṃkarāste kathaṃ na śakyaṃ tairvighātayituṃ samagraiḥ // Rkp_3.7 //

body.text: kṣititoyo nāma māraḥ sa evamāha /
body.translated_text: The <s>Māra</s> named <s>Kṣitiṭoya</s> spoke thus:

children.translated_text: "Having fully understood that all phenomena are essenceless like illusions and mirages, with craving subdued,

children.text: bhaveṣvasakto gaganasvabhāvaḥ śakyaṃ vighataḥ kathamasya kartum // Rkp_3.8 //
children.translated_text: unattached to existences, of a nature like space—how can any harm be done to him?" //3.8//

body.text: pāpīmānāha /
body.translated_text: <s>Pāpīmān</s> replied:

body.text: ihaiva tasyāsti vaśo triloke miṣṭānnapānāsanavastrasevinaḥ /
body.translated_text: "His power extends over the three worlds right here—those who partake of delicious food, drink, seats, and garments.

body.text: trivedanā cāsya matau pratiṣṭhitā kṣayaṃ praṇetuṃ na kathaṃ hi śakyam // Rkp_3.9 //
body.translated_text: The three feelings are established in his doctrine—how can he not be led to destruction?" //3.9//

body.text: tṛṣṇañjaho nāma māraḥ sa evamāha /
body.translated_text: The <s>Māra</s> named <s>Tṛṣṇañjaha</s> spoke thus:

children.text: yā ṛddhirasmin viṣaye 'sti kācit pāpīmatāṃ caiva mahoragāṇām /
children.translated_text: "Whatever supernatural power exists in this domain, belonging to <s>Pāpīmān</s> and the great serpents—

children.text: siddhārtha-ṛddherna kalāṃ spṛśanti kṣayaṃ praṇetuṃ ca kathaṃ hi śakyam // Rkp_3.10 //
children.translated_text: it does not equal even a fraction of the power of <s>Siddhārtha</s>. How then can he be led to destruction?" //3.10//

body.text: pāpīmānāha /
body.translated_text: <s>Pāpīmān</s> replied:

children.text: bhaktacchedo mayāsya hi kāritastacchilā punaḥ kṣiptā /
children.translated_text: "I caused the cutting off of his food, and stones were hurled at him.

children.text: uktāstathā krośā āśramāt kampito 'pi saḥ // Rkp_3.11 //
children.translated_text: Insults too were directed [at him], and from his hermitage he was shaken." //3.11//

body.text: bodhākṣo nāma māraḥ sa evamāha /
body.translated_text: The <s>Māra</s> named <s>Bodhākṣa</s> spoke thus:

children.text: yadā tvayā tasya kṛto vighātaḥ kaścit pradoṣaḥ kupitena tena /
children.translated_text: "When you attempted to harm him, did any anger arise in him?

children.text: saṃdarśitaste bhṛkuṭīmukhe vā kiṃ tasya sākṣāt [ku]vacaḥ śrutaṃ te // Rkp_3.12 //
children.translated_text: Did he show you a furrowed brow, or did you directly hear a harsh word from him?" //3.12//

body.text: pāpīmānāha /
body.translated_text: <s>Pāpīmān</s> replied:

children.text: pratisaṃkhyayā so kramate ca nityaṃ prahīṇarāgo gatadoṣamohaḥ /
children.translated_text: "He always proceeds with mindful contemplation, with passion, fault, and delusion abandoned.

children.text: sarveṣu sattveṣu sa maitracittaḥ saṃsargacaryā punarasya nityam // Rkp_3.13 //
children.translated_text: He has a mind of loving-kindness toward all beings, and his conduct is always one of gentle association." //3.13//

body.text: durdhaṣo nāma māraḥ sa evamāha /
body.translated_text: The <s>Māra</s> named <s>Durdharṣa</s> spoke thus:

children.text: ye ca trisaṃyojanapāśabaddhāsteṣāṃ vighātāya vayaṃ yatema /
children.translated_text: "For those bound by the fetters of the three bonds—let us strive for their destruction.

children.text: sa tu prahīṇāmayamohapāśaḥ kṣayaṃ praṇetuṃ ca kathaṃ hi śakyam // Rkp_3.14 //
children.translated_text: But he whose bonds of affliction, delusion, and disease are abandoned—how can he be led to destruction?" //3.14//

body.text: pāpīmānāha /
body.translated_text: <s>Pāpīmān</s> replied:

children.text: yūyaṃ mama prāptabalāḥ sahāyāḥ sadyo bhavanto bhavatāpramattāḥ /
children.translated_text: "You who have attained power are my allies—be vigilant at once!

children.text: apo 'dhitiṣṭhāmi mahīmaśeṣāṃ sarvā diśaḥ parvatamālinī ca // Rkp_3.15 //
children.translated_text: I shall command the waters and the entire earth, and all the directions with their mountain garlands.

body.text: gaganāt pracaṇḍaṃ ghanaśailavarṣaṃ samutsṛjāmyāyasacūrṇarāśim /
body.translated_text: From the sky I shall release fierce showers of dense boulders, heaps of iron filings,

children.translated_text: and I shall hurl barbed arrows, lances, razors, and spears at his body to crush it.

children.text: ebhiḥ prayogairabhighātadīptaistaṃ sthākyasiṃhaṃ prakaromi bhasma // Rkp_3.16 //
children.translated_text: With these blazing assaults, I shall reduce that lion of the <s>Śākyas</s> to ashes!" //3.16//

body.text: peyālam / yāvanmārakoṭībhirgāthākoṭī bhāṣiṃtā iti /
body.translated_text: And so on in full—as many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Māras</s>, that many <s>koṭis</s> of verses were spoken.

body.text: atha sarve mārāḥ ekakaṇṭhenaivamāhuḥ / evamastu / gamiṣyāmaḥ svakasvakebhyo bhavanebhyaḥ / sannāhaṃ baddhvā sasainyasaparivārāḥ āgamiṣyāmo yadasmākam ṛddhibalaviṣayaṃ tatsarvamādarśayiṣyāmaḥ / atha tvaṃ svayameva jñāsyase yādṛśaṃ śauryaṃ sa śramaṇo gautamastatkṣaṇe pradarśayati /
body.translated_text: Then all the <s>Māras</s> spoke in unison: "So be it! We shall return to our respective abodes. Having donned our armor, with our armies and retinues, we shall come back and display all our supernatural power, might, and domain. Then you yourself shall see what heroism that ascetic <s>Gautama</s> displays at that moment."

body.text: atha tā mārakoṭyaḥ svabhavanāni gatvā sannāhabandhaṃ kṛtvā ekaiko mārakoṭīsahasraparivāro vividhāni varmāṇi prāvṛtya nānāpraharaṇayukto vividhasannāhasaṃnaddhastasyāmeva rātrayā[ma]tyayenemaṃ jambudvipamanuprāptaḥ / aṅgamagadhasandhau gaganasthā yāvadevāsmiṃścāturdvīpike devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnara-mahoraga-preta-piśāca-kumbhāṇḍā bhagavato 'ntike aprasannacittā alabdhagauravamanaskārā dharme saṃghe cāprasannacittāste sarve māreṇa pāpīmatā bhagavato 'ntike vadhāya udyojitāḥ / te 'pi nānāpraharaṇavarmaprāvṛtāstatraiva tasthuḥ / māro 'pi pāpimān anuhimavataḥ pārśvaṃ gatvā yatra jyotīrasa
body.translated_text: Then those <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Māras</s>, having gone to their own abodes and donning their armor, each one accompanied by a retinue of a thousand <s>koṭis</s>, clad in various armors, equipped with diverse weapons, bound in various battle-gear, at the passing of that very night arrived in this <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. Stationed in the sky at the junction of <s>Aṅga</s> and <s>Magadha</s>, throughout this four-continent world, the <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>—

body.text: ṛṣiḥ prativasati maheśvarabhaktikaḥ aṣṭādaśasu vidyāsthāneṣu ṛddhiviṣayapāramiprāptaḥ pañcaśataparivārastasya maheśvararūpeṇa purataḥ sthitvaivamāha /
body.translated_text: ...a sage dwells there, devoted to <s>Maheśvara</s>, who has attained the perfection of supernatural powers in the eighteen branches of knowledge, accompanied by five hundred [disciples]. Standing before him in the form of <s>Maheśvara</s>, [<s>Māra</s>] said:

children.translated_text: "Surely, the foremost sage born in the <s>Gautama</s> lineage, renowned, endowed with <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledges),

children.text: magadhe saṃvasatīha so 'dya caratī piṇḍāya rājñorgṛham /
children.translated_text: dwells here in <s>Magadha</s>; today he goes for alms-food to the king's palace.

children.text: tena tvaṃ saha saṃlapasva viśadaṃ nānākathābhiḥ sthiraḥ
children.translated_text: Converse with him at length with various topics, remaining steadfast—

children.text: tatraiva tvamapyeva pañca niyataṃ prāpsyasyabhijñāvaśim // Rkp_3.17 //
children.translated_text: there, you too shall surely attain mastery of the five <s>abhijñās</s>." //3.17//

body.text: atha māraḥ pāpīmānimāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣitvā tatraivāntarhitaḥ / svabhavanañca gatvā svapārṣadyānāṃ mārāṇāmārocayati sma /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s> <s>Pāpīmān</s>, having spoken this verse, vanished right there. Going to his own abode, he told his retinue of <s>Māras</s>:

children.text: matto bhoḥ śṛṇutādya yādṛgatulā buddhirmayā cintitā
children.translated_text: "Listen now from me what matchless plan I have devised today!
Speak freely with the son of the <s>Śākyas</s>, who is endowed with supernatural power and splendor.

children.text: tāṃ māyāṃ na vidarśayet svaviṣayāṃ mārorudarpo mahān
children.translated_text: Let him not display his own domain of illusion—great is <s>Māra</s>'s fierce pride!

children.text: nityaṃ snigdhavacaḥ sa śiṣyaniyato māteva putreṣu ca // Rkp_3.18 //
children.translated_text: Always with tender words, as a disciple obedient, like a mother toward her children." //3.18//

body.text:
śiṣyāstasya hi ye prahīṇa[pra]madāścaryāṃ caranti dhruvaṃ
pūrvāṇhe nagaraṃ krameṇa nibhṛtaṃ svaireṇa tāvadvayam /
body.translated_text: "His disciples, who have abandoned intoxication, firmly practice the noble conduct. In the forenoon, [going] gradually to the city in a restrained and quiet manner—let us meanwhile

body.text: gṛṇhīmo druta nṛtyagītamadhuraprādhānyabhāvairyathā
body.translated_text: swiftly seize [them] with the foremost charms of dance, song, and sweet [music], so that

body.text: śrutvaitāṃ prakṛtiṃ manovirasatāṃ yāyāt sa śākyarṣabhaḥ // Rkp_3.19 //
body.translated_text: upon hearing this natural [allure], that bull of the <s>Śākyas</s> might become disenchanted in mind." //3.19//

body.text: aparo māra evamāha /
body.translated_text: Another <s>Māra</s> spoke thus:

children.translated_text: "Swiftly, before him—lions, tigers, elephants, camels, and fierce buffalo!
Creating many outside, thundering like monsoon clouds, with harsh roars,
let us stand with weapons and armaments ready—when he sees those wonders directly,

children.text: bhrānto ṛddhimapāsya yāsyati tato nānādiśo vismṛtaḥ // Rkp_3.20 //
children.translated_text: bewildered, abandoning his supernatural power, he will flee in all directions, confused!" //3.20//

body.text: aparo māraḥ prāha /
body.translated_text: Another <s>Māra</s> said:

children.translated_text: "Stationed repeatedly in streets, squares, and archways, with hideous faces,
bearing various sharp weapons—axes, spears, arrows, lances, swords, and daggers—
from the sky, with dense roars and terrible weapons, releasing thunderbolts and lightning,

children.text: kṣipraṃ sa sabhayaṃ prayāsyati tato bhūkampahetorvaśam // Rkp_3.21 //
children.translated_text: he will swiftly flee in fear, overcome by the earthquake's force!" //3.21//

body.text: vistareṇa yathāsau mārāṇāṃ mārabalaviṣayavikurvatāṃ sarve tathaivācakṣuḥ /
body.translated_text: In detail, all the <s>Māras</s> who were displaying their <s>Māra</s>-army's domain of supernatural transformations described [their plans] in just the same way.

body.text: bhagavāṃśca punaḥ sarvāvatīmimāṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasrīṃ lokadhātuṃ vajramayīmadhyatiṣṭhat / na ca punarbhūyo mārā rāvāṃścakrurna cāturdiśamagniparvatāstasthuḥ / na kṛ[ṣṇā]bhrā nākālavāyavo na ca kaścinnāgo 'bhipravarṣati sma antaśaḥ ekabindurapi buddhabalādhiṣṭhānena /
body.translated_text: But the Blessed One caused this entire great trichiliocosm to become as if made of <s>vajra</s> (diamond). And furthermore, the <s>Māras</s> could no longer make their roars, nor did the fire-mountains stand in the four directions, nor were there dark clouds, nor untimely winds, nor did any <s>Nāga</s> pour even a single drop of rain—through the empowering force of the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena catvāro mahāśrāvakāḥ pūrvāṇhe nivāsya pātracīvaramādāya rājagṛhaṃ mahānagaraṃ piṇḍāya praviviśuḥ / āyuṣmān śāriputro dakṣiṇena nagaradvāreṇa rājagṛhaṃ mahānagaraṃ piṇḍāya praviveśa / tatra ca nagare pañcāśanmārakumārakāḥ paramayauvanasurūpā mahatmaveṣasadṛśā nṛtyanto gāyantaḥ saṃceruḥ / te āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputramubhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ gṛhītvā vīthyāṃ dhāvanti sma nṛtyanto gāyantaḥ śāriputramevamāhuḥ / nartasva śramaṇa gāyasva śramaṇa / śāriputra āha / śṛṇuta yūyaṃ mārṣāḥ svayam / aśrutapūrvāṃ gītikāṃ śrāvayiṣyāmi / te ca sava mārakumārakā dhāvanto gītasvareṇa saha śāriputreṇaivamāhuḥ /
body.translated_text: At that time, the four great disciples, having dressed in the forenoon and taken their bowls and robes, entered the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms. The venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> entered the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms through the southern gate. In that city, fifty <s>Māra</s> youths, of supreme youth and beautiful form, dressed like great noblemen, were wandering about dancing and singing. They seized the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> by both hands and ran through the street dancing and singing, saying to <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Dance, ascetic! Sing, ascetic!' <s>Śāriputra</s> said: 'Listen, good sirs, yourselves! I shall let you hear a song never heard before.' And all those <s>Māra</s> youths, running with <s>Śāriputra</s>, said in a singing voice:

children.translated_text: Enough indeed! We have been deceived by the sense-bases (<s>āyatanas</s>), by the sense-bases!

children.text: āghatanāni hi āyatanāni antu karomyahu āyatanānām // Rkp_3.22 //
children.translated_text: The sense-bases are indeed grounds for destruction—I shall put an end to the sense-bases! // Rkp_3.22 //

children.text: alameva hi skandhakṛtehi vañcitā vayaṃ skandhakṛtehi /
children.translated_text: Enough indeed! We have been deceived by the products of the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), by the products of the aggregates!

children.text: āghatanāni hi skandhakṛtāni antu karomyahu skandhakṛtānām // Rkp_3.23 //
children.translated_text: The products of the aggregates are indeed grounds for destruction—I shall put an end to the products of the aggregates! // Rkp_3.23 //

body.text: tadyathā / vahara vahara / bhāravaha marīcivaha / sadyavaha amavaha / svāhā //
body.translated_text: That is to say: <s>vahara vahara / bhāravaha marīcivaha / sadyavaha amavaha / svāhā</s> //

body.text: sthaviraḥ śāriputro dhāvan gītasvareṇa imā gāthā imāni ca mantrapadāni bhāṣate sma / atha te pañcāśanmārakumārakāḥ paramahṛṣṭāḥ suprasannamanasa evamāhuḥ /
body.translated_text: The elder <s>Śāriputra</s>, running, spoke these verses and these <s>mantra</s> syllables in a singing voice. Then those fifty <s>Māra</s> youths, supremely delighted and with minds full of faith, spoke thus:

children.text: kṣamāpayāmo vayamadya nāthaṃ tvāmeva bandhuṃ jagataḥ sudeśikam /
children.translated_text: We beg forgiveness today of the Protector—you alone are the kinsman of the world, the excellent guide.

children.text: skandhā yathā te sabhayāḥ pradiṣṭāḥ tava vayaṃ sākṣiṇa eṣu nityam // Rkp_3.24 //
children.translated_text: Just as the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>) have been shown by you to be fearful, we are forever witnesses to this regarding them. // Rkp_3.24 //

body.text: sarve ca te śāriputrasya vīthīmadhye pādau śirasābhivandya purato niṣedurdharmaśravaṇāya /
body.translated_text: And all of them, in the middle of the street, bowed their heads at <s>Śāriputra</s>'s feet and sat before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ pūrveṇa nagaradvāreṇa rājagṛhe mahānagare piṇḍāya prāviśat / tathāpi pañcāśanmārakumārakā yāvad gītasvareṇaivāhuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> entered the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms through the eastern gate. Likewise, fifty <s>Māra</s> youths, running, said in a singing voice:

children.text: alameva hi dhātumayehi vāñcitā vayaṃ dhātumayehi /
children.translated_text: Enough indeed! We have been deceived by the products of the elements (<s>dhātus</s>), by the products of the elements!

children.text: āghatanāni hi dhātumayāni antu karomyahu dhātumayānām // Rkp_3.25 //
children.translated_text: The products of the elements are indeed grounds for destruction—I shall put an end to the products of the elements! // Rkp_3.25 //

children.text: alameva hi vedayitehi vañcitā vayaṃ vedayitehi /
children.translated_text: Enough indeed! We have been deceived by the products of feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), by the products of feeling!

children.text: āghatanāni hi vedayitāni antu karomyahu vedayitānām // Rkp_3.26 //
children.translated_text: The products of feeling are indeed grounds for destruction—I shall put an end to the products of feeling! // Rkp_3.26 //

children.text: alameva hi cetayitehi vañcitā vayaṃ cetayitehi /
children.translated_text: Enough indeed! We have been deceived by the products of volition (<s>cetanā</s>), by the products of volition!

children.text: āghatanāni hi cetayitānām antu karomyahu cetayitānām // Rkp_3.27 //
children.translated_text: The products of volition are indeed grounds for destruction—I shall put an end to the products of volition! // Rkp_3.27 //

children.text: alameva hi saṃjñākṛtehi vañcitā vayaṃ saṃjñākṛtehi /
children.translated_text: Enough indeed! We have been deceived by the products of perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), by the products of perception!

children.text: āghatanāni hi saṃjñākṛtāni antu karomyahu saṃjñākṛtānām // Rkp_3.28 //
children.translated_text: The products of perception are indeed grounds for destruction—I shall put an end to the products of perception! // Rkp_3.28 //

children.text: alameva hi saṃsaritehi vañcitā vayaṃ saṃsaritehi /
children.translated_text: Enough indeed! We have been deceived by the products of transmigration (<s>saṃsāra</s>), by the products of transmigration!

children.text: āghatanāni hi saṃsaritāni antu karomyahu saṃsaritānām // Rkp_3.29 //
children.translated_text: The products of transmigration are indeed grounds for destruction—I shall put an end to the products of transmigration! // Rkp_3.29 //

body.text: tad yathā / āmava āmava āmava / āraja raṇajaha / śamyatha śamyatha śamyatha / gaganapama svāhā //
body.translated_text: That is to say: <s>āmava āmava āmava / āraja raṇajaha / śamyatha śamyatha śamyatha / gaganapama svāhā</s> //

body.text: dhāvan gītasvareṇa āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano māraputrebhyaḥ imā gāthā imāni ca mantrapadāni bhāṣate sma / atha te pañcāśanmārakumārakāḥ paramahṛṣṭāḥ suprasannamanasaḥ evamāhuḥ /
body.translated_text: The venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, running, spoke these verses and these <s>mantra</s> syllables in a singing voice to the <s>Māra</s> sons. Then those fifty <s>Māra</s> youths, supremely delighted and with minds full of faith, spoke thus:

children.translated_text: The son of the Lord of Sages, endowed with supernatural powers, guarded in conduct, a <s>Dharma</s> lamp showing the faults of <s>saṃsāra</s> as equal [to illusion]—

children.text: pāpaṃ prahāya vayamādarabhaktijātā buddhaṃ gatādya śaraṇaṃ varadharmasaṃgham // Rkp_3.30 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned evil, we with reverence and devotion now take refuge in the <s>Buddha</s>, the excellent <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṃgha</s>. // Rkp_3.30 //

body.text: sarve te pañcāśānmārakumārakā vīthīmadhye āyuṣmato mahāmaudgalyāyanasya pādau śirasābhivandya tasyaiva purato niṣedurdharmaśravaṇāya /
body.translated_text: All those fifty <s>Māra</s> youths, in the middle of the street, bowed their heads at the feet of the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> and sat before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: athāyuṣmān pūrṇo maitrāyaṇīputraḥ uttareṇa nagaradvāreṇa piṇḍāya prāviśat / yāvad vīthyāṃ dhāvamāno gītasvareṇaivamāha /
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra</s> entered for alms through the northern gate. Running through the street, he spoke in a singing voice thus:

body.text: alameva hi sparśakṛtehi vañcitā vayaṃ sparśakṛtehi
body.translated_text: Enough indeed! We have been deceived by the products of contact (<s>sparśa</s>), by the products of contact—

body.text: āghatanāni hi sparśakṛtāni antu karomyahu sparśakṛtānām // Rkp_3.31 //
body.translated_text: the products of contact are indeed grounds for destruction—I shall put an end to the products of contact! // Rkp_3.31 //

body.text: alameva hi āghipatehi vañcitā vayam ādhipatehi

children.text: āghatanāni hi ādhipatīni antu karomyahu ādhipatonām // Rkp_3.32 //
children.translated_text: the dominant conditions are indeed grounds for destruction—I shall put an end to the dominant conditions! // Rkp_3.32 //

body.translated_text: Enough indeed! We have been deceived by the dominant conditions (<s>adhipati</s>), by the dominant conditions—

children.text: alameva hi saṃsaritehi vañcitā vayaṃ saṃsaritehi /
children.translated_text: Enough indeed! We have been deceived by the products of transmigration, by the products of transmigration!

children.text: āghatanāni hi saṃsaritāni antu karomyahu saṃsaritānām // Rkp_3.33 //
children.translated_text: The products of transmigration are indeed grounds for destruction—I shall put an end to the products of transmigration! // Rkp_3.33 //

children.text: alameva hi sarvabhavehi vañcitā vayaṃ sarvabhavehi /
children.translated_text: Enough indeed! We have been deceived by all forms of existence, by all forms of existence!

children.text: āghatanāni hi sarvabhavāni antu karomyahu sarvabhavānām // Rkp_3.34 //
children.translated_text: All forms of existence are indeed grounds for destruction—I shall put an end to all forms of existence! // Rkp_3.34 //

children.text: laghu gacchati āyu mārṣā salilā śīghrajavena veginī /
children.translated_text: Life passes swiftly, good sirs, like a stream rushing with rapid current;

children.text: na ca jānati bāliśo jano abudho rūpamadena mattakaḥ // Rkp_3.35 //
children.translated_text: but the foolish, ignorant person does not know this, intoxicated by the pride of form. // Rkp_3.35 //
Abbreviated:
the ignorant one, intoxicated by the pride of sound. // Rkp_3.36 //

body.text: abudho gandhamadena mattakaḥ // Rkp_3.37 //
body.translated_text: the ignorant one, intoxicated by the pride of smell. // Rkp_3.37 //

body.text: abudho rasamadena mattakaḥ // Rkp_3.38 //
body.translated_text: the ignorant one, intoxicated by the pride of taste. // Rkp_3.38 //

body.text: abudhaḥ sparśamadena mattakaḥ // Rkp_3.39 //
body.translated_text: the ignorant one, intoxicated by the pride of touch. // Rkp_3.39 //

body.text: laghu gacchati āyu mārṣāḥ salilā śīghrajavena veginī /
body.translated_text: Life passes swiftly, good sirs, like a stream rushing with rapid current;

body.text: na ca paśyati bāliśo jano abudho dharmamadena mattakaḥ // Rkp_3.40 //
body.translated_text: but the foolish, ignorant person does not see this, intoxicated by the pride of <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena). // Rkp_3.40 //

body.text: abudhaḥ skandhamadena mattakaḥ // Rkp_3.41 //
body.translated_text: the ignorant one, intoxicated by the pride of the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>). // Rkp_3.41 //

body.text: abudho dhātumadena mattakaḥ // Rkp_3.42 //
body.translated_text: the ignorant one, intoxicated by the pride of the elements (<s>dhātus</s>). // Rkp_3.42 //

body.text: abudho bhogamadena mattakaḥ // Rkp_3.43 //
body.translated_text: the ignorant one, intoxicated by the pride of enjoyments. // Rkp_3.43 //

body.text: abudhaḥ saukhyamadena mattakaḥ // Rkp_3.44 //
body.translated_text: the ignorant one, intoxicated by the pride of pleasure. // Rkp_3.44 //

body.text: abudho jātimadena mattakaḥ // Rkp_3.45 //
