body.translated_text: the ignorant one, intoxicated by the pride of birth. // Rkp_3.45 //

body.text: abudhaḥ kāmamadena mattakaḥ // Rkp_3.46 //
body.translated_text: the ignorant one, intoxicated by the pride of desire (<s>kāma</s>). // Rkp_3.46 //

children.text: laghu gacchati āyu mārṣāḥ salilā śīghrajavena veginī /
children.translated_text: Life passes swiftly, good sirs, like a stream rushing with rapid current;

children.text: na ca jānati bāliśo jano abudhaḥ sarvamadena mattakaḥ // Rkp_3.47 //
children.translated_text: but the foolish, ignorant person does not know this, intoxicated by the pride of all [things]. // Rkp_3.47 //

body.text: tadyathā / khargava khargava khargava / muna vijñāni / āvarta vivarta khabarta / brahmārtha jyotivarta svāhā //
body.translated_text: That is to say: <s>khargava khargava khargava / muna vijñāni / āvarta vivarta khabarta / brahmārtha jyotivarta svāhā</s> //

body.text: athāyuṣmān pūrṇo dhāvan gītasvareṇa māraputrebhya imā gāthā imāni ca mantrapadāni bhāṣate sma / atha te pañcāśanmārakumārakāḥ paramahṛṣṭāḥ suprasannamanasaḥ evamāhuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, running, spoke these verses and these <s>mantra</s> syllables in a singing voice to the <s>Māra</s> sons. Then those fifty <s>Māra</s> youths, supremely delighted and with minds full of faith, spoke thus:

children.translated_text: The path of peace has been taught by you, and the elements are like illusions and mirages;

children.text: saṃkalpamātra-janito vata jivaloko ratnatrayaṃ hi śaraṇaṃ varadaṃ vrajāmaḥ // Rkp_3.48 //
children.translated_text: the living world is born from mere conceptual construction—we go for refuge to the <s>Triratna</s> (Three Jewels), the bestower of boons! // Rkp_3.48 //

body.text: sarve te pañcāśanmārakumārakā āyuṣmataḥ pūrṇasya pādau śirasābhivandya vīthīmadhye tasya purato niṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya /
body.translated_text: All those fifty <s>Māra</s> youths bowed their heads at the feet of the venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s> and sat in the middle of the street before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: tena ca samayena āyuṣmān subhūtiḥ paścimena nagaradvāreṇa rājagṛhaṃ mahānagaraṃ piṇḍāya prāviśat / tatra ca nagaradvāre pañcāśanmārakumārakāḥ paramayauvanasurūpā mahātmaputraveṣadhāriṇo nṛtyanto gāyanto viceruḥ / te āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimubhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ gṛhya vīthyāṃ dhāvantaḥ āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtimevamāhuḥ / nartasva śramaṇa gāyasva śramaṇa / subhūtirāha / śṛṇuta mārṣā yūyam / aśrutapūrvāṃ gītikāṃ śrāvayiṣyāmi / sarve cālpaśabdā abhūvan / dhāvan gītasvareṇa āyuṣmān subhūtirevamāha /
body.translated_text: At that time, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> entered the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms through the western gate. At that city gate, fifty <s>Māra</s> youths, of supreme youth and beautiful form, wearing the attire of great noblemen's sons, were wandering about dancing and singing. They seized the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> by both hands and, running through the street, said to <s>Subhūti</s>: 'Dance, ascetic! Sing, ascetic!' <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'Listen, good sirs! I shall let you hear a song never heard before.' And all became quiet. Running, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> spoke in a singing voice thus:

children.translated_text: All entities are impermanent, like illusions and bubbles;
nothing permanent exists anywhere in the conditioned, which is of a transient nature;

children.text: marīci dṛṣṭameva yathā nāsti tatra śāśvataṃ
children.translated_text: just as a mirage, once seen, has no permanence therein—

children.text: laghu vyayo hi sarva dharma buddhimān prajānate // Rkp_3.49 //
children.translated_text: the wise person understands that all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) are of swift decay. // Rkp_3.49 //
All feelings of contact, suffering, and sensation are devoid of self;
there where all the foolish are attached, afflicted by the nature of suffering—
there is no friend anywhere who liberates from all suffering,

children.text: yathā hi śraddhā bodhimārga bhāvanā ca sevitā // Rkp_3.50 //
children.translated_text: save faith in the path of awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) and the cultivation thereof. // Rkp_3.50 //
On one side, all <s>dharmas</s> are free from the perception of purity;
the yoga of non-self, all conduct, has the character of [mere] substance and marks;
no life-force, nourisher, person, nor agent exists—
having understood the deceit and illusion, incline toward <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening). // Rkp_3.51 //
Consciousness operates in the sense faculties like lightning in the sky;
all contact, feeling, and volition are without a self;
examining wisely, there is nothing whatsoever as substantial reality—

children.text: saṃmohito hi bālavargo yantravat pravartate // Rkp_3.52 //
children.translated_text: the foolish multitude, deluded, operates like a machine. // Rkp_3.52 //

children.text: skandha sarve yoniśo vibhāvya kārako na labhyate
children.translated_text: Having wisely analyzed all the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), no agent is found;
the limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>) is peaceful, empty, free from all extremes;
this non-deluded nature of <s>dharmas</s> is called the practice of the path of awakening—
taught by the Guide who has attained awakening (<s>bodhi</s>). // Rkp_3.53 //

body.text: tadyathā / sumunde vimunde sundajahi / sili sili / sili sili / avahasili [avaha]sili / tathātvasili bhūtakoṭisili svāhā //
body.translated_text: That is to say: <s>sumunde vimunde sundajahi / sili sili / sili sili / avahasili avahasili / tathātvasili bhūtakoṭisili svāhā</s> //

body.text: athāyuṣmān subhūtirdhāvan gītasvareṇa imā gāthā imāni ca mantrapadāni bhāṣate sma / atha te pañcāśanmārakumārakāḥ paramahṛṣṭāḥ suprasannasanasaḥ evamāhuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, running, spoke these verses and these <s>mantra</s> syllables in a singing voice. Then those fifty <s>Māra</s> youths, supremely delighted and with minds full of faith, spoke thus:

children.translated_text: Not having heard such <s>dharmas</s> as these, following evil friends,
whatever evil <s>karma</s> was done through delusion and ignorance— // Rkp_3.54 //

body.text: pratideśaya taccaiva vayaṃ sākṣāj jinātmajāḥ

children.text: praṇidhānaṃ śubhaṃ kurmo buddhatvāya jagaddhite // Rkp_3.55 //
children.translated_text: we make a virtuous aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) for <s>Buddhahood</s>, for the welfare of the world. // Rkp_3.55 //

body.translated_text: we confess all that now, we who are sons of the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror);

body.text: sarva te pañcāśanmārakumārakā āyuṣmataḥ subhūteḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā tasyaiva purato vīthīmadhye niṣedurdharmaśravaṇāya /
body.translated_text: All those fifty <s>Māra</s> youths bowed their heads at the feet of the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> and sat in the middle of the street before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena sā vīthī buddhānubhāvena yojanaśatavistīrṇāvakāśaṃ saṃdṛśyate sma / tatra ca vīthīmadhye sthavira śāriputraḥ uttarāmukho niṣaṇṇaḥ / mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ pañcimāmukho niṣaṇṇaḥ / pūrṇo dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ / subhūtiḥ pūrvāmukhaḥ / parasparamardhayojanapramāṇena tasthuḥ / teṣāṃ ca caturṇāṃ mahāśrāvakāṇāṃ madhye pṛthivīpradeśe padmaṃ prādurabhūt pañcāśaddhastavistāraṃ
body.translated_text: At that time, that street, by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, appeared to extend to a width of a hundred <s>yojanas</s>. In the middle of that street, the elder <s>Śāriputra</s> sat facing north; <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> sat facing west; <s>Pūrṇa</s> faced south; <s>Subhūti</s> faced east. They stood at a distance of half a <s>yojana</s> from each other. And in the middle, between those four great disciples, on that spot of earth a lotus appeared, fifty <s>hastas</s> (cubits) in width,

body.text: jāmbūnadamayena daṇḍena nīlavaiḍūryamayaiḥ patraiḥ śrīgarbhamayena kesareṇa mukhāmayayā karṇīkayā / tataśca padmānmahānavabhāso 'bhavat / tasyāṃ ca vīthyāṃ tatpadmaṃ tripauruṣam uccatvena saṃdṛśyate sma yāvaccāturmahārājakāyikeṣu deveṣu tatpadmaṃ divyāni pañcāśad yojanāni uccatvena saṃdṛśyate sma / trāyastriṃśatsu tatpadmaṃ yojanaśatamuccatvena saṃdṛśyate sma yāvadakaniṣṭheṣu deveṣu tatpadmam ardhayojanamuccatvena saṃdṛśyate sma / tasya ca padmasya patrebhyo nānārthapadāḥ ślokā niśceruḥ / ye sattvā iha bhūmisthitāste imān ślokān śuśruvaḥ /
body.translated_text: with a stem of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold, petals of blue <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, stamens of <s>Śrīgarbha</s> [gems], and a pericarp of coral. From that lotus there was a great radiance. In that street, the lotus appeared three man-heights in elevation; among the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> gods, that lotus appeared fifty divine <s>yojanas</s> in height; among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, that lotus appeared a hundred <s>yojanas</s> in height; among the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods, that lotus appeared half a <s>yojana</s> in height. From the petals of that lotus issued forth verses of various meanings. Those beings situated on this earth heard these verses:

children.translated_text: A single person has arisen in this <s>Buddhakṣetra</s> (Buddha-field), faultless;
by him alone <s>Māra</s> with his entire army, forces, and vehicles has been defeated. // Rkp_3.56 //
By the power of that single <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of Dharma) has been set in motion;

children.text: ekākīha jagaddhetorāyā[to hi] na saṃśayaḥ // Rkp_3.57 //
children.translated_text: alone, for the sake of the world, he has come here—there is no doubt. // Rkp_3.57 //
Wise, skilled in many treatises on conduct, seekers of <s>Dharma</s>, meaning, and liberation,
knowers of policy—the excellent <s>Upatiṣya</s> and <s>Kaulita</s>, trained in the Teacher's [doctrine] here;
the wise one, skilled in the welfare of all the world, the great proclaimer of the true <s>Dharma</s>—

children.text: neṣyatyadya sa sarvalokamahito vādipradhāno muniḥ // Rkp_3.58 //
children.translated_text: he, honored by all the world, the foremost among debaters, the Sage, shall today lead [beings]. // Rkp_3.58 //

body.text:
trayadhvajñānasudeśakaḥ śramaṇarāṭ śikṣātrayodbhāvaka-
strātā vai sanarāmarasya jagato dharmāprameyārthavit /
body.translated_text: The king of ascetics, excellent teacher of the knowledge of the three times, producer of the threefold training, protector of this world with its humans and gods, knower of the immeasurable meaning of the <s>Dharma</s>,

body.text: lokasyātha hitapracārakuśalo jñānapradīpo mahān
body.translated_text: skilled in promoting the welfare of the world, the great lamp of knowledge,

body.text: sadvādī trimalaprahīṇa iha so adyaiva saṃgāsyati // Rkp_3.59 //
body.translated_text: a true speaker, free from the three defilements—he shall assemble [them] today itself. // Rkp_3.59 //

children.translated_text: For the world's sake, with unwavering mind, he wandered, liberating all suffering beings;

children.text: avidyayā nīvṛtalocanānāṃ saddharmacakṣuḥ pradadau yathāvat // Rkp_3.60 //
children.translated_text: to those whose eyes were covered by ignorance, he properly gave the eye of the true <s>Dharma</s>. // Rkp_3.60 //

children.text: sarvāvatīyaṃ pariṣat samāgatā na cirādihāyāsyati vādisiṃhaḥ /
children.translated_text: This entire assembly has gathered—soon the lion among debaters shall come here,

children.text: paramārthadarśī paramaṃ surūpo balairupeto hi parāparajñaḥ // Rkp_3.61 //
children.translated_text: the seer of the supreme truth, of supreme beauty, endowed with powers, the knower of the higher and lower [states]. // Rkp_3.61 //

body.text: dṛṣṭvā jagadduḥkhamahārṇavastham āhantumāyāsyati dharma[bherīm] / ṣaḍiṇdriyairuttamasaṃvarasthaḥ [ṣaḍāśrayaśca ṣaḍa]bhijñakovidaḥ // Rkp_3.62 //
body.translated_text: Having seen the world submerged in the great ocean of suffering, he shall come to strike the drum of <s>Dharma</s>; abiding in supreme restraint of the six sense faculties, with the six bases, skilled in the six <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges). // Rkp_3.62 //

children.translated_text: For the supreme teaching of the six <s>pāramitā</s> (perfection) doctrines, the lion among debaters shall come, bearing the six seeds;
for the subjugation of the domain of the six sense faculties, the lord among charioteers [comes] with the six supreme aims [and] mindfulness. // Rkp_3.63 //

body.text: yāvat ṣaṭsu kāmāvacareṣu deveṣu tataḥ padmādimā gāthā niśceruḥ /
body.translated_text: As far as the six gods of the <s>Kāmāvacara</s> (desire realm), from that lotus these verses issued forth:

children.text: yūyaṃ samagrā ratimadya bhuṃjatha pramattacittā madatṛṣṇa[saṃ]ratāḥ /
children.translated_text: You all together enjoy pleasures today, with heedless minds, delighting in intoxication and craving;

children.text: sadā vimūḍhā ratipānamattā na pūjayadhvaṃ sugataṃ pramādāt // Rkp_3.64(="63") //
children.translated_text: ever deluded, intoxicated with the drink of pleasure—do not, through heedlessness, fail to honor the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One)! // Rkp_3.64(="63") //
Desires are impermanent, like water and the moon; the snare of <s>saṃsāra</s> is extremely firm for beings—

children.text: aniḥsṛtānāṃ ratiṣu pramādināṃ na nirvṛto vā tu punarbhaviṣyati // Rkp_3.65(="64") //
children.translated_text: For those who have not escaped, who are heedless in pleasures, there will be no liberation nor will there be rebirth. //Rkp 3.65//

children.text: sadā pramattā na śamāya yuktā na paśyata prāksukṛtaṃ śubhāśubham /
children.translated_text: Always heedless, not engaged in peace, you do not see the good and bad deeds done before.
Surrounded by the fears of old age, disease, and death, you are headed toward the realms of misfortune. //Rkp 3.66//

children.text: dānaṃ damaṃ saṃyamamapramādaṃ niṣevata prāksukṛtaṃ ca rakṣata /
children.translated_text: Practice generosity, self-control, restraint, and diligence, and guard the good deeds done before.

children.text: utsṛjya kāmānaśūcinanantā- nupasaṃkramadhvaṃ sugataṃ śaraṇyam // Rkp_3.67(="66") //
children.translated_text: Abandoning the impure and endless desires, approach the <s>Sugata</s> who is the refuge. //Rkp 3.67//

children.text: gatvā ca tasmād vacanaṃ śṛṇudhvaṃ subhāṣitaṃ taddhi mahārthikaṃ vacaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having gone, hear the well-spoken word from him, for that speech is of great meaning.

children.text: prajñā-vimuktiḥ praśamāya hetuḥ saddharmayuktaṃ śravaṇaṃ mahārtham // Rkp_3.68(="67") //
children.translated_text: Wisdom and liberation are the cause of peace; hearing endowed with the true <s>dharma</s> is of great purpose. //Rkp 3.68//

body.text: yāvat ṣoḍaśasu devanikāyeṣu tasya padmasya patrebhyaḥ imā evaṃrūpā gāthā niśceruḥ /
body.translated_text: Throughout the sixteen classes of gods, from the petals of that lotus, verses of this kind issued forth.

children.translated_text: Contemplate the <s>dharma</s> with effort, delighting in concentrated meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), free from defilement.

children.text: abhrāntacittāśca vimokṣakāṅkṣiṇo dveṣaprahāṇāya matiṃ kurudhvam // Rkp_3.69(="68") //
children.translated_text: With unconfused minds, desiring liberation, set your minds to the abandonment of hatred. //Rkp 3.69//
Contemplate the lamp of the thirteen aspects and signs—the supreme patience (<s>kṣānti</s>).

children.text: athaiva cāpyatra vimokṣamāśu saṃprāpsyatha vyādhijarāviyuktam // Rkp_3.70(="69") //
children.translated_text: And then here you will quickly attain liberation, free from disease and old age. //Rkp 3.70//

body.text: śāśvata ye rūpavikalpasaṃjñake nityaṃ dhruvātmasthirabhāvadṛṣṭayaḥ /
body.translated_text: Those who hold views of eternalism regarding the perception of discrimination of form, who always have views of permanence, stability, self, and enduring existence—

body.text: teṣāṃ ca janma[jarayora]hāni- rapāyabhūmipravaṇā hi te vai // Rkp_3.71(="70") //
body.translated_text: for them there is no cessation of birth and aging, and they are indeed inclined toward the realms of misfortune. //Rkp 3.71//

children.text: traidhātukaṃ vīkṣya sadā nirātma- madravyamasvaṃvaśakaṃ nirīham /
children.translated_text: Seeing the three realms as always selfless, without substance, not under one's own control, and without desire,

children.text: kṣāntiṃ vibhāventi ya ānulomikīṃ bhavanti te sarvi gatipramuktāḥ // Rkp_3.72(="71") //
children.translated_text: those who develop the conforming patience (<s>ānulomikī kṣānti</s>) become freed from all destinations. //Rkp 3.72//

children.text: teṣāṃ na mṛtyurna jarā na rogo na durgatirnāpriyasaṃprayogaḥ /
children.translated_text: For them there is no death, no old age, no disease, no misfortune, no association with the unpleasant.

children.text: ākāśatulyāniha sarvadharmān ye bhāvayante vyayabhāvayuktān // Rkp_3.73(="72") //
children.translated_text: Those who contemplate all <s>dharmas</s> here as equal to space, endowed with arising and decay. //Rkp 3.73//

children.text: atyantaśuddho hi varaḥ sa mārgo yeṣāmasaṅgaṃ mana-indriyeṣu /
children.translated_text: For utterly pure indeed is that excellent path, for those who have non-attachment in mind and senses.

children.text: mārān vidhunvanti catuṣprakārān yathāhyayaṃ saṃprati śākyasiṃhaḥ // Rkp_3.74(="73") //
children.translated_text: They shake off the four kinds of <s>Māra</s>, just as this <s>Śākyasiṃha</s> (Lion of the Śākyas) does now. //Rkp 3.74//

children.text: ekaṃ nayaṃ ye tu vibhāvayanti niṣkiñcanaṃ sarvanimittavarjitam /
children.translated_text: Those who contemplate the single method, free from possessions, devoid of all signs,

children.text: dvayaprahāṇāya vinītaceṣṭā teṣāmayaṃ mārgavaraḥ praṇītaḥ // Rkp_3.75(="74") //
children.translated_text: with conduct disciplined for the abandonment of duality—for them this excellent and noble path is proclaimed. //Rkp 3.75//
Having contemplated all <s>dharmas</s> here as empty, without owner, without agent, operating through birth,

children.text: spṛśanti bodhiṃ gaganasvabhāvāṃ niruttamāṃ prārthanayā vivarjitām // Rkp_3.76(="75") //
children.translated_text: they touch <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) whose nature is like space, unsurpassed, free from aspiration. //Rkp 3.76//

body.text: ebhirevaṃrūpairarthapadadharmaśabdairniścaradbhirya iha lokadhātau manuṣyāmanuṣyāste samāgamya vīthīmadhye samantāstasya padmasya niṣeduḥ / yāvadaprameyāsaṃkhyeyā akaniṣṭhā devā akaniṣṭhābhavanādavatīrya te padmasya samantato nyaṣīdan dharmaśravaṇāya / aśrauṣīnmāraḥ pāpīmānetān ślokān / samantataśca vyavalokya adrākṣīt rājagṛhe mahānagare vīthimadhye padmam / tataśceme ślokāḥ niśceruḥ / tadā padmaṃ paricārya aprameyāsaṃkhyeyāni manuṣyakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi sanniṣaṇṇāni dharmaśravaṇāya /
body.translated_text: With such words of meaning, phrases, <s>dharma</s>-terms, and expressions issuing forth, all humans and non-humans in this world-realm gathered and sat all around that lotus in the middle of the road. And immeasurable and innumerable <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods descended from the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heaven.

body.text: atha khalu māraḥ pāpīmān ūrddhvaṃ vyavalokitavān / adrākṣīt ṣaṭsu kāmāvacareṣu deveṣu sarvatra devabhavane tatpadmam / tadeva cānuparivārya aprameyāsaṃkhyeyāni devakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi [sanniṣaṇṇāni] dharmaśravaṇāya /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra Pāpīmān</s> looked upward. He saw that lotus in every divine abode among the six classes of desire-realm gods. And surrounding it, immeasurable and innumerable tens of millions of hundreds of thousands of gods were seated.

body.text: atha bhūyasyā mātrayā māraḥ pāpīmān duḥkhito durmanā vipratisārī saṃhṛṣṭaromakūpaḥ prakhinnagātraḥ saṃprakampitaśarīro gagane pradhāvan mahatā svareṇa parān mārān prakrośannevamāha /
body.translated_text: Then, even more so, <s>Māra Pāpīmān</s>, distressed, disheartened, filled with remorse, with hair standing on end, limbs exhausted, body trembling, rushed through the sky and, crying out with a great voice to the other <s>Māras</s>, spoke thus:

children.text: śṛṇu giri mama imā samavahitamanā na me vaśo svaviṣaye na ca balamiha me /
children.translated_text: 'Listen to my words, O mountain, with concentrated mind! I have no power in my own domain, nor do I have strength here.

children.text: idamiha munibalamatiguṇaviśadaṃ prasarati jagati sthirajanakaraṇam // Rkp_3.77(="76") //
children.translated_text: The power of this sage, exceedingly brilliant in qualities, spreads throughout the world, creating stability in people.' //Rkp 3.77//
'A lotus has arisen here to delight humans and gods, arrived from all sides, devoted to good people.

children.text: paritṛṣita sugatasuvacananiratā vrajati hi śamathapathamatiguṇaparamā // Rkp_3.78(="77") //
children.translated_text: Those who are thirsting, devoted to the good words of the <s>Sugata</s>, proceed on the path of tranquility (<s>śamatha</s>), supreme in excellent qualities.' //Rkp 3.78//
'This is the magic of the ascetic, set in motion here for the delusion of the triple world.
All hosts of humans and gods, with undivided minds, stand with the lotus spread before them.
Quickly release a rain of rocks now! With terrifying voice, let us roar!
Let this <s>Māra</s> go to destruction, struck down today with the foremost weapons!' //Rkp 3.79//

body.text: athāparo māraḥ pāpīmantamevamāha /
body.translated_text: Then another <s>Māra</s> spoke thus to <s>Pāpīmān</s>:

children.translated_text: 'Listen to this beneficial word of ours. Are you one who has understood the <s>dharma</s>?

children.text: yat paśyanniha marasainyavilayaṃ nāyāsi śānti tataḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing here the dissolution of <s>Māra</s>'s army, why do you not come to peace thereby?

children.text: bhrāntāḥ sma asamīkṣya saugatamidaṃ tejovapuḥ śrīghanaṃ
children.translated_text: We are confused, not having recognized this splendid radiance of the <s>Sugata</s>, dense with glory.

children.text: rūpaṃ nānyadihottamaṃ suśaraṇaṃ buddhādṛte nāyakam // Rkp_3.80(="79") //
children.translated_text: There is no other form supreme here, no good refuge, no leader apart from the <s>Buddha</s>.' //Rkp 3.80//

body.text: athāparo māraḥ prarudan paramakrodhāviṣṭavacano māraṃ pāpīmantamevamāha /
body.translated_text: Then another <s>Māra</s>, weeping, possessed by extreme anger in his speech, spoke thus to <s>Māra Pāpīmān</s>:

children.text: kumārgasaṃprasthita mārgahīna prajānase na svabalaṃ na śaktim /
children.translated_text: 'You who have set out on the wrong path, devoid of the path, you do not know your own strength or power.

children.text: na lajjase 'patrapase na caiva yastvaṃ saha spardhasi nāyakena // Rkp_3.81(="80") //
children.translated_text: You have no shame, no modesty at all, you who compete with the Leader!' //Rkp 3.81//

children.text: asmabdalairyadvilayaṃ prayātaṃ buddhasya śaktyā tu jagat samagram /
children.translated_text: 'By our forces, what had gone to dissolution—the entire world, through the power of the <s>Buddha</s>,
has quickly come near the lotus, with pure bodies nourished by hearing the <s>dharma</s>.' //Rkp 3.82//

children.text: vayaṃ tu vībhatsatarāḥ prayātā durgandhakāyā balavīryanaṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'We have become most repulsive, with foul-smelling bodies, our strength and vigor destroyed.

children.text: yāvanna yātā vilayaṃ kṣaṇena tāvad vrajāmaḥ śaraṇaṃ munīndram // Rkp_3.83(="82") //
children.translated_text: Before we go to dissolution in an instant, let us go for refuge to the Lord of Sages.' //Rkp 3.83//

body.text: athāpare mārāḥ kṛtāñjalaya evamāhuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then other <s>Māras</s>, with palms joined, spoke thus:

children.translated_text: 'O <s>Pāpīmān</s>, you are devoid of righteous conduct, delighting in sinful deeds.
This Lord, skilled in the welfare and benefit of the world, is the <s>Buddha</s>, the foremost of the virtuous.
Let us go quickly to the city, with eyes delighted and joyful.

children.text: gacchāmaḥ śaraṇaṃ trilokamahitaṃ sarvauṣadhaṃ prāṇinām // Rkp_3.84(="83") //
children.translated_text: Let us go for refuge to the one honored by the three worlds, the universal medicine for all living beings.' //Rkp 3.84//

body.text: atha tatraiva gaganaghoṣavatirnāma māraḥ sa uccasvareṇaivamāha /
body.translated_text: Then, right there, the <s>Māra</s> named <s>Gaganaghoṣavat</s> spoke in a loud voice thus:

children.text: sava yūyaṃ samagrāḥ śṛṇuta mama vaco bhaktitaḥ prītiyuktāḥ
children.translated_text: 'All of you, assembled together, listen to my word with devotion and joy.
Turning your views away from evil, with body, mind, speech, conduct, and actions bowed in reverence,
having abandoned anger, joyful, [following] the words of the best of sages, with abundant devotion and faith,

children.text: gatvā buddhaṃ samakṣaṃ śaraṇamasulabhaṃ pūjayāmo 'dya bhaktayā // Rkp_3.85(="84") //
children.translated_text: having gone before the <s>Buddha</s>, let us today worship with devotion this refuge so rare to obtain.' //Rkp 3.85//

body.text: atha tatkṣaṇameva sarve mārā gaganatalādavatīrya rājagṛhanagaradvārāṇi saptaratnamayāni cakruḥ / kecinmāracakravartirājaveṣamātmānamabhinirmīya bhagavataḥ pūjāparāstasthuḥ / kecid brahmaveṣaṃ kecidvaśavartiveṣaṃ kecinmaheśvaraveṣaṃ kecinnārāyaṇaveṣaṃ kecittuṣitaveṣaṃ kecid yamaveṣaṃ kecicchakraveṣaṃ kecittrayastriṃśadveṣaṃ kecit kumāraveṣaṃ kecid vaiśravaṇaveṣaṃ kecid virūḍhakaveṣaṃ kecid virūpākṣaveṣaṃ kecid dhṛtarāṣṭraveṣaṃ kecit prākṛtacaturmahārājaveṣaṃ kecit sūryaveṣaṃ keciccandraveṣaṃ kecittārakaveṣaṃ kecidasuraveṣaṃ kecid garuḍaveṣaṃ kecit kinnaraveṣaṃ kecinmahoragaveṣaṃ kecid ratnaparvataveṣaṃ kecit niṣkaveṣaṃ kecinnānāratnaveṣaṃ kecid ratnavṛkṣaveṣaṃ kecit kṣatriyaveṣaṃ kecidanyatīrthikaveṣaṃ keciccakraratnaveṣaṃ kecinmaṇiratnaveṣaṃ kecidairāvaṇaveṣaṃ kecidvalāhakarājaveṣaṃ
body.translated_text: Then at that very moment, all the <s>Māras</s> descended from the sky and made the gates of the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> out of the seven precious substances. Some, having magically created themselves in the guise of <s>Māra</s> universal monarchs, stood devoted to the worship of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Some [assumed] the guise of <s>Brahmā</s>, some

body.text: kecit strīratnaveṣaṃ kecit śreṣṭhimahāratnaveṣam ātmānamabhinirmīya tasthurbhagavataḥ pūjākarmaṇe / kecinnīlā nīlavarṇāḥ śvetavarṇālaṅkārālaṃkṛtamātmānamabhinirmīya bhagavataḥ pūjākarmaṇe lohitān chatradhvajapatākāmuktāhārān dhārayantastālapramāṇāmātramuccatvena gaganatale tasthuḥ / kecidavadātā avadātavarṇā mañjiṣṭhavarṇābharaṇavibhūṣaṇāḥ pītān chatradhvajapatākāna dhārayantastasthuḥ / kecinmañjiṣṭhā mañjiṣṭhavarṇāḥ suvarṇābharaṇavibhūṣaṇā nīlān chatradhvajapatākān dhārayantastasthuḥ / kecillohitā lohitavarṇāḥ śvetamuktavarṣaṃ vavarṣuḥ / kecit śvetāḥ śvetavarṇāḥ lohitamuktavarṣaṃ vavarṣuḥ / keciddevarṣivarṇamātmānamabhinirmīya gaganāt puṣpavarṣam abhipravarṣuḥ / kecid bhagavataḥ śrāvakaveṣamātmānamabhinirmīya nānādivyagandhavarṣaṃ gaganādvavarṣuḥ / kecid gandharvavarṇā nānādivyatūryāṇi parājaghnuḥ / kecit amarakanyāvarṇā nānāratnabhājaneṣu gandhodakaṃ dhārayantaḥ pṛthivīṃ siṣiñcuḥ / kecit kālakṛṣṇavarṇāḥ gandhān pradhūpayāmāsuḥ / keciddevaputrarūpeṇa nṛtyagītasvarān mumucuḥ / kecinnānāvarṇā yena bhagavāṃstena prāñjalayo bhagavantaṃ tuṣṭuvuḥ / kecinmārāḥ mārapārṣadyā api yasyāṃ diśi bhagavāṃstadabhimukhā nānāvidhāni maṇiratnāni dadhire bhagavataḥ pūjākarmaṇe / kecid vīthīgṛhaśaraṇagavākṣoraṇaharmya-catvaraśṛṅgāṭakakūṭāgāra-dvāra-vṛkṣavimāneṣu
body.translated_text: some [assumed] the guise of jewel-women, some the guise of great merchant-jewels, and having magically created themselves, they stood for the worship of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Some, being blue and of blue color, magically created themselves adorned with white-colored ornaments, for the worship of the <s>Bhagavān</s>; [some with] red

body.text: sthitvā prāñjalayo niṣeduḥ bhagavata pūjākarmaṇe /
body.translated_text: and standing with palms joined, they sat for the worship of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: atha sa māro yadā adrākṣīt sarvāṃstān mārān saparivārān śramaṇagautamaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatān tadā bhūyasyā mātrayā kṣūbdhastrasto bhrāntaḥ prarudannevamāha /
body.translated_text: Then when that <s>Māra</s> saw all those <s>Māras</s> with their retinues having gone for refuge to the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>, he became even more agitated, frightened, confused, and weeping, spoke thus:

children.text: na bhūyo me sahāyo 'sti naṣṭā śrīrme 'dya sarvataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I have no more allies. My glory is lost today in every direction.

children.text: bhraṣṭo 'smi māraviṣayāt kuryāṃ vīryaṃ hi paścimam // Rkp_3.86(="85") //
children.translated_text: I have fallen from <s>Māra</s>'s domain. Let me make one final effort!' //Rkp 3.86//

children.text: mūlaṃ chindyāmahaṃ padmaṃ sattvā yena diśo 'vrajan /
children.translated_text: 'I shall cut the root of this lotus, by which beings have gone in all directions.

children.text: chedāt padmasya saṃbhrāntā etat syāt paścimaṃ balam // Rkp_3.87(="86") //
children.translated_text: By cutting the lotus, they will be confused—this shall be my final display of power!' //Rkp 3.87//

body.text: iti saṃcintya māraḥ pāpīmān vāyuvadavatīrya gaganād yena tatpadmaṃ vīthīgataṃ tena prasṛtya tatpadmamādaṇḍādicchati ūddhartuṃ spraṣṭumapi na śaśāka / patrāṇi chettumicchati na ca tāni dadarśuḥ / padmakarṇikāmapi pāṇinā parāhantumicchati tāmapi naiva lebhe / tad yathā vidyud dṛśyate na copalabhyate / tad yathā vā chāyā dṛśyate na copalabhyate / evameva tat padmaṃ dṛśyate na copalabhyate /
body.translated_text: Having thus reflected, <s>Māra Pāpīmān</s> descended from the sky like the wind and rushed toward that lotus in the road, wishing to uproot it from the stem—but he was not able even to touch it. He wished to cut the petals, but he could not even see them. The lotus

body.text: yadā ca māraḥ pāpīmān tat padmaṃ dadarśa na copalebhe na pasparśa atha punaḥ sarvaparṣat saṃtrāsanārtham uccaiḥ mahābhairavaṃ svaraṃ moktumicchati tadapi na śaśāka / na punarmahābalavegena ubhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāmicchati mahāpṛthivīṃ parāhantuṃ kampayituṃ tadapi spraṣṭuṃ na śaśāka naivopalebhe / tad yathāpi nāma kaścit
body.translated_text: when <s>Māra Pāpīmān</s> saw that lotus but could neither obtain it nor touch it, then, wishing to emit a great, terrifying sound to frighten the entire assembly, he was unable to do even that. Nor again, with great force and might, with both

body.text: ākāśamicchet parāmarṣṭuṃ na ca upalabhate / evameva māraḥ pāpīmān dadarśa pṛthivīṃ na ca pasparśa nopalebhe / tasyaitadabhavat / yattvahaṃ yathā saṃnipatitānāṃ sattvānāṃ prahāraṃ dadyāṃ cittavikṣepaṃ vā kuryām iti / dadarśa tān sattvān na caikasattvamapi upalebhe na ca pasparśa /
body.translated_text: he wished to grasp space but could not apprehend it. Just so, <s>Māra Pāpīmān</s> saw the earth but could neither touch nor apprehend it. Then this occurred to him: 'If only I could strike the assembled beings, causing distraction of their minds—'

body.text: atha bhūyasyā mātrayā māraḥ pāpīmān ruroda / buddhanubhāvena cāsya sarvaṃ śarīraṃ vṛkṣavat cakampe / sāśrumukhaścaturdiśaṃ ca vyavalokayannevamāha /
body.translated_text: Then, even more so, <s>Māra Pāpīmān</s> wept. And by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, his entire body trembled like a tree. With tearful face, looking in the four directions, he spoke thus:

children.translated_text: 'This magic has been wrought by the ascetic today for the purpose of attracting the entire world,

children.text: yenāhaṃ purato vimohita ida bhrāntiṃ gato 'smi kṣaṇāt /
children.translated_text: by which I have been deluded before, and have gone to confusion in an instant.

children.text: bhraṣṭo 'haṃ viṣayāt svapuṇyabalataḥ kṣīṇaṃ ca me jīvitaṃ
children.translated_text: I have fallen from my domain through the power of my own merit being exhausted, and my life force is spent.

children.text: śīghraṃ yāmi nirākṛtaḥ svabhavanaṃ yāvanna yāmi kṣayam // Rkp_3.88(="87") //
children.translated_text: I depart quickly, rejected, to my own abode, before I go to destruction.' //Rkp 3.88//

body.text: svabhavanamapi gantumicchati na tatrāpi śaśāka gantum / sa bhūyasyā mātrayā trasto ruroda / evaṃ cāsyodapādi / parikṣīṇo 'ham ṛddhibalāt māhyaivāhaṃ śramaṇasya vaśamāgaccheyam / mā vā me 'sya śatrorvā agrato jīvitakṣayaḥ syāt yat tvahamato 'ntardhāyeyaṃ sahābuddhakṣetrasya bahirdhā kālaṃ kruyāṃ yathaikasattvo
body.translated_text: He wished to go to his own abode but was unable to go even there. He became even more frightened and wept. And this occurred to him: 'I am exhausted of my magical power. Let me not fall under the ascetic's control! Or let not this enemy of mine—'

body.text: 'pi me sahābuddhakṣetre vā kālaṃ kurvantaṃ na paśyet / tathāpi na śaknoti antardhātuṃ na digvidikṣu palāyituṃ vā tatraiva kaṇṭhe paṃcabandhanabaddhamātmānaṃ dadarśa / bhūyasyā mātrayā kupitastrastaḥ uccai rudannevamāha / hā priyaputrabāndhavajanā na bhūyo drakṣyāma iti /
body.translated_text: even if one in my <s>Sahā</s> <s>Buddha</s>-field were dying, he would not be able to see it, nor to vanish, nor to flee in any direction—right there he saw himself bound at the neck with five bonds. Even more enraged and terrified, he cried out loudly: Alas, dear sons, relatives, and friends—we shall not see you again!

body.text: atha ghoṣavatirnāma māraścakravartiveṣeṇa niṣaṇṇabhūto māraṃ pāpīmantamevamāha /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s> named <s>Ghoṣavati</s>, seated in the guise of a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), said this to <s>Māra</s> the Evil One:

children.translated_text: Why, sir, are you grieving today and weeping with a distorted face and voice?

children.text: kṣipraṃ sarvajagadvaraṃ munivaraṃ nirbhīḥ śaraṇyaṃ vraja /
children.translated_text: Quickly, without fear, go to the refuge of the supreme sage, the best in all the world.
He is the protector, the guide of the world, the lamp and refuge, the lord who removes the three sufferings—

children.text: na tvetaṃ samupāsyasi sukhaśamaṃ saukhyaṃ na saṃprāpsyasi // Rkp_3.89(="88") //
children.translated_text: If you do not worship him, who is peaceful and blissful, you shall not attain happiness. //<s>Rkp</s> 3.89(=88)//

body.text: atha mārasya pāpīmata etadabhavat / yattvahaṃ santoṣavacanena śramaṇagautamaṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajeyaṃ yadahamebhyo bandhanebhyaḥ parimucyeyam /
body.translated_text: Then this thought occurred to <s>Māra</s> the Evil One: What if I, with words of contentment, were to go for refuge to the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>—perhaps I might be freed from these bonds.

body.text: ath māraḥ pāpīmān yasyāṃ diśi bhagavān vijahāra tenāñjaliṃ praṇamyaivamāha / namastasmai varapudgalāya jarāvyādhiparimocakāya / evamahaṃ tsaṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi / evaṃ cāha /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, extending his joined palms in the direction where the <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling, spoke thus: Homage to that supreme being, the liberator from old age and disease. Thus do I go for refuge to that <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>. And he said thus:

body.text:
asmānnātha mahābhayāt suviṣamāt kṣipraṃ munerbandhanāt
mucyeyaṃ śaraṇāgato 'smi sugatasyādyaprabhṛtyagraṇīḥ /
body.translated_text: May I be quickly freed from this great, most perilous fear, the bonds of the Sage! I have come for refuge to the <s>Sugata</s>; from today onward, I am foremost [among his devotees].

body.text: mohāndhena mayā tvayi prakupitenoccaiḥ pradoṣaḥ kṛtaḥ
body.translated_text: Blinded by delusion, enraged at you, I committed great offenses loudly—

body.text: tat sarvaṃ pratideśayāmi puratastvāṃ sākṣiṇaṃ sthāpya tu // Rkp_3.90(="89") //
body.translated_text: All that I confess before you, placing you as witness. //<s>Rkp</s> 3.90(=89)//

body.text: yadā ca māraḥ pāpīmān santoṣavacanena buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatastadā muktamātmānaṃ saṃjānīte / yadā punarasyaivaṃ bhavati prakrameyamiti parṣada iti punareva kaṇṭhe pañcabandhanabaddhamātmānaṃ saṃjānīte / yadā punarna kvacid gantuṃ śaśāka tadā bhagavato 'ntike trāṇaśaraṇacittamutpādayāmāsa / punarmuktamatmānaṃ saṃjānīte yavat saptakṛtvo baddhamuktamātmānaṃ saṃjānīte sma tatraiva niṣaṇṇaḥ /
body.translated_text: When <s>Māra</s> the Evil One went for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, with words of contentment, he then perceived himself to be freed. But when this thought arose in him—'Let me leave this assembly'—once again he perceived himself bound at the neck with five bonds. When he was unable to go anywhere, then he generated a mind of protection and refuge toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Again he perceived himself freed. Thus seven times he perceived himself bound and freed, while remaining seated there.

body.text: iti mahāsannipātaratnaketusūtre tṛtīyo māradamana-parivartaḥ samāptaḥ // 3 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the third chapter, the <s>Māradamana</s> (Subjugation of <s>Māra</s>), in the <s>Mahāsannipātaratnaketusūtra</s>. //3//

body.text: START Rkp 4
body.translated_text: START <s>Rkp</s> 4

body.text: caturthaḥ parivartaḥ
body.translated_text: Fourth Chapter

body.text: yāvat pūrvoktam / te catvāro mahāśrāvakastadrājagṛhaṃ mahānagaraṃ piṇḍāya praviśantastairmārakumārakairanācāreṇādhyatiṣṭhan nartasva śramaṇa gāyasva śramaṇeti / taiśca mahāśrāvakairvīthimadhye pradhāvadbhirnirvāṇamārgapadapratisaṃyuktena gītasvareṇa yadā cemā gāthā bhāṣitā tadā mahāpṛthivī pracakampe / tatkṣaṇaṃ bahūni devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragaśatasahasrāṇi bhagavacchāsanābhiprasannāni sāśrumukhānyevamāhuḥ /
body.translated_text: As previously described: those four great <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) entered the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms, and those sons of <s>Māra</s> harassed them with misconduct, [saying:] 'Dance, ascetic! Sing, ascetic!' When those great <s>śrāvakas</s>, running through the middle of the street, uttered these verses in a singing voice connected with the words of the path to <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the great earth trembled. At that instant, many hundreds of thousands of <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>, filled with faith in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching, with tearful faces spoke thus:

children.translated_text: May the excellent charioteer of the <s>Dharma</s> remain free from grief! For this is the state of the teaching of the Victor supreme.

children.text: tacchrāvakāṇāṃ janatāmadya dṛṣṭvā vijṛmbhitaṃ kena manaḥ prasādayet // Rkp_4.1 //
children.translated_text: Having seen today the display of his disciples among the people, who would not have their minds inspired with faith? //<s>Rkp</s> 4.1//

body.text: atha tāni bahūni devanāgayakṣarākṣakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi sāśrumukhāni yena bhagavāstena upajagmuḥ / upetya bhagavataḥ purataḥ sthitvā evamāhuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then those many billions and tens of billions and hundreds of thousands of <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, and <s>rākṣasas</s>, with tearful faces, went to where the <s>Bhagavān</s> was. Having approached and standing before the <s>Bhagavān</s>, they spoke thus:

children.translated_text: O <s>Bhagavān</s>, seeing the present state of this teaching,
Do not be indifferent, O Omniscient One, to the protection of the conduct of the teaching! //<s>Rkp</s> 4.2//

body.text: bhagavānāha /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

children.text: eṣa gatvā svayaṃ tatra māraṃ jitvā savāhanam /
children.translated_text: Having gone there myself and conquered <s>Māra</s> together with his forces,
I shall make all the people travelers toward the city of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. //<s>Rkp</s> 4.3//

body.text: atha te sarva evaikakaṇṭhenaivamāhuḥ / mā bhagavan gaccha / nanūktaṃ bhagavatā acintyo buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ buddhaviṣayo 'cintyo māraviṣayaḥ acintyo nāgaviṣayaḥ acintyaḥ karmaṇāṃ karmaviṣaya iti sarvaviṣayāṇāṃ buddhaviṣaya eva viśiṣṭataraḥ / śakto bhagavānihaivāsane niṣaṇṇo mārakoṭīnayutāni parājetuṃ dharmaskandhakoṭīnayutāni prakāśayituṃ kleśasāgaramucchoṣayituṃ dṛṣṭijālaṃ samuddharttuṃ sattvakoṭīnayutāni jñānasāgare 'vatārayitum / nādya bhagavato gamanakālo yuktaḥ / bhagavānāha / yāvantaḥ sattvadhātau sattvāste sarve mārā bhaveyuḥ yāvanti ca pṛthivīparamāṇurajāṃsi tāvantyekaikasya mārabalādhiṣṭhānāni bhaveyuḥ / te sarve mama vadhāya parākrameyuḥ / romakūpamapi me na śaktā vighātayitum / śaktaśca ahamihaiva niṣaṇṇo mārakoṭīnayutāni parājetuṃ sthāpyainaṃ saparivāraṃ māram / gamiṣyāmi punarahaṃ yanmama pūjākarmaṇe [e]bhirmāraiḥ sarvarājagṛhaṃ mahānagaraṃ mārabalardhi[vi]kurvaṇādhiṣṭhānavyūhairalaṃkṛtaṃ tadanukampāyai parimokṣāya yatte mārāḥ paramaprītiprasādajātāḥ kuśalamūlabījamavaropayiṣyanti anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau /
body.translated_text: Then all of them, with one voice, spoke thus: Do not go, O <s>Bhagavān</s>! Did not the <s>Bhagavān</s> say: 'Inconceivable is the <s>Buddha</s>-domain of the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavāns</s>; inconceivable is <s>Māra</s>'s domain; inconceivable is the <s>nāga</s>-domain; inconceivable is the domain of <s>karmas</s>' — yet among all domains, the <s>Buddha</s>-domain alone is the most distinguished. The <s>Bhagavān</s> is able, while seated right here on this seat, to defeat billions and tens of billions of <s>Māras</s>, to illuminate billions and tens of billions of <s>Dharma</s>-aggregates, to dry up the ocean of afflictions, to pull up the net of wrong views, and to guide billions and tens of billions of beings into the ocean of knowledge. Today is not the appropriate time for the <s>Bhagavān</s> to go. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Even if all beings in the realm of beings were to become <s>Māras</s>, and each one had as many bases of <s>Māra</s>'s power as there are atoms of dust in the earth, and all of them were to exert themselves for my destruction—they could not harm even a single pore of my body. And I am able, seated right here, to defeat billions and tens of billions of <s>Māras</s>—to say nothing of this <s>Māra</s> with his retinue. But I shall go, because those <s>Māras</s> who have adorned the entire great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> with the display of <s>Māra</s>'s power, supernatural abilities, and miraculous arrays, as an act of worship toward me—out of compassion for their liberation, those <s>Māras</s> who have generated supreme joy and faith shall plant the seed of roots of merit directed toward unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text: yadā ca bhagavān āsanādutthātukāmaḥ atha tāvadeva prabhāvaśobhanā nāma veṇuvana-paripālikā devatā sā bhagavataḥ purato 'śrumukhī sthitvaivamāha /
body.translated_text: When the <s>Bhagavān</s> wished to rise from his seat, at that very moment a deity named <s>Prabhāvaśobhanā</s>, the guardian of the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove), stood before the <s>Bhagavān</s> with a tearful face and spoke thus:

children.text: naivādya kālo bhagavan praveṣṭuṃ puraṃ samantādiha māra-pūrṇam /
children.translated_text: Today is not the time, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, to enter the city, which is entirely filled with <s>Māras</s> on all sides.

children.text: ekaika evaṃ paramapracaṇḍaḥ koṭīvṛtastiṣṭhati vādisiṃhaḥ // Rkp_4.4 //
children.translated_text: Each one, supremely fierce, stands surrounded by tens of millions, O lion among debaters! //<s>Rkp</s> 4.4//
Blazing with hatred, bearing sharp weapons, they stand with agitated minds, ready for slaughter.

children.text: mā sarvathādya praviśasva nātha mā saṃkṣayaṃ yāsyasi lokabandho // Rkp_4.5 //
children.translated_text: Do not enter by any means today, O Lord! May you not go to destruction, O kinsman of the world! //<s>Rkp</s> 4.5//

body.text: yadā ca bhagavānāsanādabhyutthitastadā dyutimatirnāma vihāradevatā sā bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandyaivamāha /
body.translated_text: When the <s>Bhagavān</s> rose from his seat, a deity of the monastery named <s>Dyutimati</s> bowed her head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and spoke thus:

children.translated_text: Five thousand of the Evil Ones stand armed,

children.text: tvāṃ pratīkṣanti nistriṃśā vraja mādya mahāmune // Rkp_4.6 //
children.translated_text: Waiting for you with drawn swords—do not go today, O Great Sage! //<s>Rkp</s> 4.6//

body.text: yadā bhagavān vihārād viniścakrame tadā siddhamatirnāmauṣadhi] devatā sā bhagavatāḥ pādau śirasābhivandyaivamāha /
body.translated_text: When the <s>Bhagavān</s> stepped out of the monastery, a deity of medicinal plants named <s>Siddhamati</s> bowed her head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and spoke thus:

children.text: hā kaṣṭaṃ naśyate mārgo dharmanetrī pralujyate /
children.translated_text: Alas, the path is being destroyed! The guiding eye of the <s>Dharma</s> is being torn apart!

children.text: dharmanauryāti saṃbhedaṃ lokadīpe kṣayaṃ gate // Rkp_4.7 //
children.translated_text: The ship of <s>Dharma</s> goes to ruin, when the lamp of the world is heading to destruction! //<s>Rkp</s> 4.7//
The noble essence of <s>Dharma</s> is declining throughout the world,
This world is overfilled with fierce and deceitful afflictions.

children.text: nanu mama bhuvi śaktiḥ kācidasti pralopaṃ
children.translated_text: Is there not some power of mine on earth to somehow
Prevent the destruction of the supreme sages, the <s>Sugatas</s>? //<s>Rkp</s> 4.8//
Exceedingly numerous here, for your destruction, are the terrifying ones,
Standing with sharp, rough swords, of evil nature.
O <s>Sugata</s>, heed my command for the protection of the world—

children.text: praviśa daśabalādya mā puraṃ siddhyātra // Rkp_4.9 //
children.translated_text: Enter not the city today, O one of the Ten Powers! May there be success here! //<s>Rkp</s> 4.9//

body.text: atha bhagavān vihārāṅganādabhipratasthe / dyutindharā ca nāma tatra vṛkṣadevatā sā karuṇakaruṇaṃ rudantī bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandyaivamāha /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> set forth from the courtyard of the monastery. And a tree-deity there named <s>Dyutindharā</s>, weeping piteously, bowed her head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and spoke thus:

children.text: sarvaṃ nātha bhaviṣyati tribhuvanaṃ naṣṭekṣaṇaṃ sāmprataṃ
children.translated_text: All the three worlds, O Lord, will now become blind,

children.text: nāśaṃ pūrṇamanorathe tvayi gate sarvārthasiddhe munau /
children.translated_text: When you, the Sage who fulfills all purposes, depart and all cherished wishes are destroyed.
In this sky, with serpent-tongues and sharp swords, arrows, and weapons,

children.text: tvannāśāya caranti vanhivadanā mā gaccha tatrādhunā // Rkp_4.10 //
children.translated_text: They roam with fire-faces for your destruction—do not go there now! //<s>Rkp</s> 4.10//

body.text: yadā ca bhagavān dvārakoṣṭhake avatatāra atha jyotivaraṇā
body.translated_text: When the <s>Bhagavān</s> descended into the gatehouse, then a deity of the gatehouse named <s>Jyotivaraṇā</s>,

body.text: nāma dvārakoṣṭhakadevatā sā uccaiḥsvareṇa rudantī bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandyaivamāha /
body.translated_text: crying out in a loud voice, bowed her head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and spoke thus:

children.translated_text: These twenty thousand in the foremost city, bearing the designation of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>,
With blazing faces, razor-edged projectiles as weapons—they watch mercilessly.
Another twenty thousand, exceedingly fierce and merciless toward each other,

children.text: tiṣṭhantyeha vināśanāya tava he mā gaccha śuddhānana // Rkp_4.11 //
children.translated_text: Stand here for your destruction—O one of pure face, do not go! //<s>Rkp</s> 4.11//

body.text: atha bhagavān dvāraśālāṃ praviveśa / tatra ca tamālasārā nāma rājagṛhanagaraparipālikā devatā / sā ca tasyoccasvareṇa rudantī bhagavataḥ sakāśaṃ tvarayopajagāma / upetya pādau śirasābhivandya evamāha /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> entered the gate-hall. And there, a deity named <s>Tamālasārā</s>, the guardian of the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, crying out in a loud voice, hastened to the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence. Having approached, she bowed her head at his feet and spoke thus:

children.translated_text: This road, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is surrounded by lions, camels, and maddened elephants.

children.text: bhikṣūṇāṃ ca viheṭhanāya bahudhā mārairvighātaḥ kṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: And the <s>Māras</s> have caused manifold harm for the affliction of the <s>bhikṣus</s>.
And the followers of other <s>tīrthas</s> (sects) are determined upon the earth for the slaughter of the Teacher—

children.text: tva meghasvana devanāgakṛpayā mā gaccha dīptaprabha // Rkp_4.12 //
children.translated_text: O you of thunder-voice, by the compassion of <s>devas</s> and <s>nāgas</s>, do not go, O one of blazing radiance! //<s>Rkp</s> 4.12//
Having seen the destruction wrought upon your teaching, the lords of humans, gods, serpents, and <s>kinnaras</s>,
Having come together, flee in fear.
O <s>Bhagavān</s>, conqueror of <s>Māra</s>, the <s>Māras</s>
Enveloped in illusion, with exceedingly hostile faces, [stand ready] once more. //<s>Rkp</s> 4.13//

body.text:
saddharmasya vilopanāṃ ca mahatīṃ lokasya copaplavaṃ
nakṣatradyutināśitaṃ ca gaganaṃ candrārkayorvibhramam /
body.translated_text: The great destruction of the true <s>Dharma</s>, and the calamity of the world, the sky with stars' light extinguished, and the confusion of the moon and sun—

body.text: saṃpaśyan vata sajjano 'dya virasaḥ proccaiḥ śirastāḍito
body.translated_text: Seeing this today, the good person, dispirited, struck hard on the head, cries out,

body.text: hā kaṣṭaṃ kathayatyatīva svagatabhraṃśaṃ samāśaṅkayan // Rkp_4.14 //
body.translated_text: 'Alas, how terrible!'—fearing greatly the loss of his own welfare. //<s>Rkp</s> 4.14//

children.translated_text: This visible sun is being destroyed; the torch of <s>Dharma</s> goes to extinction.

children.text: mṛgdāti mṛtyu saṃbuddhaṃ dharmatoyaṃ viśuṣyate // Rkp_4.15 //
children.translated_text: Death seizes the <s>Saṃbuddha</s> (Fully Awakened One); the water of <s>Dharma</s> is drying up. //<s>Rkp</s> 4.15//
When the destruction of those who practice the true <s>Dharma</s> in the world is at hand,
Then indeed the appearance of the wicked <s>Māras</s> comes about. //<s>Rkp</s> 4.16//

body.text: atha sā devatā bhagavataḥ pratinivartanamadṛṣṭvā sāśrumukhībhūya evamāha /
body.translated_text: Then that deity, seeing that the <s>Bhagavān</s> would not turn back, with a tearful face spoke thus:

children.text: lokaṃ nirīkṣasva muneḥ samagraṃ na gaccha vādipravarādya saṃkṣayam /
children.translated_text: Look upon the entire world, O Sage! Do not go to destruction today, O foremost of debaters!

children.text: ma matpure nāśamupāgate tvayi trilokanindyā satataṃ bhaveyam // Rkp_4.17 //
children.translated_text: With you going to destruction in my city, may I not forever be condemned by the three worlds! //<s>Rkp</s> 4.17//

children.text: śṛṇu me vaco nāyaka sattvasāra mā matpure gaccha vināśamadya /
children.translated_text: Hear my words, O Leader, essence of beings! Do not go to destruction in my city today!
Wait here out of compassion for beings, and liberate beings from the fear and suffering of birth! //<s>Rkp</s> 4.18//

children.text: smara pratijñāṃ hi purā tathāgatā prāpyottamaṃ tārayitā bhaveyam /
children.translated_text: Remember the vow made long ago by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>: 'Having attained the supreme, I shall become a deliverer.'

children.text: sattvānanekān bahuduḥkhataptān āśvāsaya prāṇabhṛtāṃ variṣṭha // Rkp_4.19 //
children.translated_text: Console the many beings tormented by great suffering, O best among the living! //<s>Rkp</s> 4.19//

children.text: tiṣṭhāgramūrte bahukalpakoṭyaḥ kāmeṣu sakto vata bālavargaḥ /
children.translated_text: Remain for many billions of <s>kalpas</s> (eons), O one of supreme form! The foolish multitude is indeed attached to sensual pleasures.
For their pacification, teach the path of <s>Dharma</s>—the meaning of the sense-faculties and their objects as empty by nature. //<s>Rkp</s> 4.20//

body.text: tato bhagavān dvāraśālāyāmavatatāra / atha tāvadeva dṛḍhā nāma pṛthivī devatā daśabhirmahaujaskamahaujaskābhirdevatāsahasraiḥ sārdham aśrumukhī prakīrṇakeśī bhagavataḥ purataḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitvaivamāha /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> descended from the gate-hall. At that very moment, an earth-deity named <s>Dṛḍhā</s>, together with ten thousand exceedingly powerful deities, stood before the <s>Bhagavān</s> with tearful face, disheveled hair, and palms joined, and spoke thus:

children.text: smara pradhānaṃ rudhiraprapūrṇā yatte pradattāścaturāḥ samudrāḥ /
children.translated_text: Remember the great exertion—the four oceans filled with blood that you gave,

children.text: śirāṃsi cāsthīni ca cakravāḍavaṃ netrāṇi gaṅgāsikatāsamāni // Rkp_4.21 //
children.translated_text: And heads and bones [filling] the ring of <s>Cakravāḍa</s> mountains, and eyes as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>! //<s>Rkp</s> 4.21//

body.text: ratnāni caivaṃ vividhāni pūrvaṃ putrāśca dārāśca dviradāstathāśvāḥ / āvāsavastraśayanānnapānaṃ bhaiṣajyamiṣṭaṃ ca tathāturāṇām // Rkp_4.22 //
body.translated_text: And various treasures formerly [given], and sons and wives, and elephants and horses, and lodging, clothing, bedding, food and drink, and cherished medicine for the sick. //<s>Rkp</s> 4.22//

children.text: kṛtā ca pūjā pravarā svayambhuvāṃ śīlaṃ tvayā rakṣitamapramādinā /
children.translated_text: And supreme worship was made to the Self-Arisen Ones; morality was guarded by you without negligence.

children.text: kṣāntiśrutaṃ sevitameva nityaṃ mātṛjñatā caiva pitṛjñatā ca // Rkp_4.23 //
children.translated_text: Patience and learning were always cultivated, along with gratitude toward mother and father. //<s>Rkp</s> 4.23//

children.text: jīrṇānyanantāni ca duṣkarāṇi sattvā hyanekavyasanāt pramocitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Innumerable and endless difficult deeds were performed; beings were liberated from manifold calamities.

children.text: yatpūrvamādau praṇidhiḥ kṛttaste buddho bhaveyaṃ paramārthadeśakaḥ // Rkp_4.24 //
children.translated_text: The vow that you made at the very beginning: 'May I become a <s>Buddha</s>, a teacher of the ultimate truth'— //<s>Rkp</s> 4.24//

children.text: uttārayeyaṃ janatāṃ mahaughāt lokāya dharmaṃ vata deśayeyam /
children.translated_text: 'I shall deliver the people from the great flood; I shall teach the <s>Dharma</s> to the world.'

children.text: tṛṣṇādhimūlāni mahābhayāni duḥkhānyaśeṣāṇi ca śoṣayeyam // Rkp_4.25 //
children.translated_text: 'The great fears rooted in <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) and all sufferings without exception—I shall dry them up.' //<s>Rkp</s> 4.25//

children.text: abhaye pure sattvagaṇaṃ praveśaye niveśya tān vai varabodhimārge /
children.translated_text: 'I shall cause the multitude of beings to enter the city of fearlessness; having established them on the noble path to awakening,'

children.text: vimocayeyaṃ bahuduḥkhapīḍitān tāṃ sattvadhātuṃ paripūrṇa kuryām // Rkp_4.26 //
children.translated_text: 'I shall liberate those oppressed by great suffering; I shall fulfill that realm of beings.' //<s>Rkp</s> 4.26//

body.text: mārgandhurāṇāmiha pāpacāriṇāṃ kṣamasva nātha śrutaśīlanāśinām /
body.translated_text: Forgive, O Lord, the evildoing <s>Māra</s>-leaders here, the destroyers of learning and morality.

body.text: nistārayaitāṃ samayapratijñāṃ vadasva dharmaṃ bahu kalpakoṭyaḥ // Rkp_4.27 //
body.translated_text: Deliver them! Fulfill this vow and promise! Teach the <s>Dharma</s> for many billions of <s>kalpas</s>! //<s>Rkp</s> 4.27//

children.text: oghāt samuttāraya nātha lokaṃ saṃsnāpayāṣṭāṅgajalena cainam /
children.translated_text: O Lord, deliver the world from the flood! Bathe it with the water of the Eightfold [Path]!

children.text: nehāsti sattvāḥ sadṛśāstriloke tvayā hi nātha pravaro na kaścit // Rkp_4.28 //
children.translated_text: There are no beings in the three worlds equal to you; no one, O Lord, is superior to you! //<s>Rkp</s> 4.28//

children.text: muktaḥ svayaṃ lokamimaṃ ca mocaya uttāraya [tvaṃ] tribhavārṇavājjagat /
children.translated_text: Liberated yourself, liberate this world too! Deliver the world from the ocean of the three realms of existence!

children.text: tvamekabandho jagadekabāndhava- stiṣṭhasva nityaṃ vibhajasva dharmam // Rkp_4.29 //
children.translated_text: You are the sole kinsman of the world, the sole friend of the world—remain forever and distribute the <s>Dharma</s>! //<s>Rkp</s> 4.29//

body.text: atha bhagavān dvāraśālāyāmavatatāra / tatkṣaṇādeva ca bahūni devanāgayakṣarākṣasakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi gagane vicaramāṇāni sāśrumukhānyevamāhuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> descended from the gate-hall. At that very instant, many billions and tens of billions and hundreds of thousands of <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, and <s>rākṣasas</s>, moving about in the sky, with tearful faces spoke thus:

children.text: asmābhirādau sugatā hi dṛṣṭā praśāntakāle suvinītaśiṣyāḥ /
children.translated_text: We first beheld the <s>Sugatas</s> in the time of peace, with well-disciplined disciples.

children.text: dharmopadeśaṃ vipulaṃ ca kurvatāṃ teṣāṃ vighāto na sa īdṛśo 'bhūt // Rkp_4.30 //
children.translated_text: and no such obstacle arose for those who were giving vast <s>Dharma</s> teachings. // Rkp_4.30 //

body.text: eṣo hi śāstātinihīnakāle prāptaḥ svayambhūtvamudārabuddhiḥ /
body.translated_text: For this Teacher, of noble wisdom, has arrived at self-existent (<s>svayambhū</s>) status in this most degenerate age;

body.text: kleśādi dharmaṃ samuvāca loke paripācanārthaṃ jagatāṃ munīndraḥ // Rkp_4.31 //
body.translated_text: the Lord of Sages taught the <s>Dharma</s> beginning with the afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) in the world, for the purpose of ripening beings. // Rkp_4.31 //

children.text: asmin punastiṣṭha hi vādisiṃha pāpīmatāṃ naikasahasrakoṭyaḥ /
children.translated_text: But in this [realm], O lion among debaters, remain! Thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Māra</s> <s>Pāpīmāns</s>

children.text: kurvanti dharmasya vināśamevaṃ mā buddhavīrādya pure viśvasva // Rkp_4.32 //
children.translated_text: are working to destroy the <s>Dharma</s> in this way—do not, O <s>Buddha</s>-hero, enter the city today with trust! // Rkp_4.32 //

body.text: athāparā devatā evamāha /
body.translated_text: Then another deity spoke thus:

children.translated_text: The wheel [of <s>Dharma</s>] was turned in a certain region by those previous <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors), who were devoted to the welfare of the world;

children.text: ayaṃ punargacchatu yatra tatra mā khalvavasthāṃ samavāpsyate 'dya // Rkp_4.33 //
children.translated_text: but let this one go wherever [he will]—may he not come to ruin today! // Rkp_4.33 //

body.text: athāparāpi devatā evamāha /
body.translated_text: Then yet another deity spoke thus:

body.text: kāruṇyahetoriha sārthavāha cacāra sattvārthamatīva kurvan

children.text: sa kevalaṃ tvadya pure 'tra mā vai nāśaṃ prayāyāditi me vitarkaḥ // Rkp_4.34 //
children.translated_text: only now, may he not go to destruction in this city! Such is my apprehension. // Rkp_4.34 //

body.translated_text: Out of compassion, this caravan leader practiced here, doing exceedingly much for the welfare of beings—

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena tāni bahūni devanāgayakṣarākṣasāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi sāśrudinavadanāni
body.translated_text: At that time, those many <s>koṭis</s>, <s>nayutas</s>, hundreds of thousands of gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and <s>Mahoragas</s>, with tearful faces,

body.text: gaganatalapathādavatirya bhagavataḥ purataḥ sthitvā anekaprakārān ātmano viprakārāṃścakruḥ / kecit keśān vilumpanti sma / kecidābharaṇāni mumucuḥ / kecicchatradhvajapatākāḥ prapātayāmāsuḥ / kecit svaśarīreṇa bhūmau nipetuḥ / kecid bhagavataścaraṇau jagṛhuḥ / kecidatikaṣṭaṃ ruruduḥ / kecidurasi pāṇibhiḥ parājaghnuḥ / kecid bhagavataḥ padamūle sthitva madguvat parāvartante sma / kecid bhagavataḥ purataḥ prāñjalayo bhūtvā stutinamaskārān cakruḥ / kecid bhagavantaṃ puṣpadhūgandhamālyavilepanavastrābharaṇasuvarṇasūtramuktāhārapuṣpairavakiranti sma /
body.translated_text: descending from the path of the sky and standing before the Blessed One, showed various kinds of self-affliction. Some tore their hair. Some cast off their ornaments. Some threw down their parasols, banners, and flags. Some fell to the ground with their own bodies. Some grasped the feet of the Blessed One. Some wept most piteously. Some beat their chests with their hands. Some, standing at the feet of the Blessed One, rolled about like fish. Some, standing before the Blessed One with palms joined, offered praises and salutations. Some scattered flowers, incense, fragrances, garlands, unguents, garments, ornaments, gold threads, pearl necklaces, and flowers over the Blessed One.

body.text: athāparā bavhayo devakoṭyaḥ uccairekakaṇṭhenaivamāhuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then many other <s>koṭis</s> of gods said loudly with one voice:

children.text: tvayā pracīrṇāni hi duṣkarāṇi atīva lokārthamito bahūni /
children.translated_text: You have performed exceedingly many difficult deeds from here onward for the sake of the world;

children.text: kṣīṇe tvamutpanna ihādya kāle upekṣakastiṣṭha ca mā tyajasva // Rkp_4.35 //
children.translated_text: arisen now in this time when [merit] has been exhausted, O one of noble wisdom, remain with equanimity—do not abandon [us]! // Rkp_4.35 //
Little of your <s>Buddha</s>-work has been done, O Faultless One, and only a few gods, humans, and women have been made witnesses [to the truth];

children.text: tvaṃ tiṣṭha dharmān suciraṃ prakāśayan uttārayāsmāt tribhavārṇavāj jagat // Rkp_4.36 //
children.translated_text: remain, illuminating the <s>Dharma</s> for a very long time—deliver the world from the ocean of the three realms of existence! // Rkp_4.36 //

body.text: sattvā hyaneke śubhakarmacāriṇaḥ paripakvabījā amṛtasya bhājanāḥ /
body.translated_text: Truly, many beings of virtuous conduct, with ripened seeds, are vessels of the nectar [of <s>Dharma</s>];

body.text: karuṇāṃ janasya pratidarśayātha oghebhya uttāraya lokanātha // Rkp_4.37 //
body.translated_text: show compassion to these people and deliver them from the floods, O Lord of the World! // Rkp_4.37 //

children.translated_text: Those who wander here, lost in the midst of the wilderness, whose path is lost in the jungle of <s>saṃsāra</s>—
show them their own path and liberate them with the words of the noble, supreme <s>Dharma</s>! // Rkp_4.38 //
This most wondrous and marvelous [deed] of compassion—that the excellent <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of Dharma) was set in motion—

children.text: ciraṃ hi tiṣṭha tvamudārabuddhe mā khalvanāthā janatā bhavet // Rkp_4.39 //
children.translated_text: remain for a long time, O one of noble wisdom! May the people not become orphaned [without a protector]! // Rkp_4.39 //

body.text: athāparāpi devatā evamāha /
body.translated_text: Then yet another deity spoke thus:

body.text: nāśaṃ prayāsyatyatha yadvināyako lokastathāndho nikhilo bhaviṣyati / aṣṭāṅgamārgastrivimokṣahetoḥ sarveṇa sarvaṃ na bhaviṣyatīha // Rkp_4.40 //
body.translated_text: If the Guide were to pass away, the entire world would become blind; the Eightfold Noble Path, the cause of the three liberations—all of it would altogether cease to exist here. // Rkp_4.40 //

children.translated_text: By us, a virtuous seed has been sown in you—exert your body and mind diligently!

children.text: tato vayaṃ sarvasukhaiḥ samanvitāḥ puṇyākarasyāsya hi mā bhavet kṣayaḥ // Rkp_4.41 //
children.translated_text: So that we may be endowed with all happiness—may there be no exhaustion of this mine of merit! // Rkp_4.41 //

body.text: tena ca samayena bahūni śuddhāvāsadevakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi tatraiva sannipatitānyabhūvan / tānyapyevamāhuḥ /
body.translated_text: At that time, many <s>koṭis</s>, <s>nayutas</s>, hundreds of thousands of <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abode) gods had assembled right there. They too spoke thus:

children.text: mā bhaiṣṭaṃ yūyaṃ na muneravasthā bhaviṣyati kācidudārabuddheḥ /
children.translated_text: Do not fear, all of you! No calamity will befall this Sage of noble wisdom;

children.text: pratyakṣapūrvā vayamasya sādhorūpāgatā yadbhuvi mārakoṭyaḥ // Rkp_4.42 //
children.translated_text: we have previously witnessed directly when <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Māras</s> came to this virtuous one on the earth. // Rkp_4.42 //
Leaping thirty-six <s>yojanas</s> with fierce momentum, spread out in all directions,
the terrifying army of <s>Māra</s>, resounding with abundant spears, swords, sharp [weapons], and fearsome cries—
having arrived at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, was instantly reduced to ruin, overcome with fear.

children.text: prāptārthasyādya kiṃ tatprasṛtayaśaso vighnameva prakuryāt // Rkp_4.43 //
children.translated_text: Now that he has accomplished his purpose and his fame has spread, what obstacle could there be? // Rkp_4.43 //

body.text: athāparā devatā prarudantī evamāha /
body.translated_text: Then another deity, weeping, spoke thus:

children.translated_text: That army which came before belonged to a single <s>Māra</s>, and was of great power;
but this army belongs to thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Māras</s> and is of great power! // Rkp_4.44 //
Without doubt, the Guide of the World has here come to destruction;
if he is destroyed, this world will wander without light. // Rkp_4.45 //

body.text: atha khalu te śakrabrahmalokapālā bhagavataḥ [pādau parivajyaiva]māhuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the World-Protectors (<s>Lokapālas</s>), embracing the feet of the Blessed One, spoke thus:

children.translated_text: Remain here, be gracious to those of dull understanding, [heed] our words, O foremost in compassion!

children.text: bahudevakoṭyo mahāśoka taptāstāḥ sāṃprataṃ dharmarasena siñca // Rkp_4.46 //
children.translated_text: Many <s>koṭis</s> of gods are burning with great grief—sprinkle them now with the nectar of <s>Dharma</s>! // Rkp_4.46 //

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstāṃ sarvāvatīṃ parṣadaṃ maitryā viśālabhyāṃ nayanābhyām avalokya brāhmeṇa svareṇa tāṃ samāśvāsayannevamāha /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, surveying that entire assembly with his eyes wide with <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), consoled them and spoke thus in a <s>Brahma</s>-voice:

children.text: mā bhaiṣṭa yūyaṃ bhavatādya nirbhayāḥ sarve 'pi mārāḥ sagaṇāḥ savāhanāḥ /
children.translated_text: Do not fear! Be fearless now, all of you! All the <s>Māras</s>, together with their hosts and vehicles,

children.text: śaktā na me bhīṣayituṃ samagrāḥ romāpyathaikaṃ kimu sarvadeham // Rkp_4.47 //
children.translated_text: are not able to frighten me even when assembled—not even a single hair, let alone the entire body! // Rkp_4.47 //

children.text: āśvāsayāmyadya tu sarvalokaṃ dharmaṃ sadāhaṃ bhuvi deśayiṣye /
children.translated_text: I shall now reassure the entire world; I shall always teach the <s>Dharma</s> on this earth.

children.text: mārgacyutānāmahameva samyag mārgopadeśaṃ viśadaṃ kariṣye // Rkp_4.48 //
children.translated_text: For those who have strayed from the path, I alone shall properly give the clear teaching of the path. // Rkp_4.48 //

children.text: kṛtāni pūrvaṃ bahu duṣkarāṇi mayānnapānaṃ vipulaṃ pradattam /
children.translated_text: Many difficult deeds were performed by me before; abundant food and drink were given;

children.text: āvāsabhaiṣajyamanalpakaṃ ca kartuṃ vighātaṃ mama ko 'dya śakyate // Rkp_4.49 //
children.translated_text: and no small amount of shelter and medicine—who now is able to cause me obstruction? // Rkp_4.49 //

children.text: tyaktā maya hyaśvarathā gajāśca vibhūṣaṇānyābharaṇāni caiva /
children.translated_text: Horses, chariots, and elephants were given up by me, as well as ornaments and adornments;

children.text: dāsāśca dāsyo nigamāśca rāṣṭrāḥ kartuṃ vighātaṃ mama kaḥ samarthaḥ // Rkp_4.50 //
children.translated_text: servants male and female, market-towns, and kingdoms—who is able to cause me obstruction? // Rkp_4.50 //

body.text: bhāryā sutā duhitṛ kalatravargamaiśvaryamiṣṭaṃ bhuvi rājavaṃśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Wives, sons, daughters, the entire household, cherished sovereignty, a royal lineage on earth—

body.text: datto mayā sattvahitāya kasmāccharīranāśo 'dya bhaviṣyati me // Rkp_4.51 //
body.translated_text: these were given by me for the welfare of beings; how then could destruction of my body occur today? // Rkp_4.51 //

children.text: śiraśca netre ubhe karṇanāse hastau ca pādau tanu carma lohitam /
children.translated_text: My head, both eyes, ears, nose, hands, feet, body, skin, and blood—

children.text: svajīvitaṃ tyaktamapīha dehināṃ kartuṃ vihiṃsāṃ mama kaḥ samarthaḥ // Rkp_4.52 //
children.translated_text: even my own life was given up for embodied beings here—who is able to harm me? // Rkp_4.52 //

children.text: bavhayo mayātīva hi buddhakoṭyaḥ saṃpūjitā bhaktimatā sahastam /
children.translated_text: Exceedingly many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> were worshiped by me with devoted hands;

children.text: śīlaśrutikṣāntiratena nityaṃ kartuṃ vilopaṃ mamaḥ samarthaḥ // Rkp_4.53 //
children.translated_text: by one who is always devoted to morality, learning, and patience—who is able to corrupt [my teaching]? // Rkp_4.53 //

children.text: pūrvaṃ mayā vai bahu duṣkarāṇi kṛtāni me 'tīva samāhitena /
children.translated_text: Many difficult deeds were performed by me before with exceedingly concentrated [mind];

children.text: saṃchinnagātreṇa na roṣitaṃ manaḥ kartuṃ vihiṃsāṃ mama ko 'dya śaktaḥ // Rkp_4.54 //
children.translated_text: even with limbs severed, my mind was not angered—who is able to harm me today? // Rkp_4.54 //

children.text: kleśā jitā me nitayo 'smi buddhaḥ sarveṣu sattveṣu ca maitracittaḥ /
children.translated_text: The afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>) have been conquered by me; I am eternally a <s>Buddha</s>, with a mind of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) toward all beings;

children.text: īrṣyā ca me nāsti khilaṃ na roṣo na me samarthaḥ purato 'dya kaścit // Rkp_4.55 //
children.translated_text: I have no envy, no rigidity, no anger—no one is able to stand before me today! // Rkp_4.55 //

body.text: jitaṃ mayā mārabalaṃ samagraṃ parājitā me bahu mārakoṭyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The entire force of <s>Māra</s> has been conquered by me; many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Māras</s> have been defeated by me.

body.text: yuṣmadvimokṣa niyataṃ kariṣye mā bhaiṣṭa kasmānna puraṃ pravekṣepa // Rkp_4.56 //
body.translated_text: I shall certainly accomplish your liberation—do not fear! Why would I not enter the city? // Rkp_4.56 //

children.text: ye keci diśāsu daśaśvapīha buddhā hi tiṣṭhanti tu sattvahetoḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>Buddhas</s> abide in the ten directions here for the sake of beings—
I shall invite all those <s>Buddhas</s> here, and also the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of great supernatural power! // Rkp_4.57 //

children.text: kṣetraṃ prapūrṇaṃ sakalaṃ kariṣye jñānena puṇyena ca vāsayiṣye /
children.translated_text: I shall fill this entire <s>kṣetra</s> (field) completely and permeate it with wisdom and merit;

children.text: taireva buddhaiḥ saha netṛsaṃsthitaḥ kariṣye buddhānumataṃ ca kāryam // Rkp_4.58 //
children.translated_text: together with those very <s>Buddhas</s>, standing as a guide, I shall accomplish the work approved by the <s>Buddhas</s>. // Rkp_4.58 //

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayenāprameyāsaṃkhyeyāni devanāgayakṣarākṣasāsura-garuḍa-kinnara-mahoraga-manuṣyāmanuṣya-koṭīnayuta-śatasahasrāṇi bhagavate sādhukāraṃ pradaduḥ / evaṃ cāhuḥ / nama āścaryādbhutāsaṃkhyeyavīryasamanvāgatāya / namo namo mahāścaryasamanvāgatāya buddhāya bhagavate / āśvāsito bhagavatā sadevako lokaḥ parājito bhagavatā mārapakṣaḥ vidhūtaṃ sattvānāṃ sandhikleśakāluṣyam / prahāṇaḥ sattvānāṃ mānaparvataḥ / chinno janmavṛkṣaḥ / vicūrṇito
body.translated_text: At that time, immeasurable, incalculable <s>koṭis</s>, <s>nayutas</s>, hundreds of thousands of gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, humans, and non-humans gave their applause to the Blessed One and spoke thus: 'Homage to the one endowed with wondrous, marvelous, incalculable vigor! Homage, homage to the <s>Buddha</s> Blessed One, endowed with great wonder!' The world with its gods was consoled by the Blessed One. The faction of <s>Māra</s> was defeated by the Blessed One. The defilement of the latent afflictions of beings was shaken off. The mountain of pride of beings was demolished. The tree of birth was cut down. The sun of

body.text: mṛtyusūryaḥ / vidhūto 'vidyāndhakāraḥ / prasāditā anyatīrthyāḥ / saṃśoṣitāścatvāra oghāḥ / prajvālitā[ni] dharmolkāni / darśito bodhimārgaḥ / niyojitaḥ kṣāntisauratye / krīḍāpito dhyānasaukhye / avabodhitāni cattvāryāryasatyāni / samuttārito bhagavatā mahākāruṇikena śāstrā janmasamudrāt sadevako lokaḥ / praveśitāḥ sattvā abhayapuram /
body.translated_text: death was pulverized. The darkness of ignorance was dispelled. The non-Buddhist teachers were converted. The four floods were dried up. The torches of <s>Dharma</s> were kindled. The path to awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) was shown. [Beings] were engaged in patience and gentleness (<s>kṣāntisauratya</s>). [They were] made to delight in the bliss of meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>). The Four Noble Truths (<s>catvāryāryasatyāni</s>) were awakened to. The world with its gods was delivered from the ocean of birth by the Blessed One, the greatly compassionate Teacher. Beings were led into the city of fearlessness.

body.text: atha te devamanuṣyā nānāpuṣpadhūpagandhamālyālaṃkāravibhūṣaṇairbhagavantamabhyarcayitvā bhagavato 'rthāya te mārgaṃ śobhayāmāsuḥ / divyavastrapuṣpaduṣyaiśca bhagavantaṃ saṃcchādayanti sma / divyaiśca māndārava-māhāmāndārava-pārūṣaka-mahāpārūṣaka-mañjūṣaka-roca-mahārocotpalakumudapuṇḍarīkaiḥ saṃcchādayāmāsuḥ / yatra bhagavān tau caraṇau niścikṣepa tasmiṃśca mārge ubhayoḥ pārśvayoḥ divyān saptaratnamayān vṛkṣān abhinirmīya divyavastraduṣyahastakarṇaśīrṣābharaṇairalaṃcakruḥ / teṣu ca vṛkṣāntareṣu divyāṃ puṣkariṇīṃ māpayanti sma / śītasvādūdakaviprasannā anāvilā aṣṭāṅgopetavāriparipūrṇā samantāt saptaratnālaṃkārālaṃkṛtā / antarikṣe ca saptaratnamayāni cchatrāṇi dadhire / dhvajapatākāsuvarṇasūtramuktāhārāṃśca suvarṇacūrṇavarṣāśca vavarṣuḥ / rūpyavaiḍūryacūrṇāgarutagara-candana-kālānusāri-tamālapatravarṣāṇi samutsasarjuḥ / gośīrṣoragasāracandanacūrṇaṃ
body.translated_text: Then those gods and humans, having honored the Blessed One with various flowers, incense, fragrances, garlands, ornaments, and adornments, beautified the path for the sake of the Blessed One. They covered the Blessed One with divine garments and flower-cloths. They covered [the path] with divine <s>Māndārava</s>, great <s>Māndārava</s>, <s>Pārūṣaka</s>, great <s>Pārūṣaka</s>, <s>Mañjūṣaka</s>, <s>Roca</s>, great <s>Roca</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Kumuda</s>, and <s>Puṇḍarīka</s> flowers. Where the Blessed One placed his two feet, on both sides of that path they magically created divine trees made of the seven jewels and adorned them with divine garments, cloths, and ornaments for hands, ears, and head. Between those trees, they conjured divine lotus ponds—cool, sweet, clear, untroubled, filled with water endowed with eight qualities, adorned all around with the seven jewels. And in the sky, they held parasols made of the seven jewels. They rained down banners, flags, gold threads, pearl necklaces, and showers of gold dust. They sent forth showers of silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> [lapis lazuli] powder, <s>agaru</s> [aloe], <s>tagara</s>, sandalwood, dark <s>ānusāri</s> [fragrance], and <s>tamālapatra</s> [cinnamon leaf].

body.text: ca tasmin mārge vavarṣuḥ / suvarṇasūtramuktāhāramaṇimuktābhiśca sarvaṃ gaganatalaṃ nānādivyālaṃkārairalañcakruḥ / tatastasya nagarasya ca bahirdhā devamanuṣyā bhagavataḥ pūjākarmaṇe mārgaśobhāṃ cakrire / antarnagara ca mārā mārapārṣadaśca śobhāvyūhairvyūhamāyāsurbhagavataḥ pūjākarmaṇe /
body.translated_text: And they rained <s>gośīrṣa</s>-<s>uragasāra</s> sandalwood powder on that path. With gold threads, pearl necklaces, gems, and pearls they adorned the entire expanse of the sky with various divine ornaments. Thus, outside that city, gods and humans performed the beautification of the path for the worship of the Blessed One. And within the city, the <s>Māras</s> and <s>Māra</s>'s retinue arranged decorative displays for the worship of the Blessed One.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān tasmin samaye śūraṃgamaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpede / tena ca samādhinā yathā samāpanna eva mārgaṃ jagāma / tena khalu punaḥ samayena nānāvidhaiḥ kāyarūpaliṅgeryāpathairbhagavāṃstaṃ mārgamabhipratasthe / tatra ye sattvā brahmabhaktikā brahmavainayikāste brahmarūpeṇa bhagavantaṃ mārgaṃ vrajantamadrākṣuḥ / yāvad ye śakravainayikā ye nārāyaṇavainayikā ye maheśvaravainayikā ye cāturmahārājavainayikā ye cakravartivainayikā ye koṭṭarājavainayikā ye maharṣivainayikā ye śramaṇavainayikā ye māravainayikā ye strīvainayikā ye siṃhavainayikā ye gajavainayikā ye nāgavainayikā ye asuravainayikā ye śaśabhaktikāḥ śaśavainayikāḥ śaśarūpaliṅgeryāpathena bhagavantaṃ mārgaṃ vrajantamadrākṣuḥ / ye sattvā buddhavainayikāste buddharūpaliṅgeryāpathenaiva bhagavantaṃ mārgaṃ vrajantamadrākṣuḥ / sarve ca te sattvāḥ prāñjalayo bhūtvā samabhiṣṭuvantaḥ namaskurvantaḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhata samanubaddhā jagmuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One at that time entered the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Śūraṅgama</s> (Heroic March). And having entered that <s>samādhi</s>, he proceeded along the path just as he was in that attainment. At that time, the Blessed One set out on that path with various kinds of bodily forms, marks, and deportments. Those beings who were devoted to <s>Brahmā</s> and were to be disciplined by <s>Brahmā</s> saw the Blessed One walking on the path in the form of <s>Brahmā</s>. Likewise, those to be disciplined by <s>Śakra</s>, those to be disciplined by <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, those to be disciplined by <s>Maheśvara</s>, those to be disciplined by the Four Great Kings (<s>Cāturmahārāja</s>), those to be disciplined by a <s>Cakravartin</s>, those to be disciplined by a minor king, those to be disciplined by a great sage (<s>Maharṣi</s>), those to be disciplined by an ascetic (<s>Śramaṇa</s>), those to be disciplined by <s>Māra</s>, those to be disciplined by a woman, those to be disciplined by a lion, those to be disciplined by an elephant, those to be disciplined by a <s>Nāga</s>, those to be disciplined by an <s>Asura</s>, those devoted to a hare and to be disciplined by a hare—they saw the Blessed One walking on the path in the form, marks, and deportment of a hare. Those beings who were to be disciplined by a <s>Buddha</s> saw the Blessed One walking on the path in the very form, marks, and deportment of a <s>Buddha</s>. And all those beings, with palms joined, praising and paying homage, followed along behind [him].

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena yo 'sāvanuhimavannivāsī jyotīraso nāma ṛṣirmāreṇa pāpīmatā udyojitaḥ sa pañcaśataparivāro
body.translated_text: At that time, the sage named <s>Jyotīrasa</s>, who dwelt near the <s>Himavat</s> [Himalayas], had been instigated by <s>Māra</s> <s>Pāpīmān</s>. He, together with his retinue of five hundred,

body.text: rājagṛhasya mahānagaradvārasamīpe pratīkṣya bhagavato rūpaliṅgeryāpathamapaśyat tathā mārge cāsaṃkhyeyā vṛkṣadevatāḥ pūjākarmaṇe udyuktāḥ / dṛṣṭvedaṃ tasyaitadabhavat / satyavādī maharṣirayaṃ mahānubhāvaḥ pūjārhaḥ] / ..... ..... ..... ..... ..... ..... .....
body.translated_text: waiting near the gate of the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, beheld the form, marks, and deportment of the Blessed One, as well as the innumerable tree-deities on the path engaged in worship. Having seen this, it occurred to him: 'This great sage is a speaker of truth, of great supernatural power, worthy of worship.'
