body.text: atha jyotīrasa ṛṣīḥ saparivāro buddharūpaliṅgeryāpathā[nvi]taṃ bhagavantaṃ [dṛṣṭvā pūrvakuśalamūla-sammukhībhūtaḥ]..... / sa ratnaketuṃ nāma bodhisattvasamādhiṃ pratilebhe / yaḥ samādhiḥ bhavatyasaṃhāryaḥ sarvasamāpattibhiḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the sage <s>Jyotīrasa</s> with his retinue, having seen the Blessed One endowed with the form, marks, and deportment of a <s>Buddha</s>, [had his previous good roots activated]. He attained the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Ratnaketu</s> (Jewel-Banner), which is a <s>samādhi</s> that is irreversible by all attainments.

body.text: atha jyotīraso maharṣirbhagavataḥ [purataḥ prāñjalibhūtaḥ puṣpaṃ dattvā stutvā ca] abravit /
body.translated_text: Then the great sage <s>Jyotīrasa</s>, standing before the Blessed One with palms joined, having offered a flower and praised [him], spoke:

children.translated_text: The Lord of the World, of infinite qualities (<s>varṇa</s>), speaker of truth, well-established—
all the world is illuminated by your eye-light of wisdom;
your vigor is always directed toward the welfare of beings, arisen from <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness)—
homage to you today, O leader of essential beings, free from attachment, unobstructed! // Rkp_4.[59] //

body.text:
svarṇavarṇakāñcanābha śītalā[ste aṃśavaḥ
sarvasattva bodhilābha hetuguṇa-yojaka] /
body.translated_text: Of golden hue, with the radiance of gold, your rays are cooling, connecting the qualities and causes for the attainment of <s>bodhi</s> by all beings.

body.text: dharmacakravartanena dhvasta
body.translated_text: By the turning of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of Dharma), the mountains of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) are shattered.

body.text: kleśaparvata
paścimā te caryaniṣṭhā bodhijñānakāraṇam // Rkp_4.[60] //
body.translated_text: The final culmination of your conduct is the cause of the wisdom of <s>bodhi</s>." //4.60//

children.translated_text: "O great physician, essence of beings, adorned with the [thirty-two] marks, for the sake of teaching,
having become a <s>Buddha</s>, O Leader, you are now entreated.

children.text: chindhi me tvaṃ dṛṣṭijālaṃ tīrṇo jagat tāraye
children.translated_text: Cut for me the net of [wrong] views! Having crossed over, ferry the world across!
How soon shall I become a <s>Buddha</s>? Teach me, O Best of Men!" //4.61//
"From the ocean of existence, the flood of beings' suffering, do ferry [them] across,

children.text: nirvāṇa kṣeme ca] mārge sthāpaya nirāsrave /
children.translated_text: and establish [them] on the secure and undefiled path to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.
In the ten directions, those <s>Buddhas</s> too, whose qualities are like an ocean—
to them I make supplication, devoted to <s>bodhicitta</s>." //4.62//
"All beings touched by suffering, by the terrible, the fair, and the harsh—
whatever merit of the three times through body, speech, and mind is mine today,
may beings by that become cool-minded,
and may they attain <s>Nirvāṇa</s> in the eternally secure buddha-field!" //4.63//
"May all beings' diseases depart, may the waters of <s>kleśas</s> dry up!
May they gain wisdom and faculties that are firm by nature.
And those beings afflicted by the suffering of bondage and imprisonment—

children.text: te 'pi kṣipraṃ santu muktā me ca] puṇyatejasā // Rkp_4.[64] //
children.translated_text: may they too be swiftly liberated by the splendor of my merit!" //4.64//
"May each and every being attain ocean-like qualities,
and through wisdom and immeasurable merit, may [they] satisfy all with happiness.
May they attain right view, and may their sins be swiftly shaken off!

children.text: jātismarāḥ sarve santu sattva dharmacāriṇaḥ // Rkp_4.[65] //
children.translated_text: May all beings remember their past lives and practice the <s>Dharma</s>!" //4.65//
"May they cross to the far shore of the ocean of existence for the attainment of the <s>Dharma</s>,
and may I also please the <s>Buddha</s> who has gone to the far shore of all <s>dharmas</s>!" //4.66//
"Remain for immeasurable <s>kalpas</s>, showering the rain of <s>Dharma</s>!
May all beings be bathed with the waters of the <s>Dharma</s>-cloud!" //4.67//
"Whatever transgressions I have committed by body, mind, or speech,
I confess [them]
and entreat the <s>Buddha</s> and <s>Saṃgha</s>, out of reverence for beings." //4.68//
"And I shall never again engage in deeds born of wrong views,
having always seen the inconceivable beings standing before me." //4.69//
"Whatever merit I possess, I dedicate it again to <s>bodhi</s>.

children.text: sarva caryāṃ sattvahetoḥ sarvaduḥkhaṃ samutsahe // Rkp_4.[70] //
children.translated_text: For the sake of beings, I shall endure all suffering through every [kind of] conduct." //4.70//
"I shall establish all beings on the supreme path of <s>bodhi</s>,
and I shall traverse the ocean of wisdom and the <s>kalpas</s> and fields." //4.71//
"May the attainment of the pure touch of <s>bodhi</s> be brought about,
and may he surely stand on the ground of forbearance toward all beings." //4.72//

body.text:
prāpnuyāmabhijñā pañca vādisiṃha[sya antike] /
[dṛṣṭvānāsaṅga nāyaka śāstraṃ sarvatra deśaya] /
body.translated_text: "May I attain the five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges) in the presence of the Lion of Debaters! Having seen the Unattached Leader, may he teach the doctrine everywhere!

children.text: sa ce bhaviṣye buddho loke sarveṣāṃ dharmasārathiḥ /
children.translated_text: If he shall become a <s>Buddha</s> in the world, the <s>Dharma</s>-charioteer of all,
then let the released flower-canopies standing in the sky" //4.73//
"become obedient to <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, and the rest,
and as they bow their heads at your feet, may the earth tremble!" //4.74//

body.text: atha khalu jyotīrasa ṛṣistāni puṣpāṇi yena bhagavāṃstenopari pra[kṣaptāni / tāni ca] ekacchatrastasthau / yaṃ dṛṣṭvā jyotīrasaḥ ṛṣirbhūyasyā mātrayā nirāmiṣeṇa prīti-saumanasyena udvelyamāno bhagavataḥ pādayoḥ nipapāta / samanantaranipatitaśca jyotīrasa ṛṣīrbhagavataścaraṇayoḥ / atha tāvadeva [trisāhasramahāsāhasraloka]dhātuḥ ṣaḍvikāraṃ pracakampe / yāni ca tatrāprameyāsaṃkhyeyāni sattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi [nirudvegacittāni] prāptānyabhūvan / ye ca gajavainayikāḥ sattvāste gajarūpeṇa sugataṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃtṛptāḥ yena maharṣistenopari puṣpāṇi prakṣipya tāni ca ākāśe saṃsthitāni / taṃ ca pṛthivīkampaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhūyasyā mātrayā āścaryaprāptā bhagavataścaraṇayornipetuḥ / ye 'pi buddhavainayikāḥ sattvāste sarve bhagavato buddhaveśaṃ dṛṣṭvā āścaryaprāptā abhūvan /
body.translated_text: Then the sage <s>Jyotīrasa</s> cast those flowers upward toward the Blessed One, and they remained as a single canopy. Seeing this, the sage <s>Jyotīrasa</s>, overwhelmed with even greater spiritual, non-worldly joy and gladness, fell at the feet of the Blessed One. And as soon as <s>Jyotīrasa</s> the sage had fallen at the Blessed One's feet, immediately the great trichiliocosm [trembled].

body.text: atha bhagavān śūraṅgamāt samādhervyudatiṣṭhat / tasmācca samādhervyuthitaṃ [dṛṣṭvā buddhavainayikāḥ sattvāḥ atīva] prītiprāmodyajātā
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One arose from the <s>Śūraṅgama</s> <s>samādhi</s>. Upon seeing him arise from that <s>samādhi</s>, the beings destined for the <s>Buddha</s>'s training were filled with exceeding joy and delight.

body.text: bhagavantaṃ yathālabdhaiḥ puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanavastrābharaṇālaṃkārairabhyavakiran ca imā gāthā abhāṣanta /
body.translated_text: They scattered over the Blessed One whatever flowers, incense, fragrance, garlands, ointments, garments, ornaments, and decorations they had obtained, and spoke these verses:

children.translated_text: "Arise quickly! Hear! I shall give you a prophecy,
'O great sage, you shall attain <s>bodhi</s>!'—so the Leader declared.
By his great might, the earth trembled,
and flowers became canopies in the sky!" //4.75//
"You are our <s>Buddha</s>, the foremost among bipeds,
O Mighty One, likewise a teacher for the welfare of the world!
Of infinite merit, as vast as space,
the essence of the triple world, the lamp of the universe!" //4.76//

body.text: atha jyotīraso bodhisattvo mahā
body.translated_text: Then <s>Jyotīrasa</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, said to the Blessed One: "What will that buddha-field be like, O Blessed One, where I shall turn the <s>Dharmacakra</s>?" The Blessed One replied: ...... [End of the Fourth Chapter, called 'The Conversion of the Sage Jyotīrasa.']

body.text:
sattvo bhagavantametadavocat / kīdṛśaṃ bhagavan tadbuddhakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati yattrāhaṃ dharmacakraṃ pravarttiṣye / bhagavānāha..... ..... / ..... ..... ..... ..... ..... ..... ..... .....
[ṛṣijyotīrasaprasādaparivarto nāma caturthaḥ // 4 //]
START Rkp 5
body.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Ratnaketudhāraṇī</s> Chapter 5

body.text: pañcamaḥ parivartaḥ
body.translated_text: Fifth Chapter

body.text: atha tasmin samaye buddh
body.translated_text: Then at that time, a hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Māras</s> from that buddha-field, all with their retinues, approached the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> and sat down before him.

body.text: kṣetre koṭīśatamārāste [sarve] saparivārā yena bhagavān śākyamuni[stathāgatastenopasaṃkramyāgrato nyaṣīdan /]
atha māraḥ pāpīmān
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māra</s> <s>Pāpīmān</s>, joining his palms toward the Blessed One, spoke thus:

body.text: yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamyaivamāha /

children.translated_text: "O Blessed One, I go for refuge with a deeply repentant mind.

children.text: śīghraṃ mocaya bandhānmāṃ dharmacaryāṃ ca sandiśa // Rkp_5.[1] //
children.translated_text: Swiftly release me from my bonds and instruct me in the practice of <s>Dharma</s>!" //5.1//

body.text: bhagavānāha /
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said:

children.text: na cāhaṃ tvāñca] vāremi gacchantaṃ cāgataṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: "I do not obstruct you, whether you go or come again.

children.text: mārgaṃ tvaṃ yat prajānīṣe gaccha yena [yathecchasi] // Rkp_5.[2] //
children.translated_text: The path that you discern—go wherever you wish." //5.2//

body.text: [pāpīmānāha /
body.translated_text: <s>Pāpīmān</s> said:

body.text: yadāhaṃ gantumicchāmi sānandaṃ viṣayaṃ svakam / pacabhirbandhanairbaddhamātmānamīkṣe gautama] // Rkp_5.[3] //
body.translated_text: "When I wish to go joyfully to my own domain, I see myself bound by five bonds, O <s>Gautama</s>." //5.3//

body.text: bhagavānāha /
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said:

children.text: sarva kalpa prahī[ṇā me mukto 'hamiha bandhanāt /
children.translated_text: "All my <s>kalpas</s> [of practice] are completed; I am freed from bondage here.

children.text: hiṃsā caiva mayā tyaktā sattvān bandhācca mocaye // Rkp_5.[4] //
children.translated_text: Violence too has been abandoned by me; I liberate beings from their bonds." //5.4//

Rare are faith and inclination; the practice of <s>bodhi</s> is exceedingly rare." //5.6//
"Rare it would be to hear the <s>Dharma</s> from the Protector of the World.

body.text: teṣāṃśca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ samādarśanenaiva buddhakṣetrāntargatānāṃ [sattvānāṃ rāgadveṣamohādīni]..... sarveṣāṃ cittacaityeṣu praśemuḥ / ekaikaśca sattva evaṃ saṃjānīte.....māmekaikastathāgataḥ sarvacetasā samanvāhṛtya sarvajvarapraśamanadharmaṃ deśaya[ti]..... /
body.translated_text: By the mere sight of those <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, [the beings'] <s>rāga</s> (passion), <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred), <s>moha</s> (delusion), and other [afflictions] within the buddha-field subsided in all the mind-shrines of beings. And each being perceived thus: '...each <s>Tathāgata</s>, having turned his mind fully toward me, teaches the <s>Dharma</s> for the pacification of all fevers...'

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena ye asmin kṛtsne buddhakṣetre antargatāḥ sarvasattvāḥ sarvandriyopastabdhāḥ .....yattvasmākaṃ buddhā bhagavanto dharmaṃ deśayantu / asmākaṃ bhadanta svagataṃ dharma vayaṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ dharmeṣu pratipa[tsyāmahe]..... /
body.translated_text: At that time, all the beings within this entire buddha-field, with all their faculties calmed...said: 'May the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, teach us the <s>Dharma</s>! Welcome, O Venerable Ones, to the <s>Dharma</s>! We shall practice the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones...'

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena apareṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ pūjākarmaṇe
body.translated_text: At that time, for the worship of those other <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> pervaded this entire buddha-field with a supreme, most excellent, distinguished, and magnificent fragrance surpassing the <s>Gandhavyūha</s> (array of fragrances).

body.text: sa śākyamunistathāgato gandhavyūhātikrāntena paramottamaviśiṣṭena udāreṇa gandhena sarvamidaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ sphuṭamakarot.......... /

body.translated_text: spoke thus: 'May the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, whoever they are in the world-systems of the ten directions at this time, turn their minds [toward us]...'

body.text: a
body.translated_text: "By my former vow, in this hostile world of the five defilements, I have attained <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening) for those whose aspirations are destroyed and whose paths are lost.

body.text: haṃ pūrvapraṇidhānenaivaṃ pratikūle pañcakaṣāye loke anuttarāṃ samyaksambodhim abhisaṃbuddho naṣṭāśayānāṃ pranaṣṭamārgāṇām

[avidyāndhānāṃ tamisrabhūtānāṃ kleśā]kṣiptānāṃ trayapāyasaṃprasthitānāmakuśalasamavadhānānāṃ sarvakuśalarahitānāṃ sarvavidvatpari[varjitānāmānantaryakṛtānāṃ saddharmavarjitānāṃ] caryāpavādakānām akṛpāśayānāṃ sattvānāṃ kāruṇyārthaṃ mahākṛpāvīryabalodyogena śītoṣṇavātātapapraśamanā[ya grāmanagaranigamajanapadān] padabhayāmupasaṃkramāmi / sattvahitārthaṃ svalparūkṣavirasaparamajagupsitaṃ pratikūlamāhāraṃ [bhakṣayiṣyāmi / teṣāṃ kuśalamūlajananārthaṃ] karpāsabhaṅgacīvarapāṃsukulāni prāvṛṇomi / parvatagirikandaravanaṣaṇḍa-[śūnyāgāra-śmaśāna-] śayyāsanaṃ paribhunajmi / upāyakauśalyamahākaruṇā
body.translated_text: for the sake of compassion toward beings who are blind with ignorance, immersed in darkness, cast about by <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), set upon the path to the three evil destinies, disposed toward unwholesome [actions], devoid of all wholesome [qualities], abandoned by all the wise, who have committed the acts of immediate retribution (<s>ānantarya</s>), who have rejected the true <s>Dharma</s>, who disparage [proper] conduct, and who have no compassionate disposition—with the exertion of the power of great compassion and vigor, for the alleviation of cold, heat, wind, and scorching sun, I approach villages, cities, towns, and countries on foot. For the benefit of beings, I shall eat food that is meager, rough, tasteless, most disgusting, and disagreeable. For the sake of generating their roots of merit, I don the robes of cotton rags and dust-cloth. I make use of beds and seats in mountains, hills, caves, forest groves, empty dwellings, and charnel grounds. Through skillful means and great compassion—

body.text: vīryasannahanena vividhāṃ kathāṃ
body.translated_text: with the girding of vigor, I tell various stories. To <s>kṣatriyas</s> I tell stories of royal sovereignty; to <s>brāhmaṇas</s> I tell stories of the <s>Vedas</s> and constellations; to ministers I tell stories of provincial administration; to merchants I tell stories of buying and selling; to householders stories of engagement in work; to women stories of beauty, ornaments, sons, prosperity, and co-wives; to ascetics I tell stories of patience, gentleness, the threefold practice, and vigor. For the ripening of beings, I engage those who have not attained to attainment, those who have not realized to realization, those who have not directly witnessed to direct witnessing, (

body.translated_text: for the liberation of the unfreed I endure various kinds of suffering. For the ripening of beings, I wander through the provinces.

body.text: atha ca punarye ime sattvāstatra māmākrośanti paribhāṣanti [īrṣyānvitena] dharmeṇābhūtenābhyākhyānti kuhana-lapana-māyāśāṭhya-mṛṣāvāda-pāruṣyaiḥ strīvacanairabhyākhyānti pāṃsubhirmāmavakiranti / śastraviṣāgni[cakratomaraśarakhaḍgaśakti]paraśvadhaśūlāyudhavṛṣṭibhirmama vadhāya parākrāmanti / hastyāśīviṣasiṃhavyāghravṛṣamahiṣavṛkamahānagnāṃśca madvadhāyotsṛjanti / [mamāvāsavihārakūṭāgārān] aśucinā durgandhenāpūrayanti / macchrāvakāṇāṃ cāntarnagaramanupraviṣṭānāmime anāryāḥ sattvāḥ anācāreṇa nṛtyagītenānuvicariṣyanti / [śatasahasro]pāyairmadvadhāyodyuktāḥ śāsanāntardhānāya ca dharmanetrīpradīpanirvāṇāya dharmadhvajaprapātanāya dharmanetrīprabhedāya [mama dharmacāriṇāṃ] māraṇāyodyuktāḥ / tat khalvetarhi sarve buddhā bhagavantasteṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ [dharma]netrīm avalokayata / yathā te buddhairbhagavadbhirasmin kliṣṭe pañca[kaṣāyayukte kāle] mahāsannipātaṃ kṛtvā saddharmanetrīcirasthityarthaṃ sarvamārabalaviṣayapramardanā[rthaṃ] sarvatriratnavaṃśasthityanupacchedārthaṃ sattvānāṃ kuśalamūla[vardhanārthaṃ sarva]parapravādasahadharmanigrahārthaṃ sattvānāṃ kalikalahadurbhikṣarogaparacakrabandhanavigrahavivādākālaśītoṣṇavātavṛṣṭi [kāyavāṅmanaḥkleśa]praśamanārthaṃ
body.translated_text: And furthermore, those beings there revile me, abuse me, slander me with falsehood motivated by jealousy, accuse me with deceit, garrulousness, illusion, dishonesty, false speech, harsh words, and women's words, and throw dust upon me. They attack me with rains of weapons—swords, poison, fire, discuses, lances, arrows, swords, spears, axes, tridents, and weapons—seeking to kill me. They release elephants, venomous serpents, lions, tigers, bulls, buffaloes, wolves, and great naked ascetics to kill me. They fill my dwelling places, monasteries, and mansions with impure foul-smelling [substances]. When my disciples enter the inner city, these ignoble beings follow them around with improper dancing and singing. Devoted to killing me by a hundred thousand means, they are engaged in the disappearance of the teaching, the extinguishing of the lamp of the <s>Dharma</s> eye, the pulling down of the <s>Dharma</s> banner, the splitting of the <s>Dharma</s> eye, and the killing of my <s>Dharma</s> practitioners. Therefore, now let all the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> look upon the <s>Dharma</s> eye of those <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>! Just as those <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>, in this corrupt age afflicted by the five degenerations, having made a great assembly, for the long endurance of the true <s>Dharma</s> eye, for the crushing of all the power and domain of <s>Māra</s>, for the unbroken continuity of the lineage of the <s>Triratna</s> (Three Jewels), for the increase of beings' roots of merit, for the restraint of all rival doctrines by the true <s>Dharma</s>, for the pacification of beings' strife, quarrels, famine, disease, foreign invasions, imprisonment, disputes, untimely cold, heat, wind, rain, and afflictions of body, speech, and mind,

body.text: sarvagṛhagrāmanagararāṣṭrarakṣaṇārthaṃ sarvaśāṭhyaviṣa[kākhordamohanaduḥsvapnadurdarśa]nārthaṃ sarvadhānyauṣadhiphalapuṣparasasattvopajīvyarthaṃ kṣatriyabrāhmaṇaviṭśūdrakuśalacaryāniyojanārthaṃ bodhisattva[cittotpādapāramitāpūra]ṇārthaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmupāyajñānakauśalyasmṛtimatigati-śauryapratibhāṇavivṛddhyarthamabhiṣeka-bhūmi-samāśvāsāvatārajñānapāraṅgamārthaṃ taiḥ pūrvakaistathāgatairarhadbhiḥ saṃbuddhairayaṃ vajradharmasamatāpratītya-dharmahṛdayasamucchrayavidhvaṃsanī-dharaṇī-mudrāpada-prabhedapraveśavyākaraṇo dharmaparyāyo bhāṣito 'dhiṣṭhito 'nyonyamanumoditaḥ / tat sādhu / evamevaitarhi ye daśasu dikṣu buddha bhagavantastiṣṭhanto yāpayanta iha mama buddhakṣetre pañcakaṣāye pṛcchā[yai] samāgatāḥ saṃniṣaṇṇāḥ sannipatitāste sarve asya buddhakṣetrasyārakṣāyai imaṃ vajradharmasamatāpratītya-dharmahṛdayasamucchrayavidhvaṃsanadhāraṇīmudrāpadaprabhedapraveśavyākaraṇaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ bhāsadhvamadhitiṣṭhatanyonyaṃ bhāṣadhvamanumodadhvaṃ sarddharmanetrīcirasthitaye sarvamāraviṣayabalapramardanārthaṃ yathā pūrvoktaṃ vistareṇa yāvadanāvaraṇajñānapāraṅgamārthamanukaṃpāyai mamadhyeṣaṇāya ca yadiha buddhakṣetre dharmanetrī ciraṃ tiṣṭhet / anatikramaṇī sarvaparapravādibhiravipralopadharmiṇī syāt / triratnavaṃśānupacchedanārthāya ca dharmarasaḥ sarvasattvopajīvyaḥ syāt /
body.translated_text: for the protection of all households, villages, cities, and kingdoms, for [counteracting] all deceit, poison, sorcery, bewilderment, bad dreams, and evil visions, for the sustenance of all grains, medicines, fruits, flowers, essences, and beings, for the engagement of <s>kṣatriyas</s>, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>vaiśyas</s>, and <s>śūdras</s> in wholesome conduct, for the fulfillment of <s>bodhisattvas</s>' generation of <s>bodhicitta</s> and the <s>pāramitās</s>, for the increase of <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>' skillful knowledge of means, mindfulness, intelligence, attainment, heroism, and eloquence, for reaching the far shore of the knowledge of consolation and entry into the <s>abhiṣeka</s> (consecration) stage—by those former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones, this <s>Dharma</s> discourse called the '<s>Vajradharma-samatā-pratītya-dharmahṛdaya-samucchraya-vidhvaṃsanī-dhāraṇī-mudrāpada-prabheda-praveśa-vyākaraṇa</s>' was spoken, established, and mutually approved. Therefore, excellent! Even so now, let all those <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> in the ten directions who dwell and abide, who have come and assembled in this <s>Buddhakṣetra</s> of the five degenerations for inquiry—let all of them, for the protection of this <s>Buddhakṣetra</s>, speak this <s>Dharma</s> discourse of the <s>Vajradharma-samatā-pratītya-dharmahṛdaya-samucchraya-vidhvaṃsana-dhāraṇī-mudrāpada-prabheda-praveśa-vyākaraṇa</s>, establish it, speak it to one another, and approve it, for the long endurance of the true <s>Dharma</s> eye, for the crushing of all the power and domain of <s>Māra</s>, as stated before in detail, up to the far shore of unobstructed knowledge, out of compassion and at my request—so that in this <s>Buddhakṣetra</s> the <s>Dharma</s> eye may long endure, be inviolable by all rival doctrines, and be of an undeceivable nature, and for the unbroken continuity of the lineage of the <s>Triratna</s>, and that the taste of <s>Dharma</s> may be the sustenance of all beings.

body.text: atha te buddhā bhagavanta evamāhuḥ / evametat avaśyamevāsmābhirbuddhakāryai karaṇīyam / iha buddhakṣetre dharmanetrīmadhiṣṭhā
body.translated_text: Then those <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> spoke thus: 'So be it! We must certainly perform this <s>Buddha</s> task. In this <s>Buddhakṣetra</s>, we shall establish the <s>Dharma</s> eye

body.text: syāmaḥ cirasthitaye sarvamāraviṣayabalapramardanāya yāvadanāvaraṇajñānapāraṅgamāya yānimān vajradharmasamatāpratītya-dharmahṛdayasamucchrayavidhvaṃsanadhāraṇīmudrāpadaprabhedapraveśavyākaraṇadharmaparyāyan bhāṣiṣyāmaḥ / śṛṇvantu sarvasattvāḥ ye kecidiha buddhakṣetre 'ntargatāḥ / tadyathā / aṅkara aṅkara / bhaṅkara prabhaṅkara / bhayaviha / mitra bhase / akhe akha saṃvare / dome domante / kevaṭe keyūre / samavahane samantabhadre / dharme dharme dharmake / japhale mitrānuphale phalavate / gaṇe gaṇaparante / hili hili / hili hilike / jambhavate / ṭakaṭe ṭakante ṭakavarante / ghanavahante / hirinte śirinte / viṃdruvate / govāhe / jure mitra / jure juṣe / agre avame / satya tathatā / huli hile candre / samadharme dharme / kucuru mucuru / acidra / cili cilili / cavaha / culu culu / mitravaha / kulu kulu / sara sara / kuṭu kuṭu / mahāsarasara / tuṭu tuṭu / mahāsatyahṛdaya / puṣpe supuṣpe / dhūmaparihare / abhaye / rucire / karakṣe / abhayamastu / vivaha titile mamale paśvakha / śiśira śiśira / lokavināyaka vajre vajradhare vajravate / vajramate vajradade / cakravajre / cakre cavate / dhare dhare / bhare bhare / pūre ṭara / huhure / bhaṃgavaṃvare /
body.translated_text: for its long endurance, for the crushing of all the power and domain of <s>Māra</s>, up to the far shore of unobstructed knowledge—this <s>Dharma</s> discourse of the <s>Vajradharma-samatā-pratītya-dharmahṛdaya-samucchraya-vidhvaṃsana-dhāraṇī-mudrāpada-prabheda-praveśa-vyākaraṇa</s> we shall speak. Let all beings within this <s>Buddhakṣetra</s> listen! That is to say: <s>aṅkara aṅkara / bhaṅkara prabhaṅkara / bhayaviha / mitra bhase / akhe akha saṃvare / dome domante / kevaṭe keyūre / samavahane samantabhadre / dharme dharme dharmake / japhale mitrānuphale phalavate / gaṇe gaṇaparante / hili hili / hili hilike / jambhavate / ṭakaṭe ṭakante ṭakavarante / ghanavahante / hirinte śirinte / viṃdruvate / govāhe / jure mitra / jure juṣe / agre avame / satya tathatā / huli hile candre / samadharme dharme / kucuru mucuru / acidra / cili cilili / cavaha / culu culu / mitravaha / kulu kulu / sara sara / kuṭu kuṭu / mahāsarasara / tuṭu tuṭu / mahāsatyahṛdaya / puṣpe supuṣpe / dhūmaparihare / abhaye / rucire / karakṣe / abhayamastu / vivaha titile mamale paśvakha / śiśira śiśira / lokavināyaka vajre vajradhare vajravate / vajramate vajradade / cakravajre / cakre cavate / dhare dhare / bhare bhare / pūre ṭara / huhure / bhaṃgavaṃvare /</s>

body.text: śara śaca cili curu pūre / maṇḍane maṇḍane / gagaraṇe / muhūrte sarvamuhūrtake / dhidhirayani makhiśvaralayaṇi riṣinijani dharavaci / caṇḍālī me me sarvasasyādhiṣṭhitā / ācchidyantu vāhanām / mini phalavati ojāgre vicini / vanaraha / vuvure / guru guru / muru muru / hili hili / hala hala / kākaṇḍavaha hihitāṃ / āyuhana / kuṇḍajvāla / bhase gardane / ādahati / mārgābhirohaṇi / phalasatye ārohavati / hili hili / yathā vajrāya svāgra yathāparaṃ ca hṛdayavāha / satyaparibhāva mārgābhirohaṇe acalabuddhi dada pracala pacaya / piṇḍahṛdaya candracaraṇa / acale śodhane prakrinimārge / il[ili]le / prabhe sāravrate / sarvatathatā satyānugate / anāvaraṇavrate / alatha aṅgure śamini vibrahmavayohi / ahite avāṇi / niravayava aciramārga / lana laghuṃsare / triratnavaṃśe dharmakāya jvalacandre / samudravati / mahadbhūtavyaya / samudravegavadhārṇimudreṇa makhimudra / surapratisaṃviddhamudra / āvartani / saṃmoha / skaravidyutarase kṣiti / mudrito 'si / ye kecit pṛthivī vaha vaha vaha vaha / kīṭakapaṭa / śaila pratītya hṛdayena mudritā dhāraṇī / dhara [dhara dhara] / dantilā dantindālā huska sarvahṛdaya mudrito 'si / jaḍa javaṭṭa jakhavaṭa sumativati mahadbhūta mudrita / ye kecit ṣaḍāyatananisṛtādbhutā
body.translated_text: <s>śara śaca cili curu pūre / maṇḍane maṇḍane / gagaraṇe / muhūrte sarvamuhūrtake / dhidhirayani makhiśvaralayaṇi riṣinijani dharavaci / caṇḍālī me me sarvasasyādhiṣṭhitā / ācchidyantu vāhanām / mini phalavati ojāgre vicini / vanaraha / vuvure / guru guru / muru muru / hili hili / hala hala / kākaṇḍavaha hihitāṃ / āyuhana / kuṇḍajvāla / bhase gardane / ādahati / mārgābhirohaṇi / phalasatye ārohavati / hili hili / yathā vajrāya svāgra yathāparaṃ ca hṛdayavāha / satyaparibhāva mārgābhirohaṇe acalabuddhi dada pracala pacaya / piṇḍahṛdaya candracaraṇa / acale śodhane prakrinimārge / ililile / prabhe sāravrate / sarvatathatā satyānugate / anāvaraṇavrate / alatha aṅgure śamini vibrahmavayohi / ahite avāṇi / niravayava aciramārga / lana laghuṃsare / triratnavaṃśe dharmakāya jvalacandre / samudravati / mahadbhūtavyaya / samudravegavadhārṇimudreṇa makhimudra / surapratisaṃviddhamudra / āvartani / saṃmoha / skaravidyutarase kṣiti / mudrito 'si / ye kecit pṛthivī vaha vaha vaha vaha / kīṭakapaṭa / śaila pratītya hṛdayena mudritā dhāraṇī / dhara dhara dhara / dantilā dantindālā huska sarvahṛdaya mudrito 'si / jaḍa javaṭṭa jakhavaṭa sumativati mahadbhūta mudrita / ye kecit ṣaḍāyatananisṛtādbhutā</s>

body.text: ini mine / sacake ghoṣasacane / mudritacaryādhiṣṭhānavākpathānanyathā / mahāpuṇyasamuccayāvatāra / mahākaruṇayā mudrita / sarvasamyak pratipat cirabhadraṃ jvalatu dharmanetrī / sarve munivṛṣabhāḥ mahākaruṇasamādhijñānalābhabalena maitrītyāgātivīryabalenādhiṣṭhitā sarvabhūtopacayāya svāhā /
body.translated_text: <s>ini mine / sacake ghoṣasacane / mudritacaryādhiṣṭhānavākpathānanyathā / mahāpuṇyasamuccayāvatāra / mahākaruṇayā mudrita / sarvasamyak pratipat cirabhadraṃ jvalatu dharmanetrī / sarve munivṛṣabhāḥ mahākaruṇasamādhijñānalābhabalena maitrītyāgātivīryabalenādhiṣṭhitā sarvabhūtopacayāya svāhā</s> /

body.text: atha tāvadeva te sarvabuddhakṣetrāntargatāḥ sarvasattvāstrīṣkṛtyaivamāhuḥ / namaḥ sarvabuddhebhyaḥ / namo namaḥ sarvabuddhebhya iti / evaṃ cāhuḥ / aho mahāścaryo munisaṃnipātaḥ / aho mahāścaryo bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ mahāśrāvakāṇāṃ ca saṃnipātaḥ / aho vata mahāścaryādbhutāśrutapūrvo 'yaṃ vajradharmasmatā-pratītya-dharmahṛdaya-sarvadharma-samucchraya-vidhvaṃsanī-dhāraṇī-mudrāpadaprabheda-praveśavyākaraṇo dharmaparyāyaḥ / sarva-śāstṛśāsana-dharmanetrī-triratna-vaṃśādhiṣṭhāna-nirdeśo māraviṣaya-balavidhvaṃsano mārapāśasaṃcchedanaḥ sarvaśatrunigraho dharmadhvajocchrāpaṇaḥ dharmapakṣarakṣākaro yāvat sakalabuddhaviṣayaprapūraṇārtham / etarhi sarvabuddhairbhagavadbhirayaṃ vajradharmasamatāpratītyadharmahṛdayasamucchrayavidhvaṃsanadhāraṇīmudrāpadaprabhedapraveśavyākaraṇo dharmaparyāyo bhāṣitaḥ / sarvasattvahṛdayamudrā sarvamahābhūtasaṃskāraṣaḍāyatanaparikarma yāvat sarvasattvānāmānuttaraparinirvāṇapratilābhāya / asmin khalu punardhāraṇīvyākaraṇe bhāṣyamāṇe triṃśadgaṅgānadīvālukāsamānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ dhāraṇīnirhārasamādhikṣāntipratilābho 'bhūt /
body.translated_text: Then immediately all beings within all the <s>Buddhakṣetras</s>, having cried out three times, spoke thus: 'Homage to all <s>Buddhas</s>! Homage, homage to all <s>Buddhas</s>!' And they said: 'Oh, what a great wonder, this assembly of Sages! Oh, what a great wonder, this assembly of <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> and great disciples! Oh, indeed wondrous, marvelous, and never before heard is this <s>Dharma</s> discourse of the <s>Vajradharma-samatā-pratītya-dharmahṛdaya-sarvadharma-samucchraya-vidhvaṃsanī-dhāraṇī-mudrāpada-prabheda-praveśa-vyākaraṇa</s>! It is the establishment of the teaching of all Masters, the <s>Dharma</s> eye, and the lineage of the <s>Triratna</s>; the destroyer of the power and domain of <s>Māra</s>; the cutter of <s>Māra</s>'s snares; the subduer of all enemies; the raiser of the <s>Dharma</s> banner; the protector of the side of <s>Dharma</s>; even up to the fulfillment of the entire domain of the <s>Buddha</s>. Now, by all the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>, this <s>Dharma</s> discourse has been spoken. It is the seal of the hearts of all beings, the purification of all great elements, formations, and the six sense-bases, up to the attainment of the supreme <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of all beings.' Indeed, when this <s>dhāraṇī</s> prophecy was being spoken, <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> equal in number to the sands of thirty <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers attained the <s>dhāraṇī</s> extraction, <s>samādhi</s>, and patience.

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena candraprabhaḥ kumārabhūtaḥ utthāyāsanāt prāñjalirbhūtvā samantato 'valokya buddhādhiṣṭhānena svarddhibalānubhāvena sarvamidaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ svareṇapūrya evamāha /
body.translated_text: At that time, the prince <s>Candraprabha</s>, rising from his seat, joining his palms, looking around in all directions, by the <s>Buddha</s>'s empowerment and by the power of his own supernatural abilities, filling this entire <s>Buddhakṣetra</s> with his voice, spoke thus:

children.translated_text: Rare indeed is such an assembly of the moon-like <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors);
rare too are the wise <s>bodhisattvas</s> of great vows. // Rkp_6.[1] //
The hearing of such a <s>mudrā</s> (seal) is supremely rare—
this <s>Dharma</s> eye established by the compassionate Protectors. // Rkp_6.[2] //
The defeat of all the factions and enemies of <s>Māra</s>,
the unbroken continuity of the <s>Triratna</s>—established by the perfectly awakened ones. // Rkp_6.[3] //
For the destruction of all obscurations, increasing patience and gentleness,
attracting beings here, and protecting kingdoms and realms. // Rkp_6.[4] //
Warding off evil deeds here, counteracting wrong views,
the consolation of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, revealing the path of awakening. // Rkp_6.[5] //
Increasing the <s>pāramitās</s> and fulfilling virtuous conduct,
also established for the increase of skillful knowledge and eloquence. // Rkp_6.[6] //
A collection of the wholesome side, unconquered among <s>dhāraṇīs</s>,
stainless, illuminating the path of awakening, witnessing the <s>Dharma</s>. // Rkp_6.[7] //
Having removed all doubt, one has conviction in [these] <s>dhāraṇīs</s>;

children.text: eṣa vai sakalo mārgo yena bodhiḥ pravartate // Rkp_6.[8] //
children.translated_text: this is indeed the complete path by which awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) proceeds. // Rkp_6.[8] //
We shall speak further the unconquered <s>dhāraṇī</s>,
for the protection of <s>Dharma</s> preachers and for the increase of listeners. // Rkp_6.[9] //

children.text: chandaṃ dadāti ko nvartho bodhisattvo mahāyaśāḥ /
children.translated_text: What purpose does the glorious <s>bodhisattva</s> who grants consent [serve]?
For the removal of obscurations and for the benefit and increase of beings. // Rkp_6.[10] //

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena gaṅgānadībālukāsamāḥ kumārabhūtā bodhisattvā mahāsattvā ekakaṇṭhenaivamāhuḥ / vayamapyasyāṃ dhāraṇyāṃ chandaṃ dadāmo 'dhitiṣṭhāmaḥ / yaḥ kaścit kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bhikṣurvā bhikṣuṇī vā upāsako vā upāsikā vā snātvā śucīni cīvarāṇi prāvṛtya nānāpuṣpasaṃcchanne nānāgandhapradhūpite nānārasaparivṛte nānāvastrābharaṇaduṣyasaṃsthite chatradhvajapatākocchrāpite svalaṃkṛte maṇḍalamāle mṛdusukhasaṃsparśe siṃhāsane abhiruhya imāṃ dhāraṇīṃ saṃprakāśayet na cāsya kaścit cittasaṃkṣobhaṃ kāyasaṃkṣobhaṃ manaḥsaṃkṣobhaṃ vā kariṣyati / na cāsya kaścit kāye śvāsaṃ mokṣyati śīrṣarogaṃ ca kartuṃ śakṣyati / nedaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate / na kāyarogaṃ vā na jivhārogaṃ vā na dantarogaṃ
body.translated_text: At that time, <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> in the form of princes, equal in number to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, spoke with one voice: 'We too give our consent and establish [our support] in this <s>dhāraṇī</s>. Whatever son of good family or daughter of good family, <s>bhikṣu</s> or <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, <s>upāsaka</s> or <s>upāsikā</s>, having bathed and put on clean robes, seated upon a lion-throne in a well-adorned <s>maṇḍala</s>-pavilion covered with various flowers, perfumed with various fragrances, surrounded by various flavors, spread with various cloths, ornaments, and silks, with parasols, banners, and flags raised, on a seat of soft and pleasant touch, should proclaim this <s>dhāraṇī</s>—no one will be able to cause disturbance to that person's mind, body, or mental state. No one will be able to release breath upon that person's body or cause headache. This is impossible. No one will be able to cause bodily disease, tongue disease, tooth disease,

body.text: nākṣirogaṃ na grīvārogaṃ na bāhurogaṃ na pṛṣṭharogaṃ na antrarogaṃ nodararogaṃ na śroṇīrogaṃ na ūrurogaṃ na jaṅghārogaṃ kaścit kartuṃ śakṣyati / na cāsya svarasaṃkṣobho bhaviṣyati / yaśca tasya dharmabhāṇakasya pūrvāśubhakarmaṇā dhātusaṃkṣobhaḥ svarasaṃkṣobho vā syāt tasyemāṃ dhāraṇīṃ vācayataḥ sarvo niḥśeṣaṃ praśamiṣyati / karmaparikṣayāt svasti bhaviṣyati / ye 'pi tatra dharmaśrāvaṇikāḥ saṃnipatiṣyanti teṣāmapi na kaścit dhātusaṃkṣobhaṃ kariṣyati svarasaṃkṣobhaṃ vā / ye ca tatra imāṃ dhāraṇīṃ śroṣyanti teṣāṃ yadaśubhena karmaṇā dīrghaglāniḥ dhātusaṃkṣobho vā svarasaṃkṣobho vā syāt tat sarvaṃ parikṣayaṃ yāsyati /
body.translated_text: eye disease, neck disease, arm disease, back disease, intestinal disease, stomach disease, hip disease, thigh disease, or leg disease. Nor will there be disturbance of that person's voice. And whatever disturbance of the bodily elements or voice that <s>dharmabhāṇaka</s> (dharma-preacher) might have due to previous unwholesome <s>karma</s>—all of that will be completely pacified when reciting this <s>dhāraṇī</s>. Through the exhaustion of <s>karma</s>, there will be well-being. And those who will gather there as listeners of the <s>dharma</s>—no one will cause disturbance of their bodily elements or voice either. And for those who will hear this <s>dhāraṇī</s> there, whatever long illness, disturbance of bodily elements, or disturbance of voice they might have due to unwholesome <s>karma</s>—all of that will be utterly exhausted.

body.text: atha khalu candraprabhaḥ kumārabhūto yena te buddhā bhagavanto gaṅgānadīvālukāsamā bodhisattvaparivārāstenāñjaliṃ praṇamyaivamāha / samanvāharantu me buddhā bhagavanto 'syāṃ dhāraṇyāṃ chandaṃ dadatu / tad yathā / kṣānte asamārūpe / maitre somavate / ehi nava kuṃjave / nava kuṃjave nava kuṃjave / mūlaśodhane / vaḍhakha vaḍhakha / māratathatā-pariccheda / vahasa vahasa / amūle acale dada / pracale vidhile ekanayapariccheda / caṇḍinavorasatṛṇe bhūlare bhūsaratṛṇe khagasuratṛṇe snavasuratṛṇe bhūtakoṭe paricchede / jalakha jalakhavaye / jalanāmaśakha kakakha / haha haha / huhu huhu / sparśavedanapariccheda /
body.translated_text: Then Prince <s>Candraprabha</s> joined his palms in salutation before those <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>, together with their retinues of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, equal in number to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and spoke thus: 'May the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> bear me in mind and give their consent in this <s>dhāraṇī</s>. That is to say: <s>kṣānte asamārūpe / maitre somavate / ehi nava kuṃjave / nava kuṃjave nava kuṃjave / mūlaśodhane / vaḍhakha vaḍhakha / māratathatā-pariccheda / vahasa vahasa / amūle acale dada / pracale vidhile ekanayapariccheda / caṇḍinavorasatṛṇe bhūlare bhūsaratṛṇe khagasuratṛṇe snavasuratṛṇe bhūtakoṭe paricchede / jalakha jalakhavaye / jalanāmaśakha kakakha / haha haha / huhu huhu / sparśavedanapariccheda /</s>

body.text: amamā numama khyama-masa mudrava / mudra khasaṃskārāṇāmaṃpariccheda / bodhisattvākṣativima mahāvima bhūtakoṭi ākāśaśvāsapariccheda / svāhā /
body.translated_text: <s>amamā numama khyama-masa mudrava / mudra khasaṃskārāṇāmaṃpariccheda / bodhisattvākṣativima mahāvima bhūtakoṭi ākāśaśvāsapariccheda / svāhā /</s>

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena sarvabuddhakṣetrāntargatā bodhisattvā mahāsattvāste ca mahāśrāvakāḥ śakrabrahmalokapāladevanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragendrāste ca mahaujaskamahaujaskāḥ sattvāḥ sarve sādhukāraṃ pradaduḥ / te ca buddhā bhagavanta evamāhuḥ / mahābalavegavatī sarvaśatrunivāriṇī vata iyaṃ dhāraṇī sarvabhayavyādhiduḥsvapnadurnimittamokṣaṇī yāvadanāvaraṇajñānamahāpuṇyajñānasamuccayānuttarajñānaniṣyandā iyaṃ dhāraṇī bhāṣitā /
body.translated_text: At that time, all the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> and great <s>śrāvakas</s> within all the <s>buddha-kṣetras</s> (buddha-fields), together with <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, the world-protectors, gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoraga</s> lords, and those beings of great power and majesty—all gave their approval. And those <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> spoke thus: 'This <s>dhāraṇī</s> is of great force and momentum, repelling all enemies, liberating from all fears, diseases, bad dreams, and evil omens, and this <s>dhāraṇī</s> has been spoken as the outflow of unobstructed knowledge, the accumulation of great merit-knowledge, and unsurpassed knowledge.'

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena bhuteśvaro nāma mahābrahmā mahābrahmabalaviṣayavyūhādhiṣṭhānena strīrūpeṇa bhagavato 'mitāyuḥ purato niṣasāda paramavarṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgato divyābhikrāntaiḥ paramodārairvastrālaṅkāraiḥ puṣpagandhamālyavilepanaiścābhyalaṃkṛtaḥ / atha bhūteśvaro mahābrahmā utthāyāsanādañjaliṃ praṇamyaivamāha / adhitiṣṭhantu / me buddhā bhagavantaḥ svaramaṇḍalavāgvyāhāraviniścayanirdeśaṃ yadaham idaṃ kṛtsraṃ buddhakṣetraṃ svareṇābhivijñapayeyam / na ca me atra kaścid vighno bhavet / yat idametarhi dharmabhāṇakānāṃ dharmaśrāvaṇikānāṃ cārthāya tādṛśīṃ mantrapadarakṣāṃ bhāṣeta yathā yaḥ kaścit paścime kāle māro vā māraparṣad vā devo vā nāgo vā nāgī vā nāgamahallako vā nāgamahallikā
body.translated_text: At that time, the great <s>Brahmā</s> named <s>Bhūteśvara</s>, through the display of the great <s>Brahmā</s>'s power and domain, sat before the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Amitāyus</s> in the form of a woman, endowed with supreme beauty and radiance, adorned with divinely exquisite and most noble garments, ornaments, flowers, fragrances, garlands, and ointments. Then the great <s>Brahmā</s> <s>Bhūteśvara</s> rose from his seat, joined his palms in salutation, and spoke thus: 'May the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> bestow their blessing! May they grant the instruction for the determination of the vocal <s>maṇḍala</s> and speech-utterance, so that I may fill this entire <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> with my voice, and may there be no obstacle for me herein. May they now speak such a protective <s>mantra</s>-formula for the benefit of <s>dharma</s>-preachers and <s>dharma</s>-listeners, so that in the future age, whatever <s>Māra</s> or <s>Māra</s>'s retinue, <s>deva</s>, <s>nāga</s>, female <s>nāga</s>, elder <s>nāga</s>, elder female <s>nāga</s>,

body.text: vā nāgapārṣado vā nāgapārṣadī vā nāgaputrako vā nāgaputrikā vā vistareṇa kartavyaṃ yāvat piśāco vā piśācī vā piśācamahallako vā piśācamahallikā vā piśācapārṣado vā piśācapārṣadī vā piśācaputrako vā piśācaputrikā vā manuṣyo vā amanuṣyo vā dharmabhāṇakānāṃ dharmaśrāvaṇikānāṃ vā avatāraprekṣī avatāragaveṣī pratyarthikaḥ pratyamitro vā upasaṃkrametāntaśo dharmabhāṇakānāṃ dharmaśrāvaṇikānāṃ vā ekaromakūpamapi viheṭhayed vihiṃsayed vilopayet ojo vā haret śvāsaṃ vā kāye prakṣipet duṣṭacitto vā prekṣeta antaśaḥ ekakṣaṇamapi teṣāmahaṃ yāvat mārāṇāṃ manuṣyā-manuṣyāṇāṃ pratiṣedhaṃ daṇḍaparigrahaṃ vā kuryām / jṛmbhaṇaṃ mohanaṃ śapathaṃ dadyām / abhitiṣṭhantu me buddhā bhagavantaḥ svaramaṇḍalavāgvyāhāraṃ yadahamidaṃ kṛtsnaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ svareṇāpūrayeyam / kaścātra me sahāyo bhaviṣyatīti / atha khalu te buddhā bhagavantastūṣṇīṃbhāvenādhivāsayāmāsuḥ /
body.translated_text: member of the <s>nāga</s> retinue, female member of the <s>nāga</s> retinue, <s>nāga</s> son, <s>nāga</s> daughter—and so on in detail—up to <s>piśāca</s>, female <s>piśāca</s>, elder <s>piśāca</s>, elder female <s>piśāca</s>, member of the <s>piśāca</s> retinue, female member of the <s>piśāca</s> retinue, <s>piśāca</s> son, <s>piśāca</s> daughter, human or non-human—whoever approaches seeking an opportunity, searching for an opening, as an adversary or enemy of the <s>dharma</s>-preachers or <s>dharma</s>-listeners, and would harass, harm, despoil, steal their vital essence, cast breath upon their bodies, or look upon them with malicious intent—even for a single hair-pore, even for a single moment—I shall impose restraint and punishment upon all those <s>Māras</s>, humans, and non-humans. I shall apply paralyzing, bewildering, and binding [spells]. May the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> bestow their blessing upon my vocal <s>maṇḍala</s> and speech-utterance, so that I may fill this entire <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> with my voice. And who will be my ally herein?' Then those <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> assented through silence.

body.text: tatra ca śikhindharī nāma śakro jāmbūnadamayena niṣkāvabhāsenālaṃkṛtakāyo nātidūre niṣaṇṇaḥ / atha śikhindharaḥ śakro bhūteśvaraṃ brahmāṇam evamāha / mā bhagini amitāyuṣastathāgatasya purato niṣīdasva / mā bhaginī atra pramādyasva / mā bhagavantaṃ viheṭhaya / tat kasya hetoḥ /
body.translated_text: And there, the <s>Śakra</s> named <s>Śikhindhara</s>, his body adorned with the radiance of a golden ornament, was seated not far away. Then <s>Śakra Śikhindhara</s> spoke to the <s>Brahmā</s> <s>Bhūteśvara</s> thus: 'O sister, do not sit before the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s>! O sister, do not be heedless here! Do not trouble the <s>Bhagavān</s>! For what reason?

children.translated_text: Fools delight in proliferation (<s>prapañca</s>), while <s>Tathāgatas</s> are free from proliferation.
They will demonstrate <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned formations) characterized by arising and decay.' //Rkp 6.11//

body.text: sarvarūpākṣarapadaprabhedatathatānayaprāptāstathāgatāḥ / na bhagini tathāgatastathatāṃ virodhayati ekasamatayā tathatayā yadutākāśasamatayā / ākāśamapyasamāropa-trisaṃskāravyayalakṣaṇam / yathākāśamakalpamavikalpaṃ saṃskāreṣu evameva tathāgataḥ / kāmaguṇān na prapañcayati na kalpayati na vikalpayati nādhitiṣṭhati nābhiniviśati / evaṃ na jīvaṃ na jantuṃ na poṣaṃ na pudgalaṃ na skandhāyatanāni prapañcayati nābhiniviśati nādhitiṣṭhati na kalpayati na vikalpayati / kathaṃ nāma tvaṃ bhagini tathāgatakāyaṃ prapañcayasi /
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Tathāgatas</s> have attained the method of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) through the analysis of all forms, syllables, and words. O sister, the <s>Tathāgata</s> does not contradict <s>tathatā</s>, through the single sameness of <s>tathatā</s>, that is, through the sameness of space. Space too is without superimposition, characterized by the decay of the three <s>saṃskāras</s>. Just as space is without conceptualization and without discrimination regarding <s>saṃskāras</s>, so too is the <s>Tathāgata</s>. He does not proliferate the qualities of desire, does not conceptualize, does not discriminate, does not establish, does not cling. Similarly, he does not proliferate regarding a being, a creature, a person, an individual, or the <s>skandhas</s> and <s>āyatanas</s>; he does not cling, does not establish, does not conceptualize, does not discriminate. How then do you, sister, proliferate regarding the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>?'

body.text: amitāyustathāgata āha / samīkṣya devānāmindra vācaṃ bhāṣasva / mā te syāddīrgharātramaniṣṭaṃ phalam / mahāsatpuruṣo hyeṣa bahubuddhakṛtādhikāro 'varopitakuśalamūlo buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmantike / anena punaḥ satpuruṣeṇa tathāgatapūjākarmaṇe svalaṃkṛtastrīrūpamabhinirmitam / mā tvamenaṃ strībhāvena samudācara /
body.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s> said: 'O lord of the gods, consider [carefully] and speak your words! Lest there be an unpleasant result for you for a long time. For this is a great and virtuous person who has planted roots of merit under many <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>, with much service performed. Moreover, this virtuous person has magically created a well-adorned female form for the purpose of worshipping the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Do not address him as if he were a woman.'

body.text: atha śikhindharaḥ śakro bhūteśvaraṃ brahmāṇamevamāha / kṣamasva kulaputra mamānukampāmupādāya / mā cāhamasya bhāṣitasyāniṣṭaṃ phalaṃ prāpnuyāmiti / atha kautūhaliko bodhisattvā āha / yadi bhagavan śakraṇedaṃ vacanamapratideśitamabhaviṣyat kiyāṃstasya
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra Śikhindhara</s> spoke to the <s>Brahmā</s> <s>Bhūteśvara</s> thus: 'Forgive me, O son of good family, out of compassion for me! May I not receive the unpleasant result of this speech!' Then <s>Kautūhalika Bodhisattva</s> said: 'O <s>Bhagavān</s>, if <s>Śakra</s> had not confessed this speech, what would have been

body.text: phalavipākaḥ / amitāyustathāgata āha / yadi kulaputra anena na pratideśitamabhiṣyat caturaśītijanmasahasrāṇi kāmagarbhaparibhūtastrībhāvaḥ parigṛhītaḥ syāt / tasmāttarhi rakṣitavyaṃ vākkarma / pratibhā[tu] te kulaputrādhiṣṭhitastathāgataistava svaramaṇḍalavāgvyāhāraḥ /
body.translated_text: the ripening of its result?' The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s> said: 'O son of good family, if he had not confessed, for eighty-four thousand births he would have taken on a female body, despised by the womb of desire. Therefore, one should guard one's verbal <s>karma</s>. May it be manifest to you, O son of good family—the <s>Tathāgatas</s> have established your vocal <s>maṇḍala</s> and speech-utterance.'

body.text: atha bhūteśvaro brahmā buddhādhiṣṭhānena prāñjalidaśadiśo vyavalokyaivamāha / samanvāharantu māṃ buddhā bhagavanto bodhisattvāśca mahāsattvā mahāśrāvakāśca devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragāścātra cchandaṃ dadatu yasyāyamabhiprāyaḥ syāt / iyaṃ dharmanetrī cirasthitikā bhavet / dharmabhāṇakānāṃ dharmaśrāvaṇikānāṃ ca pratipattiyuktānāṃ mā viheṭho bhavediti / sa ca me cchandaṃ dadātu yacca paścime kāle na mārā[na] manuṣyāmanuṣyāsteṣāṃ viheṭhaṃ kuryuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā</s> <s>Bhūteśvara</s>, through the blessing of the <s>Buddha</s>, with palms joined, looked in the ten directions and spoke thus: 'May the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, and the great <s>śrāvakas</s>, together with the gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>, bear me in mind and give their consent here, whoever shares this intention—that this <s>dharma</s>-eye may be long-enduring, that there may be no harm to the <s>dharma</s>-preachers and <s>dharma</s>-listeners who are endowed with practice. And may they give me consent that in the future age, <s>Māras</s>, humans, and non-humans shall not cause harm to them.'

body.text: atha sa bhūteśvaro brahmā teṣāṃ duṣṭacittānāṃ pratiṣedhanāya śapa[thagraha]ṇāyoccasvaraśabdaṃ mumoca / tena ca śabdena sarvāmimāṃ lokadhātumāpūrayāmāsa / tena khalu punaḥ samayena sarve brahmendrā ekakaṇṭhenaivamāhuḥ / vayamasyāṃ dhāraṇyāṃ chandaṃ dadāmaḥ / svayaṃ ca paścime kāle imāṃ dhāraṇīṃ dhārayiṣyāmaḥ prakāśayiṣyāmaḥ saddharmaṃ rakṣiṣyāmaḥ tāṃśca dharmabhāṇakān dharmaśrāvaṇikāṃśca pratipattiyuktān rakṣiṣyāmaḥ / vada tvaṃ satpuruṣa / vayaṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ
body.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā</s> <s>Bhūteśvara</s>, for the purpose of restraining those with malicious intent and for the seizing of oaths, released a loud vocal sound. And with that sound he filled this entire world-realm. At that time, all the <s>Brahma</s>-lords and <s>Indras</s> spoke with one voice: 'We give our consent in this <s>dhāraṇī</s>. And we ourselves in the future age will uphold this <s>dhāraṇī</s>, will proclaim it, will protect the true <s>dharma</s>, and will protect those <s>dharma</s>-preachers and <s>dharma</s>-listeners who are endowed with practice. Speak, O virtuous one! Before the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>,

body.text: bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ ca mahāśrāvakāṇāṃ ca purato 'syāṃ dhāraṇyāṃ chandaṃ dadāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, and the great <s>śrāvakas</s>, we give our consent in this <s>dhāraṇī</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu bhūteśvaro brahmā evamāha / adhitiṣṭhantu me buddhā bhagavanto bodhisattvā mahāsattvā mahāśrāvakāśca / tad yathā /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā</s> <s>Bhūteśvara</s> spoke thus: 'May the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, and the great <s>śrāvakas</s> bestow their blessing! That is to say:

body.text: amale vimale gaṇaṣaṇḍe / mahāre caṇḍe mahācaṇḍe / came mahācame / some sthāme / avaha vivaha / aṅganī netrakhave mūlaparicchede / yakṣacaṇḍe piśācacaṇḍe āvartani saṃvartani / saṃkāraṇi jambhani mohani uccāṭani / hamaha maha maha maha / ākuñcane khagaśava / amale amūla parivarte asārakhava svāhā /
body.translated_text: <s>amale vimale gaṇaṣaṇḍe / mahāre caṇḍe mahācaṇḍe / came mahācame / some sthāme / avaha vivaha / aṅganī netrakhave mūlaparicchede / yakṣacaṇḍe piśācacaṇḍe āvartani saṃvartani / saṃkāraṇi jambhani mohani uccāṭani / hamaha maha maha maha / ākuñcane khagaśava / amale amūla parivarte asārakhava svāhā /</s>

children.translated_text: Whoever would transgress these <s>mantras</s> and not observe the assembly of the host,

children.text: akṣi mudret sphālet śīrṣamaṅgabhedo bhavedapi // Rkp_6.[12] //
children.translated_text: their eyes would be sealed, their head would burst, and there would be dismemberment of their limbs. //Rkp 6.12//

body.text: tad yathā / acaca avaha / cacacu krakṣa cacaṭa cacāna / khaga caca cacacaca na ca / amūla caca amūla cacaha māmūla cacaha mūla mūpaḍa mahā svāhā /
body.translated_text: <s>acaca avaha / cacacu krakṣa cacaṭa cacāna / khaga caca cacacaca na ca / amūla caca amūla cacaha māmūla cacaha mūla mūpaḍa mahā svāhā /</s>

body.text: atha tāvadeva sarve brahmendrā yāvat pi[śā]cendrāḥ sādhukāraṃ daduḥ / evaṃ cāhuḥ / atīva mahāsahasrabalavegapramardanāni etāni mantrapadāni / pāśo 'yaṃ saktaḥ sarvāhitaiṣiṇāṃ bhūtānāṃ kutaḥ punasteṣāṃ jīvitam / bhūteśvaro brahmā evamāha / ye duṣṭāśrayā akṛpā akṛtajñā bhūtāḥ sattvānāṃ viheṭhakāmā vā mārapārṣadyā vā
body.translated_text: Then at that very moment, all the <s>Brahma</s>-lords and up to the lords of the <s>piśācas</s> gave their approval. And they spoke thus: 'These <s>mantra</s>-words are exceedingly crushing with the force of a great thousandfold [power]. This is a snare bound upon all beings who wish harm—how much more so their very life!' <s>Brahmā</s> <s>Bhūteśvara</s> spoke thus: 'Those beings who are of evil disposition, without compassion, ungrateful, who wish to harm beings or who are of <s>Māra</s>'s retinue,

body.text: avatāraprekṣiṇo buddhaśāsanābhiprasannānāṃ rājñāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ mūrdhābhiṣiktānāmabatāraprekṣiṇa upasaṃkrameyuḥ / agramahiṣīṇāṃ putraduhitṝṇāṃ cāntaḥpurikāṇāṃ vāmātyabhaṭabalāgrapārṣadyānāmanyeṣāṃ vā buddhaśāsanābhiprasannānāṃ strīpuruṣadhārakadhārikāṇāsupāsakopāsikānāṃ vā dharmabhāṇakānāṃ dharmaśrāvaṇikānāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ bhikṣuṇīnāṃ vā dhyānasvādhyāyābhiyuktānāṃ vaiyāvṛtyābhiyuktānāṃ vā avatāraprekṣiṇa upasaṃkrameyuḥ / antaśaḥ eka[muhūrtamapi sattvānām] ekaromakūpamapi viheṭhayeyuḥ vihiṃsayeyurvipralopayeyuḥ / ojo vā apahareyuḥ śvāsaṃ vā kāye prakṣiperan duṣṭacittā vā prekṣeran klinnadurgandhakāyānāṃ teṣāṃ mārāṇāṃ yāvanmanuṣyāmanuṣyāṇāṃ saptadhā mūrdhā sphālet akṣīṇī caiṣāṃ viparivarteran hṛdayānyucchuṣyeran śvitrā bhaveyuḥ klinnadurgandhakāyā ṛddhiparihīnā bhūmiśca teṣāṃ vivaramanuprayacchet / vāyavaśca tān caturdiśaṃ vikṣepeyuḥ / pāṃsubhiravakīrṇāstatraiva vikṣiptacittā paryaṭeyuḥ / ye bhūmicarāste pṛthivīvivaram anupraviśeyuḥ caturaśītiyojanasahasrāṇi adhastatraiva teṣāmāyuḥparikṣayaḥ syāt / ye jalacarā duṣṭabhūtā buddhaśāsane nābhiprasannāḥ syuḥ rājñāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ buddhaśāsanābhiprasannānāṃ yāvadvaiyāvṛtyābhiyuktānāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ viheṭhaṃ kuryusteṣāmapi tathaiva saptadhā mūrdhā sphālet / yāvattatraiva teṣāmāyuḥparikṣayaḥ syāt ya imān mantrānatikrameyuḥ / api ca yasmin
body.translated_text: they should approach those kings and <s>kṣatriyas</s>, consecrated sovereigns, who are devoted to the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching, looking for an opportunity—or their chief queens, sons, daughters, women of the inner palace, or ministers, soldiers, military leaders, chief attendants, or other men and women, male and female lay followers (<s>upāsakas</s> and <s>upāsikās</s>) devoted to the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching, or <s>Dharma</s>-preachers, <s>Dharma</s>-listeners, <s>bhikṣus</s>, <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, or those devoted to meditation and self-study, or those devoted to service—they should approach looking for an opportunity. If even for a single moment they should harass, harm, or rob even a single hair-pore of any being, or steal their vitality, or cast disease into their bodies, or look at them with malicious intent—then those <s>Māras</s>, up to humans and non-humans, with foul-smelling wet bodies, their heads shall split into seven pieces, their eyes shall be overturned, their hearts shall dry up, they shall become leprous, with foul-smelling wet bodies, deprived of supernatural powers, and the earth shall open up a chasm for them. And the winds shall scatter them in the four directions. Covered with dust, they shall wander about with scattered minds right there. Those who dwell on the earth shall enter the chasm of the earth, eighty-four thousand <s>yojanas</s> (leagues) below—right there their lifespan shall be exhausted. Those hostile beings who dwell in water, who are not devoted to the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching, who would harm the kings, <s>kṣatriyas</s> devoted to the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching, up to the <s>bhikṣus</s> devoted to service—for them too, likewise, their heads shall split into seven pieces, and right there their lifespan shall be exhausted if they transgress these <s>mantras</s>. Moreover, in whatever realm

body.text: viṣaye iyaṃ māramaṇḍalāparājitadhāraṇīdharmaparyāyaḥ pracariṣyati tatra vayaṃ rakṣāvaraṇaguptaye autsukyamāpatsyāmahe savāṃśca tatra dharmakāmān sattvān paripālayiṣyāmaḥ / mahāsannipātaratnaketusūtre ṣaṣṭhaḥ dhāraṇīparivartaḥ // 6 //
body.translated_text: this <s>Māramaṇḍalāparājita</s> (Invincible against <s>Māra</s>'s Circle) <s>dhāraṇī</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse shall circulate, there we shall undertake earnest effort for protection, guarding, and defense, and we shall safeguard all beings there who desire the <s>Dharma</s>. Sixth chapter, the <s>Dhāraṇī</s> Chapter, in the <s>Mahāsannipātaratnaketusūtra</s>. //6//
