body.text: daśamaḥ parivartaḥ
body.translated_text: Tenth Chapter

body.text: sarvo 'bghātuḥ sarvastejodhātuḥ sarvo vāyudhātuḥ sarva ākāśadhāturadhiṣṭhitaḥ saddharmanetrīcirasthityarthaṃ triratnavaṃśānupacchedārthaṃ sarvasattvaparipākārthaṃ yāvat saṃsārapāraṅgamanārtham /
body.translated_text: All the water element, all the fire element, all the wind element, and all the space element are empowered for the purpose of the long endurance of the guiding eye of the true <s>Dharma</s>, for the purpose of the unbroken continuity of the lineage of the Three Jewels, for the purpose of the ripening of all beings, and for the purpose of crossing beyond <s>saṃsāra</s>.

body.text: atha khalu sarve te buddhā bhagavanto ye tadbuddhakṣetranivāsino bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ śakrabrahmalokapālā devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragendrā ye ca mahaujaskamahaujaskāḥ sattvā ye ca cāturdvīpikāyāṃ lokadhātau naivāsikāstān sarvānāmaṃtryaivamāhuḥ / yuṣmākaṃ mārṣā haste bhūyiṣṭhatarāmimāṃ saddharmanetrīmadhiṣṭhāya parindāmi sarvasattvaparipākārtham / tathā yuṣmābhiriyaṃ saddharmanetrī manasi kartavyā ujjvālayitavyā rakṣitavyā / yathā na kṣipramihāyaṃ saddharmaḥ pralujyeta nāntardhīyeta / ye ca śrāddhāḥ kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaraścemaṃ mahāsannipātadharmaparyāyaṃ dhārayiṣyanti yāvallikhitvā bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikāḥ saddharmadhārakāḥ pudgalāstān sarvān [paripālanārthaṃ] yuṣmākaṃ haste nyāsataḥ parindāmaḥ ārakṣa-paripālanatāyai / dharmabhāṇakāḥ
body.translated_text: Then all those <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavāns</s>, those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> dwelling in that <s>Buddha</s>-field, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, the world-protectors, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, lords of <s>mahoragas</s>, and those exceedingly powerful beings, and those dwelling in the four-continent world-system—addressing all of them, they said: Into your hands, O venerable ones, we most emphatically entrust this guiding eye of the true <s>Dharma</s> for the purpose of ripening all beings. Thus should you bear this guiding eye of the true <s>Dharma</s> in mind, illuminate it, and protect it, so that this true <s>Dharma</s> may not quickly be destroyed or disappear. And those faithful sons and daughters of good family, and those individuals who uphold the true <s>Dharma</s>—<s>bhikṣus</s>, <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, <s>upāsakas</s>, <s>upāsikās</s>—who shall preserve this <s>Mahāsannipāta</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, even to the extent of writing it in a book and preserving it, and <s>Dharma</s>-preachers, <s>Dharma</s>-listeners, those devoted to meditation, and those who uphold the true <s>Dharma</s>—into your hands we entrust all of them as a deposit, for the sake of protection and safeguarding. <s>Dharma</s>-preachers,

body.text: pudgalā dharmakāmā dhyānābhiratā dharmaśrāvaṇikāḥ saddharmadhārakāḥ yuṣmābhiḥ rakṣitavyāḥ / tat kasya hetoḥ / ye iha bhūtāstathāgatā arhantaḥ samyak saṃbuddhāḥ sarvaistaistathāgataiḥ kliṣṭe pañcakaṣāye buddhakṣetre sanipatya sarveṣāṃ śakrabrahmalokapālānāṃ haste iyaṃ dharmanetrī pari[da]ttā rakṣāyai yāvat sarvasattvaparipākāya / evameva ye bhaviṣyanti anāgate 'dhvani daśasu dikṣu buddhā bhagavantaḥ te 'pi sarve kliṣṭeṣu pañcakaṣāyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu kṣaṇāt sannipatya sattvahitārtham etāhi dhāraṇīmantrapadāni bhāṣiṣyante / imāṃ ca dharmanetrīmadhiṣṭhāsyanti / sarveṣāṃ śaktrabrahmalokapālānāṃ haste imāṃ dharmanetrīmanuparindāsyanti rakṣāparipālanārtham / vayamapyetarhi yuṣmākamiha buddhakṣetranivāsināṃ cāturdvīpikanivāsināṃ ca śakrabrahmālokapāladeva-nāgayakṣa-gandharvāsuragaruḍakinnara-mahoragendrāṇāṃ haste bhūyiṣṭhataram anuparindāmaḥ ārakṣāyai sattvaparipākārtham / tathā yuṣmābhiriyaṃ saddharmanetrī manasi kartavyā projjvālayitavyā yathā na kṣiprameva pralujyeta nāntardhīyeta / ye ca śrāddhāḥ kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaraśca saddharmadhārakāśca pudgalā bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikā ye imaṃ mahāsannipātaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ dhārayanti yāvat pustakalikhitamapi kṛtvā dhārayanti dharmabhāṇakā dharmaśrāvaṇikā dhyānayuktāḥ saddharmadhārakā yuṣmābhiste rakṣitavyāḥ pūjayitavyāḥ / tat kasya hetoḥ / sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhito 'yaṃ dharmaparyāyo
body.translated_text: individuals who desire the <s>Dharma</s>, who delight in meditation, who listen to the <s>Dharma</s>, who uphold the true <s>Dharma</s>—they should be protected by you. For what reason? Those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones who have been here in the past—all those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, having assembled in this defiled <s>Buddha</s>-field of the five corruptions, entrusted this guiding eye of the <s>Dharma</s> into the hands of all the <s>Śakras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, and world-protectors for its protection, up to the ripening of all beings. Just so, those who in the future shall be <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> in the ten directions—they too, having assembled in an instant in the defiled <s>Buddha</s>-fields of the five corruptions, for the welfare of beings, shall speak these <s>dhāraṇī</s> <s>mantra</s>-words. And they shall empower this guiding eye of the <s>Dharma</s>. They shall entrust this guiding eye of the <s>Dharma</s> into the hands of all the <s>Śakras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, and world-protectors for the purpose of protection and safeguarding. We too now entrust it most emphatically into the hands of you who dwell in this <s>Buddha</s>-field and in this four-continent [world-system]—<s>Śakra</s>-lords, <s>Brahmā</s>-lords, world-protector <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, lords of <s>mahoragas</s>—for their protection and for the ripening of beings. Thus should you bear this guiding eye of the true <s>Dharma</s> in mind and illuminate it, so that this true <s>Dharma</s> may not quickly be destroyed or disappear. And those faithful sons and daughters of good family, and individuals who uphold the true <s>Dharma</s>—<s>bhikṣus</s>, <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, <s>upāsakas</s>, <s>upāsikās</s>—who preserve this <s>Mahāsannipāta</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, even to the extent of writing it in a book and preserving it, <s>Dharma</s>-preachers, <s>Dharma</s>-listeners, those devoted to meditation, those who uphold the true <s>Dharma</s>—they should be protected and honored by you. For what reason? This <s>Dharma</s>-discourse is empowered by all <s>Buddhas</s>.

body.text: yatra kvacid grāme vā nagare vā nigame vā janapade vā karvaṭe vā rājakule vāraṇyāyatane vā yāvat kuṭumbikagṛhe vāyaṃ dharmaparyāyaḥ pracaret prakāśyeta uddiśyeta paryavāpyeta vā antaśaḥ pustakalikhitamapi kṛtvā bhāṣyeta tena dharmarasena pṛthivīrasasattvaujāṃsi vivardhiṣyante / tena yūyamojovantastejobalavīryaparākramavanto bhaviṣyatha / parivāra-vimāna-vṛddhiśca yuṣmākaṃ bhaviṣyati / manuṣyarājā apyārakṣitā bhaviṣyanti / rājaiśvaryeṇa te vivardhiṣyante sarvarāṣṭraṃ ca teṣāṃ surakṣitaṃ bhaviṣyati / tena ca dharmarasena santarpitā jambudvīpe rājānaḥ parasparahitacittā bhaviṣyanti / karmavipākaṃ śraddhāsyanti / kuśalacittā bhaviṣyanti / amatsaracittā hitavastucittāḥ sarvasattvadayācittā yāvat samyagdṛṣṭikā rājāno bhaviṣyanti / prati prati svaviṣaye 'bhiraṃsyante / ayaṃ ca jambudvīpaḥ sphīta udāro janākīrṇo bhaviṣyati / subhīkṣataro ramaṇī[ya]taraśca bhaviṣyati / bahujanamanuṣyākīrṇā ojovatī ca pṛthivī bhaviṣyati snigdhatarā ca / mṛdutaraphalāni ca / yatrauṣadhi-dhana-dhānya-samṛddhatarā ca ārogya-sukhasparśavihāra-saṃjananī ca bhaviṣyati / sarvakali-kalaha-durbhikṣa-roga-paracakra-daṃśa-maśaka-śalabhāśiviṣa-duṣṭayakṣa-rākṣasa-mṛga-pakṣi-vṛkā akālavātavṛṣṭayaḥ praśamiṣyanti / samyag nakṣatra-rātri-divasārdhamāsa-ṛtu-saṃvatsarāṇi
body.translated_text: Wherever—in a village, city, market town, province, small town, royal household, forest hermitage, or even a householder's dwelling—this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse shall circulate, be illuminated, be expounded, or be studied, even if merely written in a book and recited—by that essence of <s>Dharma</s>, the essence of the earth and the vitality of beings shall increase. Thereby you shall become endowed with vitality, radiance, strength, vigor, and valor. And your retinue, mansions, and prosperity shall increase. Even human kings shall be protected. They shall increase in royal sovereignty, and their entire realm shall be well-protected. And the kings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, nourished by that essence of <s>Dharma</s>, shall have minds of mutual welfare. They shall have faith in the ripening of <s>karma</s>. They shall have wholesome minds, free from jealousy, with minds devoted to beneficial things, with minds of compassion for all beings—the kings shall have right views. Each shall delight in their own domain. And this <s>Jambudvīpa</s> shall be prosperous, exalted, and teeming with people. It shall become more abundant and more delightful. The earth shall be teeming with many people and humans, rich in vitality, more fertile, with softer fruits, enriched with medicinal herbs, wealth, and grain, and shall generate health, happiness, pleasant contact, and comfortable dwelling. All strife, conflict, famine, disease, foreign invasion, gadflies, mosquitoes, locusts, venomous serpents, hostile <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, wild animals, birds, wolves, and untimely storms shall be pacified. The constellations, nights, days, half-months, seasons, and years shall proceed properly.

body.text: pravahiṣyanti / sattvāśca prāyo daśakuśalakarmapathacāriṇo bhaviṣyanti / itaścyutāḥ sugatisvargagāmino bhaviṣyanti / te 'pi yuṣmatparivārā bhaviṣyanti / evaṃ bahuguṇamahānuśaṃso 'yaṃ dhāraṇīdharmaparyāyaḥ sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhito mahāsaṃnipātaḥ sattvānāṃ saṃskārapāraṅgamāya yaśovivṛddhipāripūryai bhaviṣyati / niravaśeṣaṃ mātṛgrāmabhāvaparikṣayāya upapattivedanīyo 'paraparyāyavedanīyaḥ saṃkṣepād dṛṣṭadharmavedanīyo 'pi sa mātṛgrāmātmabhāvaḥ ākṣiptaḥ sa sarvaḥ parikṣayaṃ yāsyati sthāpyanantaryakāriṇaṃ saddharmapratikṣepakaṃ vā āryāpavādakaṃ vā / yadanyat kāyavāṅmanaḥphalavipākadauṣṭhulyaṃ tat sarvaṃ parikṣayaṃ yāsyati /
body.translated_text: Beings shall mostly follow the path of the ten wholesome courses of action. Having died from here, they shall go to good destinies and heavens. They too shall become your retinue. Thus this <s>dhāraṇī</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, the <s>Mahāsaṃnipāta</s>, empowered by all <s>Buddhas</s>, of many virtues and great benefits, shall serve for beings' crossing beyond conditioned formations and for the full completion of the increase of fame. For the complete exhaustion of female nature without remainder—whether to be experienced at rebirth, in subsequent lives, or briefly even in this very life—all that female nature which has been projected shall go to complete exhaustion, excepting those who have committed the acts of immediate retribution, or those who reject the true <s>Dharma</s>, or those who slander the noble ones. Whatever afflictive results of deeds of body, speech, and mind there may be—all that shall go to complete exhaustion.

body.text: ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyam antaśaḥ pustakalikhitamapi kṛtvā dhārayiṣyati tasya sumerumātrāṇi karmakleśavaraṇāni parikṣayaṃ yāsyanti / sarvakuśalamūlālambanāni ca vivṛddhiṃ pāripūriṃ yāsyanti / sarvāṅgapāripūriḥ sarvābhiprāyasaṃpattiḥ sarvāṇi kāyavāṅmanaḥsucaritāni ca vivardhiṣyante / sarvakudṛṣṭiprahāṇaṃ sarvaśatruḥ sahadharmanigrahaḥ sarvasūkṣmaśāntamārgāvatāro bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: Whoever shall preserve this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, even merely by writing it in a book, their karmic and afflictive obstructions, even if as vast as Mount <s>Sumeru</s>, shall go to complete exhaustion. And all bases of roots of merit shall increase and be fulfilled. Completeness of all limbs, fulfillment of all aspirations, and all good conduct of body, speech, and mind shall increase. There shall be the abandonment of all wrong views, the subduing of all enemies together with the <s>Dharma</s>, and the entry into the entire subtle, peaceful path.

body.text: asya sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhitasya mahāsaṃnipātadhāraṇīdharmaparyāyasya prabhāveṇa yatra ca viṣaye punarayaṃ dharmaparyāyaḥ pracariṣyati tatra sā pṛthivī snigdhatarā bhaviṣyati / ojovatī mṛduphalarasā bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: By the power of this <s>Mahāsaṃnipāta</s> <s>dhāraṇī</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, empowered by all <s>Buddhas</s>, in whatever realm this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse shall circulate, there the earth shall become more fertile, rich in vitality, with soft and flavorful fruits,

body.text: tiktakaṭukaparuṣavirasaparivarjitā bhaviṣyati / puṣpaphalasamṛddhatarā dhanadhānyakoṣakoṣṭhāgārakumbhakalaśavṛddhirbhaviṣyati vastrānnapānauṣadhopakaraṇā bhūyiṣṭhatarā / ye ca tatra annapānopajīvitasattvāste nīrogatarā bhaviṣyanti varṇavanto balavantaḥ smṛtimantaḥ prajñāvanto dharmakāmāḥ kuśalaparyeṣṭyabhiratāḥ pāpaparivarjitāḥ / te tataścyavitvā yuṣmākaṃ sahabhāvyatāyopapatsyante / tathā yūyaṃ parivāravṛddhā balavanto 'pratihatacakrā dharmabalena cāturvarṇyaṃ janakāyaṃ paripālayiṣyatha / sattvān dharmārtheṣu niyokṣyatha / evaṃ yuṣmābhiḥ sarvatryadhvānugatānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ pūjā kṛtā bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: free from bitter, pungent, rough, and tasteless [qualities]. It shall be more abundant in flowers and fruits; there shall be increase of wealth, grain, treasuries, granaries, pots, and vessels; and clothing, food, drink, medicines, and implements shall become more plentiful. And those beings who subsist on food and drink there shall become more free from disease, endowed with good complexion, strong, mindful, wise, desiring the <s>Dharma</s>, delighting in the pursuit of virtue, and avoiding evil. Having passed away from there, they shall be reborn as your companions. Thus you, with increased retinue, powerful, with unobstructed authority, shall protect the people of the four classes by the power of <s>Dharma</s>. You shall employ beings in the purposes of <s>Dharma</s>. Thus by you, worship of the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> of all three times shall have been accomplished.

body.text: atha khalu māndāravagandharocastathāgato viśuddhena buddhaviṣayajñānasvaraghoṣeṇārthapadavyāhārānurūpeṇa kṛtsnamidaṃ buddhakṣetramāpūrya sarve ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ śakrendrā yāvad brahmendrā mahoragendrā ye ceha buddhakṣetre nivāsino bhūyiṣṭhataram asyāṃ cāturdvīpikāyāṃ nivāsinaḥ sarvabuddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ ca vacanena cāsya saṃnipātasūtrasya dharmanetrayā dhāraṇāya prakāśanā[ya] rakṣaṇāyotsāhayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Māndāravagandhāroca</s>, with the pure sound of <s>Buddha</s>-domain knowledge, in a manner conforming to the articulation of meaning and words, filling this entire <s>Buddha</s>-field, encouraged all the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, <s>Śakra</s>-lords, up to <s>Brahmā</s>-lords, lords of <s>mahoragas</s>, and those dwelling in this <s>Buddha</s>-field and especially those dwelling in this four-continent [world-system], by the word of all the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>, to preserve, illuminate, and protect the guiding eye of this <s>Dharma</s> of this <s>Saṃnipāta Sūtra</s>.

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena maitreyapūrvaṅgamāṇāṃ saptanavatikoṭīsahasrāṇi kṣāntipratilabdhānāṃ mahāsattvānāmiha buddhakṣetre nivāsīni tāni sarvāṇi ekakaṇṭhenaivamāhuḥ / vayamapi sarvabuddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ vacanena sarvatryadhvānugatānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ
body.translated_text: At that time, led by <s>Maitreya</s>, ninety-seven thousand <s>koṭis</s> (billions) of <s>mahāsattvas</s> who had attained <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), dwelling in this <s>Buddha</s>-field, all with one voice spoke thus: We too, by the word of all the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>, for the worship of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> of all three times,

body.text: pūjārthamimaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ nyāyataḥ śāstrasaṃma[ta]to gurugauraveṇa pratigṛṇhīmaḥ / kāruṇyena sattvaparipākārthaṃ yāvadanuttare mārge pratiṣṭhāpanārthaṃ vayamimaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ grāmanagaranigamajanapadarājadhānyaraṇyāyataneṣu vistareṇa uddayotayiṣyāmaḥ / sattvāṃśca paripācayiṣyāmaḥ saddharmacirasthityartham / tena khalu punaḥ samayena sarve buddhā bhagavantastabduddhakṣetrāntargatāḥ sādhukāraṃ pradaduḥ / sādhu sādhu satpuruṣā evaṃ yuṣmābhiḥ karaṇīyam /
body.translated_text: accept this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse properly, in accordance with the teachings, with reverence for our teachers. Out of compassion, for the purpose of ripening beings, up to establishing them on the unsurpassed path, we shall illuminate this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse extensively in villages, cities, market towns, provinces, royal capitals, and forest hermitages. And we shall ripen beings for the long endurance of the true <s>Dharma</s>. At that time, all the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> within that <s>Buddha</s>-field gave their approval: Well done, well done, O good persons! Thus should it be done by you.

body.text: atha khalu sarve śakrabrahmamahoragendrā ye ceha buddhakṣetre [a]parāṇī catuḥṣaṣṭikoṭīnayutāni mahaujaskamahaujaskānāṃ sattvānāṃ te sarve ekakaṇṭhenaivamāhuḥ / vayamapyetaṃ mahāsannipātaṃ dharmaparyāyam udgrahīṣyāmaḥ / yāvad vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyāmaḥ samuddayotayiṣyāmaḥ sattvāṃśca paripācayiṣyāmaḥ saddharmacirasthityartham / saddharmadhārakān dharmaśrāvaṇikāṃśca rakṣiṣyāmaḥ paripālayiṣyāmaḥ / yatra cāyaṃ dharmaparyāyaḥ pracariṣyāti tatra vayaṃ sarvabuddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ vacanena sarvakalikalahavigrahavivādadurbhikṣa-rogaparacakrākālavātavṛṣṭiśītoṣṇāni ca duṣṭarūkṣaparuṣavirasatiktakaṭukabhāvān praśamayiṣyāmaḥ / kṣemaramaṇīyatāṃ subhikṣasāmagrīṃ saṃpādayiṣyāmaḥ / saddharmanetrī-cira-sthityarthamudyogamāpatsyāmaḥ / bhūyasyā mātrayā dhārmikān rājñaḥ paripālayiṣyāmaḥ / dhyānābhiratāṃśca sattvān rakṣiṣyāmaḥ / atha sarve te buddhā bhagavantaḥ sādhukāraṃ pradaduḥ / sādhu sādhu bhadramukhāḥ / evaṃ yuṣmābhiḥ karaṇīyam / ātmobhayaparārthamudyogamāpattavyam /
body.translated_text: Then all the <s>Śakras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, lords of <s>Mahoragas</s>, and sixty-four <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of other beings of great splendor in this buddha-field, all spoke with one voice: "We too shall take up this great assembly <s>Dharma</s>-discourse. We shall extensively illuminate and elucidate it, and we shall ripen beings—"

body.text: evaṃ ca yuṣmābhiḥ trayadhvānugatānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ pūjā kṛtā bhaviṣyati / yatra hi nāma yūyaṃ sattvaparipākārthaṃ saddharmanetrayā ujjvālanārthaṃ saddharmacirasthityartham udyuktā na cireṇa yūyaṃ kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyak saṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyatha /
body.translated_text: "In this way, worship of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, of the three times will have been performed by you. Indeed, since you are diligently engaged for the purpose of ripening beings, for illuminating the lamp of the True <s>Dharma</s>, and for the long endurance of the True <s>Dharma</s>—before long, you shall swiftly attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening)."

body.text: atha khalu ye asyāṃ madhyamāyāṃ cārtudvīpikāyāṃ nivāsinaḥ śakrabrahmadevendrā mahoragendrā ye ca mahojaskamahaujaskāḥ sattvāste sarve utthāyāsanāt prāñjalayaḥ sthitvaivamāhuḥ / vayamapi sarvabuddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ vacanenemāṃ saddharmanetrīmuddyotayiṣyāmo rakṣiṣyāmaḥ / imaṃ ca mahāsannipātaṃ sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhitaṃ dhāraṇīmudrādharmaparyāyaṃ nyāyataḥ pratigrahīṣyāmaḥ / yāvad grāmanagaranigamajanapadarājadhānyaraṇyāyataneṣu vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyāmaḥ / saddharmadhārakāṃśca pudgalān rakṣiṣyāmaḥ paripālayiṣyāmaḥ / ye ca dharmapratipattisthitā dharmabhāṇakā dharmaśrāvaṇikā bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikāḥ śrāddhāḥ kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaraścemaṃ dharmaparyāyamudgrahīṣyanti yāvat pustakalikhitamapi kṛtvā dhārayiṣyanti dhyānābhiyuktāstān vayaṃ sarvān rakṣiṣyāmaḥ paripālayiṣyāmaḥ satkariṣyāmaḥ mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ cīvaracchatradhvajapatākāvilepanairyāvat sarvabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ satkariṣyāmaḥ / asya ca dharmaparyāyasya bhāṣyamāṇasya prakāśyamānasya vayaṃ svayamupasaṃkramiṣyāmaḥ śravaṇāya śāstṛsaṃjñayā
body.translated_text: Then all the <s>Śakras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, <s>Devendras</s>, lords of <s>Mahoragas</s>, and beings of great splendor dwelling in this middle four-continent [world], all rising from their seats and standing with palms joined, spoke thus: "We too, in accordance with the words of all the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, shall illuminate and protect this lamp of the True <s>Dharma</s>. And this Great Assembly, all the <s>Buddhas</s>—"

body.text: vayamimaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaśchatradhvajapatākābhiḥ / tat kasya hetoḥ / asmin vayaṃ sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhite dhāraṇīmudrādharmaparyāye prakāśyamāne dharmarasena ojovanto bhaviṣyāmaḥ / balavanto vīryavantaḥ smṛtimanto jñānavantaḥ pakṣaparivāravantaḥ apratihatacakraparākramā bhaviṣyāmaḥ / evaṃ vayaṃ sarvaviṣaye sarvān kalikalahavivādadurbhikṣa-rogaparacakrā-kālavātavṛṣṭyati-śītoṣṇānāvṛṣṭi-duḥsvapnadurnimitta-duṣṭarūkṣaparuṣatikta-kaṭukavirasākuśalapakṣāntakarāna bhāvān praśamayiṣyāmaḥ / bhūyasyā mātrayā kṣemasubhikṣānta-ramaṇīyā-rogyasāmagrīṃ sampādayiṣyāmaḥ / kālena vātavṛṣṭiśītoṣṇaughān āvāhayiṣyāmaḥ / samyaggraharātridivasa-māsārdhamāsartu-saṃvatsarānāvāhayiṣyāmaḥ / samyag grahanakṣatrasūryācandramasau vāhayiṣyāmaḥ / nadyutas-sarastaḍāgapuṣkariṇīḥ prapūrayiṣyāmaḥ / yatra sattvānāmudakaughena pīḍā bhaviṣyati tadvayaṃ pratinivārayiṣyāmaḥ / bhūyasyā mātrayā vayaṃ teṣu grāmanagaranigamajanapadeṣu sattvahitārthaṃ patraśākhāpuṣpaphalagandhadhānyauṣadhaśasyāni snigdhamṛṣṭavarṇarasamahatprabhūtatarāṇi niṣpādayiṣyāmaḥ / dhanadhānyauṣadhavastrābharaṇaiḥ sattvānāmavaikalyaṃ saṃpādayiṣyāmaḥ / teṣāṃ ca sattvānāṃ kuśalaparyeṣṭito dharāṇīmudrādharmaparyāyaḥ prakāśyeta / antaśaḥ pustakalikhitamapi kṛtvā dhāryeta vā vācyeta vā pūjāsatkāreṇa vā dhāryeta / teṣu ye rājāno bhaviṣyanti tān vayaṃ kṣatriyān mūrdhābhiṣiktān rakṣiṣyāmaḥ
body.translated_text: "We shall honor, revere, respect, and worship this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse with canopies, banners, and flags. For what reason? Because when this <s>dhāraṇī</s>-seal <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, empowered by all the <s>Buddhas</s>, is being proclaimed, we shall become nourished by the flavor of <s>Dharma</s>—powerful, vigorous, mindful, wise, endowed with followers and retinue, irresistible—"

body.text: paripālayiṣyāmaḥ / ahitaṃ caiṣāmapaneṣyāmaḥ / ahita caiṣāmupasaṃhariṣyāmaḥ / sarvakautukamaṅgalakudṛṣṭikukārya-kvadhiṣṭhāna-kupraṇidhi-kuśaraṇa-kuhanalapanamāyāṣaṭhyamṛṣāvāderyāroṣamātsa]ryāṇi praśamayiṣyāmaḥ / samyagdṛṣṭimārge ṛjuke śraddhā-dama-saṃyama hryapatrāpyeṣu saṃniyokṣyāmaḥ / evamagramahiṣīnāmantaḥpurakāṇā[ma]mātyagaṇamahāmātra-naigamapauruṣajānapadānāṃ caturṇāṃ varṇānāṃ strīpuruṣadārakadārikāṇāmapi rakṣāṃ kariṣyāmaḥ paripālanaṃ yāvat hyapatrāpye sanniyokṣyāmaḥ / antaśaścatuṣpadānapi teṣu viṣayeṣu rakṣiṣyāmaḥ / eṣu asya dharmaparyāyasya prakāśanaṃ bhaviṣyati yāvallikhitamapi pustake sthāsyati / evaṃrūpairvayaṃ mahadbhirudyogaparākramaistān sattvān paripālayiṣyāmo dharmanetrīsamud dyotanārtham anantardhānāya udyogamāpatsyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: "We shall protect [them]. We shall remove what is harmful to them. We shall ward off what is harmful to them. We shall pacify all [forms of] superstitious omens, evil views, evil deeds, evil empowerments, evil vows, evil refuges, deception, flattery, illusion, dishonesty, false speech, envy, anger, and jealousy. We shall establish [beings] on the straight path of right view, in faith, self-control, restraint, conscience, and moral shame. Thus the foremost great—"

body.text: atha te sarve buddhā bhagavantastebhyaḥ satpuruṣebhyaḥ sādhukāraṃ pradaduḥ / sādhu sādhu bhadramukhāḥ / evaṃ yuṣmābhiḥ karaṇīyaṃ yad yūyaṃ dharmanetryāstriratnavaṃśasya ca anantardhānāya udyuktāḥ evaṃ yuṣmābhiḥ sarvatryadhvānugatānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ pūjā kṛtā bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: Then all those <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, gave their approval to those good beings: "Excellent! Excellent, O fair-faced ones! Thus it should be done by you, who are diligently engaged for the non-disappearance of the lamp of <s>Dharma</s> and the lineage of the Three Jewels. In this way, worship of all the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, of the three times will have been performed by you."

body.text: iti ratnaketusūtre daśamaḥ ārakṣaparivartaḥ samāptaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the Tenth Chapter, the Chapter on Protection, in the <s>Ratnaketu</s> Sūtra. //

body.translated_text: Beginning of <s>Ratnaketudhāraṇī</s> Chapter 11

body.text: ekādaśaḥ parivartaḥ
body.translated_text: Eleventh Chapter

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān śākyamunistathāgataḥ śakrabrahmavirūḍhaka-virupākṣa-dhṛtarāṣṭra-kuverānāmantrayati sma / ahaṃ bhadramukhāḥ iha kliṣṭe pañcakaṣāye buddhakṣetre sattvānāṃ kāruṇya-praṇidhānena anuttarāṃ samyak saṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ [sattvānāma] vidyāndhakāraprakṣiptānāṃ kleśataskaradhūrtopadrutānāṃ [kleśānāṃ praśamanāya] mārapakṣo me parājitaḥ saddharmadhvaja ucchrepito 'pramāṇāḥ sattvā [duḥkhāt] parimokṣitāḥ / saddharmavṛṣṭirutsṛṣṭā mārakoṭyo me parājitāḥ / yadetarhi bhadra]mukhā yuṣmākaṃ haste 'nuparindāmi tadebhirapramāṇairgaṇanāsamatikrāntaiḥ buddhairbhagavadbhirbodhisattvairmahāsattvaiśca daśa[diśi lokadhātau sannipatitairadhiṣṭhāya rakṣito]vajradharmasamatā-pratītyadharmahṛdaya-sarvasamucchraya-vidhvaṃsano dhāraṇīmudrāpadaprabhedapraveśavyākaraṇo dharmaparyāyaḥ / [iha buddhakṣetre] pṛthivīrasa-sattvāvāsadoṣāṇāṃ praśamāya sattvaparipākāya sarvāśubhakarmaniravaśeṣaparikṣayārthaṃ triratna[vaṃśacirasthityarthaṃ buddhābhiprāya]pariniṣpattyarthameṣa yuṣmābhirapyadhi]ṣṭhāya rakṣitavya iti / yacca me [sad-]dharmanetrīsaṃrakṣaṇa kuśalamūlapuṇyābhisaṃskārāṇi uccāraṇadeśana[smaraṇavācana]triśaraṇagamanopāsakasaṃvara-brahmacaryāvāsa-kuśamūlapuṇyābhisaṃ[skārāṇi
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, addressed <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, and <s>Kuvera</s>: "O fair-faced ones, I, in this afflicted buddha-field of the five defilements, out of compassion and [former] vows for beings, have attained <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening). [These] beings, cast into the darkness of ignorance, harassed by the thieves and rogues of the <s>kleśas</s>—"

body.text: yāvat prathamadhyānabhāvanā] yāvat saṃjñāvedayitanirodhabhāvanā yāvat srota-āpattiphala-sākṣātkṛ[tiryāvadaparāṇi kuśalamūlapuṇyābhisaṃskārāṇi etarhi kṛtāni anāgate karaṇīyāni vā mama saddharmapradīpaprajvālana-puṇyābhisaṃskārāṇi sarvametad yuṣmākaṃ haste parindāmi /]
body.translated_text: "...up to the cultivation of the first <s>dhyāna</s>...up to the cultivation of the cessation of perception and feeling...up to the direct realization of the fruit of stream-entry...up to all other wholesome roots and meritorious formations, whether made now or to be made in the future—all this merit of kindling the lamp of my True <s>Dharma</s>, I entrust into your hands."

body.text: asya dharmaparyāyasya prakāśanārthaṃ [dharmabhāṇakaṃ pudgalaṃ saṃco]dayiṣyāmaḥ / dharmabhāṇaka-dharmaśrāvaṇikānāṃ dhanadhānyasarvabhogasampad vivṛddhiṃ sādhayiṣyāmaḥ / avipralopadharmaṃ jinaśāsanaṃ saṃdhārayiṣyāmaḥ / atha khalu[sarve buddhā bhagavantaḥ sarveṣāṃ manuṣyāmanuṣyāṇāṃ sādhukāraṃ pradaduḥ /]
body.translated_text: "We shall inspire individuals who are <s>Dharma</s>-preachers for the purpose of proclaiming this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse. We shall bring about the increase of wealth, grain, and all enjoyments and prosperity for those who preach and those who listen to the <s>Dharma</s>. We shall preserve the teaching of the Conqueror as the <s>Dharma</s> of non-deception." Then all the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, gave their approval to all humans and non-humans—

body.text: atha kautūhaliko bodhisattvo mahāsattvastaṃ śākyamuniṃ tathāgataṃ[paryeṣate / kiṃ bhagavan mārakoṭyaḥ saparivārāḥ samāgatāḥ /] bhagavānāha / sarve saparivārāḥ / [atha khalu] kautūhaliko bodhisattvaḥ [āha / kiṃ saparivārā mārā triratne labdhaprasādāḥ] / bhagavānāha / kulaputrāyaṃ khalu māraḥ pāpīmān sahasraparivāro 'labdhaprasādaḥ [kupitaḥ anāttamanā vartamāne anāgatakāle 'pi
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Kautūhalika</s> approached the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> and asked: "O Blessed One, have the <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Māras</s> with their retinues assembled?" The Blessed One replied: "All, with their retinues." Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Kautūhalika</s> asked: "Have the <s>Māras</s> with their retinues gained faith in the Three Jewels?" The Blessed One replied: "O son of good family, this <s>Māra</s> <s>Pāpīmān</s>—"

body.text: yāvadeṣo 'vatāraprekṣī avatāragaveṣī saddharmanetrīvipralopārthaṃ [prayatyate / ..............tathā] ............ekaviṃśatiparivārā ete alabdhaprasādāḥ kupitāḥ anāttamanā [vartamāne anāgatakāle 'pi yāvat saddharma]netrīpravistāraḥ tāvadete mama śāsane avatāraprekṣiṇaḥ avatāragaveṣiṇaḥ [saddharmanetrīvipralopārthaṃ prayatyate / tat kasya hetoḥ / pūrva]vairādhiṣṭhitatvādanavaropitakuśalamūlatvādakalyāṇamitraparigṛhītatvāt...... [nirvāṇasukhe alabdhaprasādatvāt praṇidhānaparigatatvāt] cittena cittaṃ na saṃdadati na prasīdanti na saṃtiṣṭhanti na pramādyanti / [buddhānāṃ mahāsannipātaṃ dṛṣṭvā gambhīrāṃ dhāraṇīṃ śru]tvānenaivaṃ hetunā paścācchraddhāṃ pratilapsyate / anuttarāyāṃ samyak saṃbodhau [prasādaṃ lapsyate /
body.translated_text: "...he is one who watches for an opening, who seeks an opening, who strives for the destruction of the lamp of the True <s>Dharma</s>... ...these twenty-one retinues have not gained faith, are angry and displeased. In the present and future time too, as long as the lamp of the True <s>Dharma</s> is being spread, they will watch for openings in my teaching, seek openings, [and strive] for the destruction of the True <s>Dharma</s>—"

body.text: atha kautūhaliko bodhisattvaḥ āha / bhagavannayaṃ] dharmaparyāyo 'navaruptakuśalamūlānāmapi sattvānāṃ sacet.....śravaṇamārge nadet teṣāṃ .....[anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbo]dhau cittamutpādayet / tena khalu punaḥ samayena nāgadatto nāma māraḥ pūrva........nuttarāyāṃ samyak saṃbodhau / sa maharṣiveṣeṇa śākyamuninā.....
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Kautūhalika</s> asked: "O Blessed One, this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, even for beings in whom wholesome roots have not been planted, if...it resounds on the path of hearing...it would generate in them the aspiration for <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening)." At that time, a <s>Māra</s> named <s>Nāgadatta</s>, formerly...[aspired to] <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. He, in the guise of a great sage, [approached] the <s>Śākya</s>—

body.text: mahāsannipātaratnaketudhāraṇīsūtraṃ samāptam //
body.translated_text: The <s>Mahāsaṃnipāta Ratnaketudhāraṇī Sūtra</s> is complete. //
